### GV-19E — White-Reality-Check, Hansen-SPA, StepM, and Model-Confidence-Set multiple-comparison family
- **Domain:** governance, validation, research selection control, benchmark-relative model comparison, and data-snooping control
- **Purpose:** Preserve one canonical home for benchmark-relative multiple-comparison procedures so Codex does not stop at PSR/DSR/PBO when a candidate family has been selected from many materially related forecasting, alpha, execution, or parameter-search variants against one declared benchmark.
- **Families included once here:** `WHITE_REALITY_CHECK`, `HANSEN_SUPERIOR_PREDICTIVE_ABILITY`, `STEPWISE_MULTIPLE_TESTING`, `MODEL_CONFIDENCE_SET`
- **Formula / operating law:**
  - for benchmark loss stream `L_{0,t}` and candidate-model loss streams `L_{k,t}` on one declared loss basis where lower is better, define loss differentials `d_{k,t} = L_{0,t} - L_{k,t}` so positive values favor model `k` over the benchmark;
  - the White Reality Check benchmark statistic admitted here is `T_RC = max_k sqrt(T) * mean(d_k)` on the declared bootstrap basis, with the bootstrap null constructed from the full materially related candidate set so the benchmark is not silently compared only to the single ex post winner;
  - the Hansen SPA benchmark statistic admitted here is `T_SPA = max(0, max_k (sqrt(T) * mean(d_k) / omega_hat_k))`, where `omega_hat_k` is the declared studentizing scale estimate for candidate `k`; SPA must preserve the re-centering policy and studentization policy explicitly rather than leaving them implicit;
  - the StepM family admitted here is the stepwise multiple-testing extension that applies repeated benchmark-relative superior-predictive-ability testing to determine which candidates are superior to the benchmark while controlling familywise error on the declared comparison basis;
  - the MCS family admitted here is the iterative model-confidence-set procedure on a declared loss matrix `ell_{i,t}` that tests equal predictive ability inside the current candidate set, removes one inferior member under the declared elimination rule when equal predictive ability is rejected, and stops only when the surviving set is a model-confidence set at the declared confidence level `1 - alpha`;
  - all four procedures are admissible only on one declared loss basis, one declared trial inventory, one declared bootstrap dependence policy, and one declared benchmark identity; they may not silently infer hidden benchmark changes, hidden discarded candidates, or IID resampling assumptions when serial dependence is present.
- **Inputs:** benchmark loss series when applicable, candidate-loss matrix, complete materially related candidate inventory, declared loss basis, sample size `T`, bootstrap replications, bootstrap family, block-size policy, studentization policy, re-centering policy when applicable, familywise error size `alpha`, MCS elimination method when applicable, and comparator receipts linking the surviving set back to economic-delta evidence
- **Outputs / basis:** Reality-Check p-value packet, SPA p-value packet, StepM superior-model packet, MCS included/excluded-model packet, bootstrap dependence-policy receipt, benchmark-relative rejection/acceptance receipt, and promotion-admissibility advisory state
- **Public default:** advisory and research/shadow governance only; no strategy family, parameter family, or optimizer search may claim benchmark-relative superiority from a materially searched candidate set without a declared RC/SPA-or-stronger multiple-comparison control path when the search inventory is large enough to make data snooping material
- **Seed authority route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed):** preserve one declared benchmark loss stream and a materially complete candidate-loss matrix; preserve White RC as the conservative data-snooping baseline, Hansen SPA as the stronger benchmark-relative default due to studentization and re-centering, StepM as the optional surviving-superior-candidate extractor when benchmark-relative winner identification matters, and MCS as the surviving-indistinguishable-model set when several candidates remain statistically competitive; preserve stationary-block bootstrap as the Day-1 dependence-aware default; preserve `reps = 1000`; preserve explicit familywise error size `alpha = 0.05`; preserve `studentize = True` and `nested = False` for SPA-style Day-1 implementation surfaces; preserve MCS elimination method `'R'` as the Day-1 seed with `'max'` retained as the bounded challenger
- **Bounded search range:** loss basis `{NEG_LOG_LOSS, BRIER_LOSS, MSE_LOSS, MAE_LOSS, NEGATIVE_NET_PNL_PER_RISK_UNIT}` with `NEG_LOG_LOSS` or `BRIER_LOSS` preferred for probability forecasts and `NEGATIVE_NET_PNL_PER_RISK_UNIT` admissible only when the economic basis is declared; bootstrap family `{stationary, circular_block, moving_block}` with `stationary` as Day-1 default; block-size policy `{SQRT_T_DEFAULT, DECLARED_EXPLICIT_BLOCK, DEPENDENCE_FIT_BLOCK}`; replications `{1000,2000,5000}` with Day-1 seed `1000`; familywise error size `alpha in {0.10,0.05,0.01}` with Day-1 seed `0.05`; SPA `studentize in {True,False}` with Day-1 seed `True`; SPA `nested in {False,True}` with Day-1 seed `False`; MCS method `{'R','max'}` with Day-1 seed `'R'`
- **Runtime resolution:** batch_evaluation_only after a completed replay, walk-forward, forecast, or parameter-search campaign; never run-time live-authoritative
- **Fallback behavior:** if benchmark identity is missing, if candidate inventory is incomplete, if the loss basis is ambiguous, if serial dependence is material but the bootstrap dependence policy is missing, or if the candidate count is too small to justify multiple-comparison overhead, quarantine RC/SPA/StepM/MCS as advisory-only diagnostics and fall back to the already-declared PSR/DSR/PBO companion packet plus plain economic-delta comparators with an explicit `MULTIPLE_COMPARISON_DIAGNOSTIC_FALLBACK_RECEIPT`; no promotion-sensitive packet may silently treat a missing multiple-comparison control as green
- **Validation hooks:** `test_reality_check_requires_complete_candidate_inventory.py`, `test_spa_requires_declared_loss_basis_and_benchmark.py`, `test_spa_studentization_and_recentering_declared.py`, `test_stepm_requires_familywise_error_size.py`, `test_mcs_requires_declared_method_and_surviving_set_receipt.py`, `test_multiple_comparison_diagnostic_fallback_receipt.py`
- **Promotion class:** research_to_triggered_live_concurrent_shadow_comparison_to_owner_approved_live

Older packets must resolve here rather than forcing Codex to create a second benchmark-relative multiple-comparison family.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `REALITY_CHECK_DIAGNOSTIC_CARD`
- `SPA_DIAGNOSTIC_CARD`

Hard rules:
- no research packet may present the ex post best candidate from a materially searched benchmark-relative family as statistically superior without either RC/SPA/StepM/MCS control or an explicit declaration that candidate count and snooping risk were immaterial;
- hidden discarded candidates, silent benchmark swaps, and silent loss-basis swaps are forbidden anywhere RC/SPA/StepM/MCS are shown;
- RC/SPA/StepM/MCS are companion diagnostics, not replacements for replay realism, walk-forward evidence, shadow evidence, or economic implementation evidence;
- all multiple-comparison procedures admitted here consume **losses**, not arbitrary score signs; Codex must preserve the loss-sign convention explicitly rather than guessing whether larger or smaller is better;
- if serial dependence is materially present and the bootstrap dependence policy is absent, IID resampling is forbidden by default.

## 19. Formula and basis reference

This section centralizes high-load formulas and basis conventions so downstream cards can refer back to one source instead of re-explaining them repeatedly.

### 19.1 Probability transforms
- **Probability:** `p` in `(0,1)`
- **Odds:** `p / (1-p)`
- **Logit / log-odds:** `L = ln(p/(1-p))`
- **Inverse logit:** `p = 1 / (1 + exp(-L))`

Rule:
probability-model internals may operate in logit space, but any handoff to execution must declare the final execution basis explicitly.

### 19.2 Kelly family
For binary payoffs with net payoff ratio `b`:
- `q = 1 - p`
- `f* = (b p - q) / b`

Operational rule:
raw full Kelly is a mathematical reference, not the default live stake. Live stake must declare:
- base Kelly,
- fractional multiplier,
- time-to-resolution modifier,
- fragility haircut,
- sample-size confidence haircut,
- volatility scaler,
- concentration / inventory caps.

### 19.3 Volatility annualization
Annualization basis must always be declared:
- daily to annual: multiply stdev by `sqrt(252)` unless another basis is explicitly declared,
- intraday series must declare the bar-to-day conversion and session assumptions.

### 19.4 EWMA variance
`σ_t^2 = λ σ_{t-1}^2 + (1-λ) r_t^2`

Rule:
`λ` is not universal. It must be declared by horizon and use case.

### 19.5 GARCH(1,1)
`σ_t^2 = ω + α r_{t-1}^2 + β σ_{t-1}^2`

Rule:
distribution family, parameter constraints, and annualization basis must be declared.

### 19.5A Range-based and realized-volatility estimator convention closure
- Parkinson / Garman-Klass / Rogers-Satchell / Yang-Zhang style estimators must declare intraday-vs-overnight handling explicitly.
- Realized-volatility families must declare return basis (`log_return` vs `simple_return`), bar frequency, annualization factor, and whether microstructure-noise correction is absent or attached.
- Realized-kernel and bipower variation families must declare their jump/noise-handling profile explicitly rather than being treated as interchangeable “realized vol” labels.
- EWMA lambda seeds such as `0.94` and `0.97` are horizon-coupled references, not basis-free universal constants.

Hard rule:
No realized-volatility or jump-aware estimator may silently mix bar frequencies, annualization factors, or overnight conventions.

### 19.6 Avellaneda–Stoikov reference equations
Reservation price:
`r = s - q γ σ^2 (T - t)`

Reference half-spread:
`δ = (1/γ) ln(1 + γ/k) + 0.5 γ σ^2 (T - t)`

Rule:
this family is a reference framework, not a permission slip to hide spread basis, inventory basis, intensity basis, or time horizon assumptions.

### 19.6A Avellaneda–Stoikov intensity and spread parameter card
- **Canonical typed card:** `AS_INTENSITY_PARAMETER_CARD`
- **Purpose:** prevent quote-generation implementations from guessing the arrival-intensity family, spread storage basis, or clipping/rounding policy.
- **Minimum required storage fields:** risk-aversion basis, sigma horizon basis, arrival-intensity intercept `A`, arrival-decay parameter `k` / `kappa`, spread storage basis, tick-rounding policy, fee-aware quote-clipping policy, inventory basis, and horizon basis.
- **Canonical storage law:** `gamma` must declare whether it is stored as a horizon-specific quoting-risk coefficient or another explicit transformed basis; `sigma` must be horizon-matched; arrival intensity must declare both level and decay terms; spread storage must explicitly choose half-spread or full-spread basis and may not mix them in the same packet.
- **Minimum required detailed profile IDs:**
  - `as_gamma_horizon_ref`
  - `as_sigma_horizon_ref`
  - `as_arrival_intensity_A_candidate`
  - `as_arrival_decay_kappa_candidate`
  - `as_reservation_price_candidate`
  - `as_optimal_half_spread_candidate`
  - `as_optimal_full_spread_candidate`
  - `as_half_spread_storage_basis_ref`
  - `as_full_spread_storage_basis_ref`
  - `as_tick_rounding_policy_ref`
  - `as_fee_aware_quote_clip_ref`
- **Validation hooks:** `test_as_intensity_parameter_card_present.py`, `test_as_spread_basis.py`, `test_as_tick_rounding_and_fee_clip.py`

Hard rules:
- no Avellaneda–Stoikov implementation may go forward if `gamma`, `sigma` horizon alignment, `A`, `kappa`, spread basis, tick rounding, or fee-aware clipping is implicit;
- half-spread and full-spread formulations may not be silently mixed;
- if the family is used only as a comparator or advisory overlay, that scope must still be declared explicitly in the packet basis.

### 19.7 Mean-variance utility
Generic quadratic objective:
`maximize μᵀ w - λ wᵀ Σ w - costs - penalties`

Rule:
`λ`, constraints, turnover costs, leverage caps, and no-trade buffers must all be explicit.

### 19.8 Generic QUBO
`minimize xᵀ Q x + cᵀ x + penalty_terms`

Rule:
all penalties must be named, bounded, and versioned.

### 19.8A Portfolio-selection QUBO specialization
A canonical portfolio-selection specialization is:
`minimize θ Σ_{i,j} Cov(i,j) x_i x_j - M (Σ_i r_i x_i - R)^2 + λ_card (Σ_i x_i - K)^2 + λ_budget budget_penalty + λ_turnover turnover_penalty`

Interpretation:
- `x_i ∈ {0,1}` for inclusion / exclusion in the simplest binary form,
- `θ` scales covariance / risk,
- `M` enforces the target-return term,
- `K` is the explicit cardinality target when a pick-`K` constraint is used.

Rule:
Direct Sharpe-ratio division is not the default circuit objective. When Sharpe-style logic is desired, Codex must use an explicit surrogate utility or transformed objective rather than silently embedding division inside a quantum circuit.

### 19.8B Continuous-variable / sum-constrained portfolio comparator reference
- **Formula / basis:** a continuous or sum-constrained alternative may minimize average overlapping-period cost or related allocation utility without forcing every allocation into binary inclusion variables.
- **Canonical storage basis:** `CV_PORTFOLIO_COMPARATOR_PACKET`, explicit allocation-basis flag, and comparator receipt versus the incumbent classical or binary-QUBO formulation.
- **Hard rule:** this section is a comparator reference only. Codex may not silently replace the canonical binary-QUBO specialization with a continuous-variable solver unless the task family, allocation basis, and comparator win are all declared explicitly.

### 19.12A Classical Monte Carlo vs amplitude-estimation convergence
- **Formula / basis:** classical Monte Carlo error `O(1/√N)` versus amplitude-estimation family error `O(1/N)` under identical payoff/state-preparation assumptions.
- **Canonical storage basis:** estimator-family comparator packet with identical payoff definition, budget, and confidence target.
- **Hard rule:** no quantum speedup claim is admissible unless the same payoff, same state-preparation assumptions, and same resource accounting are declared for both the classical and quantum comparator.

### 19.12B Amplitude-estimation payoff-encoding and amplification reference
- **Formula / basis:** the payoff must be encoded into a bounded amplitude through an explicit state-preparation/operator contract, followed by an explicit amplification contract based on the declared Grover-style iterate or equivalent amplitude-amplification primitive.
- **Canonical storage basis:** `AE_PAYOFF_ENCODING_PACKET`, `AMPLIFICATION_OPERATOR_PACKET`, rescaling receipt, and estimator-output receipt.
- **Hard rule:** Codex may not write amplitude-estimation code that leaves payoff rescaling, amplification operator identity, or estimator-output interpretation implicit.

### 19.17A Shannon entropy regime filter
- **Formula / basis:** `H(X) = - Σ_x p(x) log p(x)`
- **Canonical storage basis:** entropy scalar, normalization receipt, and regime-band packet
- **Hard rule:** window, binning/discretization policy, and normalization basis must be explicit.

### 19.17B Transfer entropy information-flow reference
- **Formula / basis:** `TE_{Y→X} = Σ p(x_{t+1}, x_t^k, y_t^l) log ( p(x_{t+1}|x_t^k, y_t^l) / p(x_{t+1}|x_t^k) )`
- **Canonical storage basis:** directed information-flow scalar plus source/target clock alignment receipt
- **Hard rule:** source clock, target clock, lag orders, and conditioning basis may never remain implicit.

### 19.17C Maximum-entropy neutral-density reference
- **Formula / basis:** choose the density that maximizes entropy subject to the declared moment or pricing constraints.
- **Canonical storage basis:** density parameter packet, constraint set, and comparator receipt versus the incumbent classical neutral-density method
- **Hard rule:** this family is challenger-only unless constraints, numerical method, and comparator parity are all explicit.

### 19.17D Risk-neutral density-operator research reference
- **Formula / basis:** research family only; when a quantum-information framing is used, the no-arbitrage challenger study must state the declared density-operator object, martingale condition, and mapping back to the incumbent classical risk-neutral-density method.
- **Canonical storage basis:** `RND_OPERATOR_RESEARCH_PACKET`, martingale-condition receipt, and comparator receipt versus the declared classical neutral-density baseline.
- **Hard rule:** Codex may not present density-operator language as production truth, live pricing law, or live arbitrage detector without an explicit research-only flag and comparator parity.

### 19.9 Brier score
`BS = (1/N) Σ_i (p_i - y_i)^2`

Rule:
the monitoring layer should track reliability and resolution decomposition where data is sufficient.

### 19.9A QLIKE volatility-forecast loss
- **Formula / basis:** for positive realized or proxy variance `v_t > 0` and positive forecast variance `h_t > 0`, preserve the canonical QLIKE loss as `L_QLIKE(v_t,h_t) = v_t / h_t - ln(v_t / h_t) - 1`, with `ln(h_t) + v_t / h_t` admissible only as an explicitly declared equivalent form on the same basis.
- **Canonical storage basis:** variance proxy basis, forecast-variance basis, positivity receipt, and score packet.
- **Hard rule:** QLIKE may not silently mix standard deviation forecasts, variance forecasts, log-variance forecasts, or negative / zero proxy values.

### 19.9B Quantile and interval scores
- **Formula / basis:** for quantile level `alpha in (0,1)`, observation `y`, and quantile forecast `q_alpha`, preserve the canonical quantile score as `QS_alpha(q_alpha,y) = (1-alpha) * (q_alpha - y)` when `y < q_alpha` and `alpha * (y - q_alpha)` when `y >= q_alpha`; for symmetric interval miscoverage `alpha`, lower endpoint `l`, and upper endpoint `u`, preserve the canonical interval score as `IS_alpha(l,u,y) = (u-l) + (2/alpha)(l-y) 1(y<l) + (2/alpha)(y-u) 1(y>u)`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** quantile level, interval coverage, endpoint identity receipt, and score packet.
- **Hard rule:** quantile and interval scores may not silently switch between asymmetric quantile endpoints and symmetric central-interval conventions.

### 19.9C Continuous ranked probability score
- **Formula / basis:** for predictive CDF `F` and realization `y`, preserve the canonical CRPS as `CRPS(F,y) = integral_{R} (F(z) - 1{y <= z})^2 dz`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** CDF-threshold basis or declared sample-forecast approximation basis, threshold-weight receipt when weighted CRPS is used, and score packet.
- **Hard rule:** CRPS calculations may not assume a valid monotone CDF unless the CDF monotonicity check or sample-forecast approximation basis is explicit.

### 19.9D Energy and variogram multivariate scores
- **Formula / basis:** for multivariate realization `y in R^d` and forecast samples `X_1,...,X_m`, preserve the canonical energy score as `ES(F,y) = (1/m) sum_i ||X_i - y|| - (1/(2m^2)) sum_i sum_j ||X_i - X_j||`; preserve the variogram score of order `p` as `VS_p(F,y) = sum_i sum_j w_{ij} ( |y^(i)-y^(j)|^p - (1/m) sum_k |X_k^(i)-X_k^(j)|^p )^2`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** multivariate sample forecast matrix, norm basis, `w_ij` weight policy, variogram order `p`, and score packet.
- **Hard rule:** multivariate scores may not silently guess weight matrices, norm basis, or the variogram order; if no custom weight matrix is declared, the all-ones weight policy must be stated explicitly.

### 19.9E Pairwise Diebold-Mariano and HLN predictive-accuracy comparison
- **Formula / basis:** for two forecast systems evaluated on one declared loss basis with loss differential `d_t = L_{1,t} - L_{2,t}`, preserve the canonical Diebold-Mariano statistic as `DM = mean(d) / sqrt(f_hat_d(0) / T)` where `f_hat_d(0)` is the declared HAC estimate of the long-run variance of `d_t`; when the small-sample correction is active, preserve the Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold corrected statistic as `DM_HLN = DM * sqrt((T + 1 - 2h + h(h-1)/T) / T)`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** pairwise loss basis, forecast horizon `h`, HAC lag policy, small-sample-correction mode, and pairwise superiority packet.
- **Hard rule:** pairwise predictive-accuracy testing may not silently switch loss basis, forecast horizon, or serial-correlation treatment; when `h > 1`, the HAC lag policy must remain explicit.

### 19.10 CVaR / expected shortfall
For loss `L` and tail level `α`, CVaR is the expected loss conditional on being in the worst `1-α` tail.

Rule:
tail level and sampling basis must be explicit.

### 19.10A WCVaR / weighted-tail objective
For sampled losses or energies `ℓ_i` in a declared tail set `T_α` and declared non-negative weights `w_i`,

`WCVaR_α = (Σ_{i ∈ T_α} w_i ℓ_i) / (Σ_{i ∈ T_α} w_i)`

Rule:
- the tail-membership rule, tail side, and weighting basis must all be explicit;
- and WCVaR may never be reported as plain CVaR unless the weighting basis is uniform.

### 19.10B WCVaR supporting sample-statistics formulas
For declared sampled returns or payoffs `r_{ki}` over samples `k=1..M` and assets / components `i,j`, the supporting sample-statistics identities used by the uploaded-file WCVaR figure are:

`μ_i = (1/M) Σ_{k=1}^{M} r_{ki}`

`σ_{ij} = (1/(M-1)) Σ_{k=1}^{M} (r_{ki} - μ_i)(r_{kj} - μ_j)`

Rule:
- if WCVaR, energy-weighted CVaR, or any tail-weighted portfolio objective is reported with supporting sample statistics, the sample basis `r_{ki}`, the averaging window `M`, and the covariance basis must all be explicit;
- if those support-statistics identities are not explicit, the run may still use plain CVaR or expected-value aggregation, but it may not claim the stronger WCVaR-support formulation.

Validation hooks:
- `test_wcvar_supporting_sample_statistics.py`
- `test_wcvar_sample_basis_and_window.py`

### 19.10C Expected-shortfall decomposition and tail-budget reference
- **Formula / basis:** `VaR_α(L) = inf{l : F_L(l) >= α}`; `ES_α(L) = E[L | L >= VaR_α(L)]`; Euler component contribution `RC_i = w_i * ∂ ES_α / ∂ w_i`; incremental contribution `IES_i = ES_α(w) - ES_α(w_{-i})`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** total ES receipt, marginal-ES vector, component-ES vector, incremental-ES receipt, declared loss-sign / horizon / weighting basis.
- **Hard rule:** expected shortfall, component contributions, and incremental contributions may not be compared across sleeves unless the loss sign, horizon, confidence level, weighting scheme, and stress basis are identical or explicitly reconciled.

### 19.11 Markout
Markout basis must declare:
- horizon,
- side convention,
- price benchmark,
- fee adjustment,
- units (ticks, bps, cents, dollars, log-return).

### 19.11A Execution-schedule benchmark formulas
- **Formula / basis:** `q_t^TWAP = Q / N`; `q_t^VWAP = Q * v_t^forecast / Σ_t v_t^forecast`; `q_t^PVOL = ρ * V_t^mkt`; arrival-price implementation shortfall `IS = side * (P_exec_avg - P_arrival)` on the declared fee/rebate basis; close benchmark `CLOS = side * (P_exec_avg - P_close)`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** parent-order size `Q`, bucket count `N`, forecast-volume curve `v_t^forecast`, realized market-volume path `V_t^mkt`, participation rate `ρ`, arrival benchmark, close benchmark, fee/rebate basis.
- **Hard rule:** TWAP, VWAP, PVOL, arrival-price, and close-target execution are distinct objective families and may not be mixed under one ambiguous “smart execution” label.

### 19.11B Market-impact and illiquidity reference
- **Formula / basis:** temporary impact `I_temp = side * (P_exec_avg - P_arrival_mid)`; permanent impact `I_perm(h) = side * (P_mid_{t+h} - P_arrival_mid)`; square-root benchmark `I_sr(Q) = Y * σ * sqrt(Q / V)`; Kyle-style benchmark `r_t = λ q_t + ε_t`; Amihud illiquidity benchmark `ILLIQ_t = |r_t| / DollarVolume_t`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** arrival mid, execution VWAP, post-trade horizon mid, signed size, volatility basis `σ`, volume basis `V`, signed-order-flow proxy, dollar-volume basis.
- **Hard rule:** impact metrics are basis-sensitive and may not share horizon, sign, or volume conventions implicitly; the square-root law is a calibration benchmark, not a hidden universal production constant.

### 19.11C Almgren-Chriss optimal-execution reference
- **Formula / basis:** discrete price path `S_k = S_{k-1} + σ * sqrt(τ) * ξ_k - τ g(n_k/τ)`; execution price `S̃_k = S_{k-1} - h(n_k/τ)`; remaining inventory `x_k = X - Σ_{j=1}^k n_j`; canonical objective `min E[C] + λ Var(C)` with `x_0 = X`, `x_N = 0`, and declared benchmark / sign basis.
- **Canonical storage basis:** parent order size `X`, bucket count `N`, interval `τ`, volatility basis `σ`, temporary-impact family `h`, permanent-impact family `g`, normalized risk-aversion `λ`, participation cap, physical-time versus volume-time flag.
- **Hard rule:** Almgren-Chriss schedules may not be compared across runs unless impact family, benchmark basis, horizon basis, and utility normalization are identical or explicitly reconciled.

### 19.11D Liquidation value-at-risk and liquidation-expected-shortfall reference
- **Formula / basis:** `LVaR_α = Quantile_α(C)` for liquidation-cost random variable `C`; normal-approximation benchmark `LVaR_α ≈ E[C] + z_α * sqrt(Var(C))`; liquidation expected shortfall `LES_α = E[C | C >= LVaR_α]`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** confidence level `α`, horizon basis, cost-sign convention, distribution-family receipt, benchmark basis, and scenario / variance support packet.
- **Hard rule:** no `LVaR` or `LES` number may be rendered owner-facing unless confidence, horizon, loss-sign, and distribution-family semantics are explicit.

### 19.12 Quantum amplitude estimation family
The system must separately declare:
- family (`canonical_qae`, `iqae`, `mlae`, `fae`, etc.),

### 19.13 Bayesian posterior update
- **Formula / basis:** `Posterior = Likelihood × Prior / Evidence`
- **Canonical storage basis:** probability in `[0,1]`
- **Hard rule:** prior basis must be declared as market-implied, model-implied, or blended; posterior may never mix odds and probability without explicit transform.

### 19.14 Bayesian information gain gate
- **Formula / basis:** `IG = KL(Posterior || Prior)`
- **Canonical storage basis:** nonnegative divergence scalar
- **Public default:** always store the realized information-gain scalar when posterior updating is used
- **Seed authority route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed):** gating thresholds are calibrated, not hardcoded universally

### 19.15 LMSR market-impact reference
- **Formula / basis:** `C(q) = b ln(Σ exp(q_i / b))`
- **Canonical storage basis:** cost and marginal price-impact packet
- **Hard rule:** the liquidity parameter `b` must be venue- and market-specific; no static one-size-fits-all LMSR depth assumption is allowed.

### 19.15A Dual-sided prediction-market spread, LP-reward, and adverse-selection reference
- **Formula / basis:** same-contract dual-sided spread identity `π = 1 - (p_yes + p_no)` under the declared venue payout convention; LP-reward programs that use midpoint-distance penalties must declare their reward function explicitly, including quadratic-decay or equivalent basis where applicable; any active venue reward program that imposes a minimum on-book eligibility floor must declare that floor explicitly in seconds.
- **Canonical storage basis:** dual-sided spread packet, LP-reward schedule packet, LP minimum-quote-age receipt, adverse-selection warning receipt
- **Hard rules:** this reference is `RESEARCH_ONLY` and tied to prediction-market liquidity-provider / market-making research; no dual-sided YES/NO quoting path may be promoted without an explicit adverse-selection comparator, liquidity threshold, batch-limit compatibility receipt when batched posting is used, and fee/rebate-normalized profitability receipt; reward-program formulas may orient research but may not be treated as standalone alpha; when the active official Polymarket reward program declares a minimum quote-age floor, the current public research seed is `3.5` seconds and must remain venue-rule-driven rather than guessed.

### 19.16 Hawkes conditional intensity reference
- **Formula / basis:** `λ(t) = μ + Σ α exp(-β(t - t_i))` for exponential-kernel reference studies
- **Canonical storage basis:** baseline intensity, excitation kernel, branching-ratio receipt
- **Canonical family home:** `EX-11C` for the admitted Hawkes event-intensity family; this reference section remains formula-only.
- **Hard rule:** intensity outputs must remain separate from direct trade signals unless a dedicated evaluation lane approves them.

### 19.17 Peaks-over-threshold / GPD reference
- **Formula / basis:** exceedances over a declared threshold are modeled with generalized Pareto scale and shape parameters
- **Canonical storage basis:** threshold quantile, exceedance count, scale, shape, tail-risk packet
- **Hard rule:** threshold basis must be explicit, usually a declared quantile such as `0.90`, `0.95`, or `0.99`.

### 19.18 Poisson and Tweedie link basis
- **Formula / basis:** Poisson uses log-link mean; Tweedie link basis must be declared explicitly when `power` changes the target semantics
- **Canonical storage basis:** canonical mean and inverse-link transformed mean kept distinct
- **Hard rule:** no downstream consumer may confuse log-link output with natural-scale mean.

### 19.19 Venue fee-basis reference
- **Formula / basis:** fee schedule logic is connector-versioned and persisted by venue rather than hardcoded globally in the strategy layer
- **Canonical storage basis:** per-order fee estimate, realized fee, maker/taker basis, venue schedule version
- **Hard rule:** venue fees are resolved through connector metadata and schedule versioning, not freehand constants inside trading logic.

### 19.19A Omega ratio reference
Let `r_t` be returns and `τ` the minimum acceptable return over the window.
- `Omega(τ) = Sum(max(r_t - τ, 0)) / Sum(max(τ - r_t, 0))`
- required declared companions: threshold-return basis, sampling frequency, and whether sums or expectation approximations are used

Rule:
Omega is an advanced companion metric for asymmetric return paths. It is owner-visible and benchmark-usable only when the threshold-return basis is explicit.

### 19.19B Information ratio reference
For active return `a_t = r_t - b_t` against benchmark `b_t`:
- `IR = mean(a_t) / std(a_t)`
- annualized variants must declare the annualization profile explicitly

Rule:
Information Ratio may not be shown without benchmark identity, benchmark sampling frequency, and tracking-error basis.

### 19.19B1 Calmar ratio reference
For compound annual growth or another explicitly annualized return basis `R_ann` and maximum drawdown magnitude `|MDD|` over the same declared window:
- `Calmar = R_ann / |MDD|`
- when an excess-return variant is used, the numerator must declare the risk-free subtraction basis explicitly rather than being silently assumed
- the standard benchmark review window is trailing 36 months unless a shorter or longer declared horizon is materially required by the sleeve's live history length or strategy horizon

Rule:
Calmar may not be shown without explicit return basis, explicit maximum-drawdown window, and explicit horizon identity. It is a companion drawdown-efficiency metric and may not silently replace Sharpe, Sterling, Ulcer, or realized net-P&L review.

### 19.19B2 MAR ratio reference
For compound annual growth rate since inception `CAGR_since_inception` and maximum drawdown magnitude `|MDD_since_inception|` over the same since-inception history:
- `MAR = CAGR_since_inception / |MDD_since_inception|`
- the inception date and the history actually admitted into the since-inception window must be explicit

Rule:
MAR is an allocator-facing companion to Calmar rather than a replacement for it. MAR may not be compared across sleeves unless the inception window, CAGR basis, and maximum-drawdown basis are explicit, because MAR is since-inception while Calmar commonly uses a trailing-window basis.

### 19.19B3 K-ratio reference
For a declared Value-Added Monthly Index (`VAMI`) or an explicitly declared equivalent cumulative-return curve:
- K-ratio uses a linear regression on the logarithmic cumulative-return path of the declared VAMI basis
- the slope of that regression is the return-trend component and the standard error of the slope is the instability component
- the active formula profile must be explicit: `{KESTNER_1996, KESTNER_2003, KESTNER_2013}`
- required declared companions at minimum: `k_ratio_formula_profile`, `k_ratio_vami_start_notional`, `vami_sampling_frequency`, `log_cumulative_return_basis`, `regression_slope_basis`, `regression_standard_error_basis`, and `observation_count_window`

Rule:
K-ratio is an allocator-facing equity-curve-consistency companion metric. It may not be compared across sleeves, managers, or bundles unless the same VAMI basis, same sampling frequency, same log-cumulative-return basis, same regression-slope basis, and same formula-profile variant are preserved side by side. It complements Sharpe / Sortino / Calmar rather than replacing them.

### 19.19B4 Treynor ratio reference
For declared portfolio return `R_p`, risk-free rate `R_f`, and benchmark-relative systematic-risk coefficient `β_p`:
- `Treynor = (R_p - R_f) / β_p`
- the benchmark used to estimate `β_p` must be explicit and must match the sleeve's declared investable benchmark family rather than one unrelated broad index
- negative or near-zero beta cases must emit a `NOT_MEANINGFUL_ON_DECLARED_BASIS` or `BENCHMARK_SCOPE_REVIEW_REQUIRED` state rather than silently ranking such sleeves

Rule:
Treynor is an allocator-facing reward-to-systematic-risk companion metric. It is admissible only when the sleeve is sufficiently diversified for beta to be interpretable, the benchmark identity is explicit, and the beta-estimation window is declared next to the reported value.

### 19.19B5 Jensen alpha reference
For realized portfolio return `R_p`, risk-free rate `R_f`, realized benchmark return `R_m`, and benchmark-relative beta `β_p` under a declared CAPM basis:
- `JensenAlpha = R_p - (R_f + β_p * (R_m - R_f))`
- required declared companions at minimum: declared `benchmark_id` scope binding, `benchmark_relative_beta_estimation_window`, `risk_free_rate_window`, `market_return_window`, and `capm_formula_profile`
- positive, negative, and zero alpha outcomes must remain benchmark-relative interpretations rather than universal live-promotion thresholds

Rule:
Jensen alpha is an abnormal-return companion metric for manager- and sleeve-review workflows. It may not be displayed or compared across sleeves unless the benchmark identity, beta-estimation basis, and risk-free-rate basis are all explicit, because otherwise alpha and simple active return can be silently conflated.

### 19.19B6 M2 / Modigliani risk-adjusted performance reference
For declared portfolio return `R_p`, risk-free rate `R_f`, portfolio volatility `σ_p`, benchmark volatility `σ_m`, and benchmark or market return `R_m` on the same explicit horizon basis:
- first compute the Sharpe basis `SR = (R_p - R_f) / σ_p`
- compute the risk-adjusted return on the benchmark-volatility basis as `M2_return = R_f + SR * σ_m`
- compute benchmark-relative excess on that same basis as `M2_excess = M2_return - R_m` when a benchmark-return comparison is rendered
- required declared companions at minimum: declared `benchmark_id` scope binding, `benchmark_volatility_window`, `portfolio_volatility_window`, `risk_free_rate_window`, and `m2_formula_profile`
- zero or near-zero `σ_p` cases must emit `NOT_MEANINGFUL_ON_DECLARED_BASIS` rather than a silently infinite ranking

Rule:
M2 is an allocator-facing companion to Sharpe that expresses risk-adjusted performance in return units on the benchmark-volatility basis rather than as a dimensionless ratio. It may not be compared across sleeves unless the benchmark identity, volatility windows, and return basis are explicit.

### 19.19B7 Appraisal ratio reference
For declared active-management alpha `α_p` and residual or idiosyncratic risk `σ_ε` from the declared factor-regression basis:
- `AppraisalRatio = α_p / σ_ε`
- required declared companions at minimum: `benchmark_or_factor_model_id`, `alpha_estimation_window`, `residual_risk_window`, `factor_regression_profile`, and `benchmark_relative_annualization_profile_when_used`
- if residual risk is zero, non-estimable, or not comparable on the declared factor basis, the metric must emit `NOT_MEANINGFUL_ON_DECLARED_BASIS` or `FACTOR_MODEL_REVIEW_REQUIRED` rather than silently ranking the sleeve

Rule:
Appraisal ratio is an active-management companion metric for benchmark-relative or factor-relative alpha review. It may not be conflated with Information Ratio because the denominator is residual active-management risk from the declared factor model rather than generic tracking error.

### 19.19B8 Up-market and down-market capture ratio reference
For declared benchmark-relative sleeve return `R_p` and benchmark return `R_b` on the same horizon basis:
- `UpMarketCapture = (R_p_up / R_b_up) * 100` using only benchmark-up subperiods where `R_b_up > 0`
- `DownMarketCapture = (R_p_down / R_b_down) * 100` using only benchmark-down subperiods where `R_b_down < 0`
- required declared companions at minimum: declared `benchmark_id` scope binding, `benchmark_relative_up_down_market_partition_rule`, `benchmark_relative_capture_return_aggregation_profile`, and `benchmark_relative_annualization_profile_when_used`
- if the relevant benchmark-up or benchmark-down denominator is zero, missing, or not comparable on the declared basis, the corresponding capture metric must emit `NOT_MEANINGFUL_ON_DECLARED_BASIS`

Rule:
Capture ratios are benchmark-relative allocator companion metrics. `UpMarketCapture > 100` indicates outperformance in benchmark-up periods, while `DownMarketCapture < 100` indicates shallower losses than the benchmark during benchmark-down periods. QTT may not show one capture ratio without the other when the sleeve is benchmark-relative, because upside participation without downside-protection context is incomplete.

### 19.19B9 Burke ratio reference
For declared excess return `(R_p - r_f)` and realized drawdown sequence `D_j <= 0` over the declared review window:
- `Burke = (R_p - r_f) / sqrt(Sum_j D_j^2)` under the declared drawdown enumeration and return annualization basis
- `ModifiedBurke = (R_p - r_f) / sqrt((1/n) * Sum_j D_j^2)` only when the modified-normalized variant is explicitly selected and `n` is the declared drawdown-count normalization basis
- required declared companions at minimum: `burke_formula_profile`, `burke_drawdown_series_basis`, `burke_drawdown_enumeration_window`, `burke_return_annualization_profile`, and `burke_risk_free_rate_basis_family`
- if excess return, drawdown enumeration, or normalization basis is missing or not comparable on the declared horizon, the Burke-family metric must emit `NOT_MEANINGFUL_ON_DECLARED_BASIS`

Rule:
Burke-family metrics are drawdown-dispersion allocator companions, not substitutes for Calmar, MAR, Sterling, or Ulcer-family metrics. QTT may not compare Burke-family values across sleeves unless the return horizon, drawdown enumeration window, and normalization profile are explicit and matched.

### 19.19B10 Gain-to-Pain ratio reference
For declared aggregated return series `r_t` on an explicit observation basis:
- `GainToPain = Sum_t r_t / |Sum_{t: r_t < 0} r_t|` on the declared aggregation basis
- equivalently, if gains and losses are stored separately on the same basis, `GainToPain = NetReturn / |CumulativeLoss|`
- required declared companions at minimum: `gain_to_pain_observation_basis`, `gain_to_pain_aggregation_frequency`, `gain_to_pain_negative_return_inclusion_rule`, `gain_to_pain_fee_inclusion_basis`, and `gain_to_pain_zero_cumulative_loss_policy`
- if cumulative loss is zero or not comparable on the declared basis, the metric must emit `NOT_MEANINGFUL_ON_DECLARED_BASIS` or an explicit zero-loss handling state rather than silently ranking the sleeve as infinite

Rule:
Gain-to-Pain is a trading-manager companion metric for comparing cumulative net gain against cumulative loss burden on the same declared basis. It may not be compared across sleeves unless the observation basis, fee inclusion basis, and zero-loss handling rule are explicit, because monthly, daily, and trade-by-trade constructions can diverge materially.

### 19.19C Sterling ratio reference
For cumulative or annualized return `R` and drawdown family `DD` with an explicit drawdown buffer `c`:
- `Sterling = R / (|DD| + c)`

Rule:
Sterling variants differ across literature. QTT must therefore bind Sterling to a named formula profile and emit a `PERFORMANCE_METRIC_FORMULA_PROFILE_RECEIPT` whenever it is used. Canonical Day-1 parameterization resolves through `GV-19A3` once Sterling-family values are rendered on owner-facing performance cards or promotion-review packets.

### 19.19D Ulcer Index and Ulcer Performance Index reference
For percentage drawdown series `d_t <= 0` over window length `n`:
- `UlcerIndex = sqrt( (1/n) * Sum(d_t^2) )`
- `UPI = (R - r_f_or_target) / UlcerIndex` under the declared return and threshold convention

Rule:
Ulcer-family metrics are about underwater-path pain, not just endpoint loss. They are especially useful where recovery duration matters materially to survivability or owner comfort.

### 19.19D1 Drawdown duration and time-under-water reference
- `drawdown_duration` and `time_under_water` must preserve the elapsed time from a local equity peak to recovery of that peak on the declared timestamp basis.
- required declared companions at minimum: `max_drawdown_duration_window`, `average_drawdown_duration_window`, `current_time_under_water`, `peak_to_recovery_clock_basis`, and `underwater_depth_series_receipt`
- drawdown-duration cards may use trading days, calendar days, hours, or declared venue-native event bars, but the clock basis may not be mixed silently across sleeves

Rule:
drawdown-depth review is incomplete without duration review. Owner-facing drawdown-pain panels may not compare sleeves on Calmar, MAR, Sterling, or Ulcer-family metrics alone when materially different recovery-duration profiles exist; adjacent duration or time-under-water context is mandatory.


### 19.19E Advisory benchmark-band labeling rule
### 19.19F Sharpe, Sortino, and trade-outcome metric reference
- Sharpe and Sortino are dimensionless ratios, but any annualized view must declare sampling frequency and annualization factor explicitly.
- `risk_free_rate_window` must match the metric horizon and sampling frequency.
- `downside_target_rate_window` for Sortino must be explicit; allowed day-1 seeds include `0` or a matched risk-free profile, but never implicitly.
- Sharpe / Sortino canonical Day-1 parameterization resolves through `GV-19A2B` once owner-facing cards, promotion packets, or benchmark-safe comparison views render those ratios.
- Profit factor, hit rate, expectancy, MAE, and MFE must all declare their storage basis explicitly:
  - `profit_factor_window` uses gross-profit / gross-loss and must declare the explicit zero-gross-loss division policy when gross loss is zero;
  - `hit_rate_window` must declare whether it is stored on `[0,1]` or percent basis;
  - `expectancy_window` must declare whether it is per trade, per event, per contract, per share, or per unit notional;
  - `mae_window` and `mfe_window` must declare whether they are stored in price units, return units, currency P&L, or bps.
- These metric families are admissible companion metrics, not basis-free universal live thresholds.

Hard rule:
No owner-facing performance card may annualize Sharpe or Sortino, or compare hit rate / expectancy / MAE / MFE across sleeves, unless the underlying basis and observation window are explicit.
Public benchmark bands may be displayed only as:
- `ADVISORY_BENCHMARK_GUIDE`
- `OWNER_VISIBLE`
- `NON_AUTHORITATIVE_FOR_PROMOTION`
- `MARKET_SCOPE_REVIEW_REQUIRED`

Hard rule:
Benchmark bands may orient the owner, but no public metric band may become an automatic live-authority threshold without internal replay, shadow, and owner-gated validation.

### GV-19E2 — Pairwise predictive-accuracy and proper-scoring forecast-evaluation family
- **Domain:** governance, validation, replay / shadow selection control, probabilistic forecast evaluation, and benchmark-safe model comparison
- **Purpose:** Preserve one canonical home for pairwise forecast-comparison and proper-scoring procedures so QTT does not stop at RC / SPA / StepM / MCS, Brier, or log-score overlays when materially used sleeves still need exact pairwise predictive-accuracy tests and exact loss families for volatility, quantile, interval, density, or multivariate probabilistic forecasts.
- **Families included once here:** `DIEBOLD_MARIANO_EQUAL_PREDICTIVE_ACCURACY`, `HARVEY_LEYBOURNE_NEWBOLD_SMALL_SAMPLE_CORRECTION`, `ROBUST_VOLATILITY_PROXY_LOSS_PANEL`, `PROPER_SCORING_RULE_PANEL`
- **Formula / operating law:**
  - on one declared scoring basis where smaller is better, define pairwise loss differentials `d_t = L_{1,t} - L_{2,t}` and preserve the canonical pairwise Diebold-Mariano statistic `DM = mean(d) / sqrt(f_hat_d(0) / T)` on the declared HAC long-run-variance basis;
  - when the small-sample correction is active, preserve the canonical HLN-corrected statistic `DM_HLN = DM * sqrt((T + 1 - 2h + h(h-1)/T) / T)` rather than leaving small-sample handling implicit;
  - for positive volatility proxy `v_t` and positive forecast variance `h_t`, preserve the canonical QLIKE loss `L_QLIKE(v_t,h_t) = v_t / h_t - ln(v_t / h_t) - 1` on the declared proxy and variance basis;
  - for quantile level `alpha`, observation `y`, and quantile forecast `q_alpha`, preserve the canonical quantile score as `QS_alpha(q_alpha,y) = (1-alpha) * (q_alpha - y)` when `y < q_alpha` and `alpha * (y - q_alpha)` when `y >= q_alpha`;
  - for interval miscoverage `alpha`, lower endpoint `l`, upper endpoint `u`, and observation `y`, preserve the canonical interval score `IS_alpha(l,u,y) = (u-l) + (2/alpha)(l-y) 1(y<l) + (2/alpha)(y-u) 1(y>u)` on the declared symmetric central-interval basis;
  - for predictive CDF `F` and realization `y`, preserve the canonical CRPS `CRPS(F,y) = integral_{R} (F(z) - 1{y <= z})^2 dz`;
  - for multivariate forecast samples `X_1,...,X_m` and realization `y`, preserve the canonical energy score `ES(F,y) = (1/m) sum_i ||X_i - y|| - (1/(2m^2)) sum_i sum_j ||X_i - X_j||` and the canonical variogram score `VS_p(F,y) = sum_i sum_j w_{ij} ( |y^(i)-y^(j)|^p - (1/m) sum_k |X_k^(i)-X_k^(j)|^p )^2` on the declared weight and order basis;
  - all procedures admitted here are comparator and governance families only; none may self-authorize live orders, hidden benchmark swaps, or hidden loss-basis swaps.
- **Inputs:** pairwise forecast streams or score streams, observed outcomes, declared scoring basis, forecast horizon `h`, HAC lag policy, small-sample-correction mode, volatility proxy basis when QLIKE is used, quantile levels, interval endpoints and coverage, predictive CDF or sample forecast basis, multivariate sample forecast matrix, weight matrix policy, and comparator receipts linking statistical results back to economic-delta evidence
- **Outputs / basis:** pairwise predictive-accuracy packet, HLN-corrected pairwise superiority packet, QLIKE volatility-loss packet, quantile-score packet, interval-score packet, CRPS packet, energy-score packet, variogram-score packet, proper-scoring winner packet, and promotion-admissibility advisory state
- **Public default:** pairwise predictive-accuracy diagnostics remain advisory and replay / shadow governance only; when a materially used sleeve preserves volatility-proxy forecasts, quantile forecasts, interval forecasts, or probabilistic sample forecasts, the appropriate proper scoring rule from this family must be declared explicitly rather than silently collapsing everything to MSE or MAE
- **Seed authority route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed):** preserve Diebold-Mariano with HLN small-sample correction active by default, forecast horizon `h = 1` unless a longer declared horizon is used, HAC lag policy `h-1` as the Day-1 default, QLIKE as the Day-1 robust volatility-proxy loss when forecasted objects are variances, quantile score at the active declared quantile level, symmetric interval score at 90% central coverage when no stricter interval contract is declared, CRPS for univariate distribution forecasts, energy score for multivariate sample forecasts, and variogram score with `p = 0.5` and all-ones weights as the Day-1 default multivariate challenger basis
- **Bounded search range:** pairwise loss basis `{MSE_LOSS,MAE_LOSS,NEG_LOG_LOSS,BRIER_LOSS,QLIKE_LOSS,QUANTILE_SCORE,INTERVAL_SCORE,CRPS,ENERGY_SCORE,VARIOGRAM_SCORE,NEGATIVE_NET_PNL_PER_RISK_UNIT}` with `QLIKE_LOSS` preferred for noisy variance-proxy comparison and `CRPS` preferred for univariate distribution forecasts; forecast horizon `h in {1,2,5,10,20}`; HAC lag policy `{H_MINUS_1,SQRT_T,DECLARED_EXPLICIT_LAG}` with `H_MINUS_1` as Day-1 default; small-sample correction mode `{HLN_ON,HLN_OFF}` with `HLN_ON` as Day-1 default; interval coverage `{0.50,0.80,0.90,0.95}` with `0.90` as Day-1 default when no stricter forecast contract exists; variogram order `p in {0.5,1.0}` with `0.5` as Day-1 default; weight policy `{ALL_ONES,DECLARED_DISTANCE_AWARE_WEIGHT_MATRIX}` with `ALL_ONES` as Day-1 default
- **Runtime resolution:** batch_evaluation_only after completed replay, walk-forward, or shadow campaigns; never hidden live-authoritative
- **Fallback behavior:** if the pairwise loss basis, forecast horizon, HAC lag policy, quantile level, interval coverage, volatility-proxy basis, multivariate weight policy, or score sign convention is ambiguous, QTT must quarantine the affected comparison as advisory-only and fall back to the strongest already-declared simpler metric packet with a `PAIRWISE_FORECAST_EVAL_FALLBACK_RECEIPT` rather than guessing a basis
- **Validation hooks:** `test_pairwise_forecast_eval_loss_basis_declared.py`, `test_dm_hln_horizon_and_hac_policy_declared.py`, `test_qlike_requires_positive_variance_basis.py`, `test_quantile_score_level_declared.py`, `test_interval_score_coverage_declared.py`, `test_crps_basis_declared.py`, `test_multivariate_score_weight_policy_declared.py`, `test_pairwise_forecast_eval_fallback_receipt_required_when_basis_ambiguous.py`
- **Promotion class:** research_to_triggered_live_concurrent_shadow_comparison_to_owner_approved_live

Hard rules:
- no materially used sleeve may claim pairwise superiority from a Diebold-Mariano family without an explicit loss basis, forecast horizon, and serial-correlation treatment;
- no volatility-forecast family using noisy variance proxies may silently compare candidates on arbitrary squared-error surfaces when the declared robust-volatility-proxy basis is QLIKE;
- QLIKE may not silently compare standard deviations to variances or allow zero / negative forecast variance;
- quantile, interval, CRPS, energy, and variogram scores are companion diagnostics, not replacements for economic-delta, replay realism, shadow evidence, or implementation evidence;
- multivariate sample-forecast scores may not silently guess `w_ij` or the variogram order `p`;
- pairwise statistical superiority may not be treated as live-eligibility unless the stronger existing profitability, implementation, and owner-gate laws are also green.

### GV-19E3 — Forecast-calibration, nested-model-comparison, and density-and-quantile-adequacy family
- **Domain:** governance, validation, replay / shadow selection control, point-forecast calibration, nested-model comparison, predictive-density adequacy, and quantile / VaR forecast screening
- **Purpose:** Preserve one canonical home for forecast-calibration and adequacy procedures so QTT does not stop at DM / HLN, RC / SPA / StepM / MCS, Brier, log score, or proper-scoring overlays when materially used sleeves still need exact calibration regressions, exact nested-model forecast comparison, exact PIT / density adequacy checks, and exact quantile-hit adequacy screening on the forecast object actually emitted.
- **Families included once here:** `MINCER_ZARNOWITZ_CALIBRATION_REGRESSION`, `CLARK_WEST_NESTED_FORECAST_COMPARISON`, `PIT_UNIFORMITY_AND_BERKOWITZ_DENSITY_ADEQUACY`, `DYNAMIC_QUANTILE_ADEQUACY_TEST`
- **Formula / operating law:**
  - for realized outcome `y_t` and point forecast `\hat y_t`, preserve the canonical Mincer-Zarnowitz regression `y_t = alpha + beta \hat y_t + eta_t`; the Day-1 efficiency / unbiasedness diagnostic null is `alpha = 0` and `beta = 1` on the declared forecast basis unless a narrower diagnostic null is declared explicitly;
  - for parsimonious-model forecast `\hat y_{1,t,t+h}`, larger nested-model forecast `\hat y_{2,t,t+h}`, and corresponding errors `e_{1,t+h} = y_{t+h} - \hat y_{1,t,t+h}` and `e_{2,t+h} = y_{t+h} - \hat y_{2,t,t+h}`, preserve the canonical Clark-West adjusted loss differential `\hat f_{t+h} = e_{1,t+h}^2 - [e_{2,t+h}^2 - (\hat y_{1,t,t+h} - \hat y_{2,t,t+h})^2]`; the active test packet is the t-statistic of the sample mean of `\hat f_{t+h}` on the declared HAC variance basis with a one-sided alternative that the larger model has lower MSPE;
  - for predictive CDF `\hat F_t` and realization `y_t`, preserve the canonical probability integral transform `x_t = \hat F_t(y_t)`; under a correctly specified predictive density the Day-1 calibration target is iid `U(0,1)` on the declared density basis;
  - when the Berkowitz path is active, preserve the canonical transformed sequence `z_t = Phi^{-1}(x_t)` and test the transformed PIT sequence on the declared mean / variance / autocorrelation null rather than silently relying on visual inspection alone;
  - for quantile / VaR level `alpha` and active forecast `q_{alpha,t}`, preserve the canonical hit process `Hit_t(alpha) = 1(y_t < q_{alpha,t}) - alpha`; the Dynamic Quantile family tests whether the hit sequence is unbiased, independent, and independent of the active quantile estimate on the declared regressor set and declared test-distribution basis;
  - all procedures admitted here are comparator and governance families only; none may self-authorize live orders, hidden benchmark swaps, hidden calibration-null swaps, or hidden forecast-object reinterpretation.
- **Inputs:** realized outcomes, point forecasts, nested-model point forecasts, forecast horizon `h`, HAC lag policy, scoring-basis and sign convention, predictive CDF packet or sample-to-CDF bridge, PIT transform mode, Berkowitz lag count, tail-censoring mode when used, active quantile or VaR level `alpha`, hit-definition profile, DQ regressor-set profile, and comparator receipts linking statistical diagnostics back to economic-delta evidence
- **Outputs / basis:** Mincer-Zarnowitz calibration packet, Clark-West adjusted nested-model comparison packet, PIT adequacy packet, Berkowitz density-adequacy packet, Dynamic Quantile adequacy packet, calibration / adequacy winner packet, and promotion-admissibility advisory state
- **Public default:** advisory and replay / shadow governance only; when a materially used sleeve emits point forecasts, nested-model point forecasts, predictive densities, or quantile / VaR forecasts, the appropriate calibration or adequacy procedure from this family must be declared explicitly rather than silently collapsing everything to raw forecast error, generic RMSE, or simple exception counts
- **Seed authority route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed):** preserve Mincer-Zarnowitz with `alpha = 0, beta = 1` as the Day-1 calibration null for point forecasts, Clark-West as the Day-1 nested-model point-forecast comparison path with one-sided larger-model alternative and HAC variance on the declared horizon basis, PIT as the Day-1 density-calibration primitive, Berkowitz z-transform adequacy as the Day-1 formal density-screening path when predictive densities are materially used, and Dynamic Quantile with hit-process regressors covering constant, lagged hits, and the active quantile estimate as the Day-1 adequacy screen when quantile / VaR forecasts are materially used
- **Bounded search range:** calibration-null profile `{ALPHA_ZERO_BETA_ONE,ALPHA_ZERO_ONLY,BETA_ONE_ONLY,DIAGNOSTIC_UNRESTRICTED}` with `ALPHA_ZERO_BETA_ONE` as Day-1 default; forecast horizon `h in {1,2,5,10,20}`; HAC lag policy `{H_MINUS_1,SQRT_T,DECLARED_EXPLICIT_LAG}` with `H_MINUS_1` as Day-1 default; Clark-West side `{ONE_SIDED_LARGER_MODEL_BETTER}`; PIT transform mode `{RAW_U01_UNIFORMITY_CHECK,NORMAL_QUANTILE_ZTRANSFORM_FOR_BERKOWITZ}` with the z-transform active when Berkowitz diagnostics are materialized; Berkowitz lag count `{1,2,5}` with `1` as Day-1 default; Berkowitz tail mode `{FULL_DENSITY,LOWER_TAIL_CENSORED,TWO_SIDED_CENSORED}` with `FULL_DENSITY` as Day-1 default; DQ regressor-set profile `{CONST_PLUS_5_LAGGED_HITS,VAR_ESTIMATE_ONLY,CONST_PLUS_1_LAGGED_HIT_PLUS_VAR,CONST_PLUS_5_LAGGED_HITS_PLUS_VAR}` with `CONST_PLUS_5_LAGGED_HITS_PLUS_VAR` as Day-1 default; DQ test-distribution basis `{CHI_SQUARE_CONDITIONAL_ON_ESTIMATED_BETAS,HAC_WALD_DIAGNOSTIC}` with chi-square conditional-on-estimated-betas as Day-1 default
- **Runtime resolution:** batch_evaluation_only after completed replay, walk-forward, or shadow campaigns; never hidden live-authoritative
- **Fallback behavior:** if the calibration null, forecast horizon, HAC lag policy, PIT transform, Berkowitz lag or tail mode, quantile level, hit-definition profile, or DQ regressor set is ambiguous, QTT must quarantine the affected comparison as advisory-only and fall back to the strongest already-declared simpler forecast-evaluation packet with a `FORECAST_CALIBRATION_ADEQUACY_FALLBACK_RECEIPT` rather than guessing a basis
- **Validation hooks:** `test_gv19e3_mz_null_declared.py`, `test_gv19e3_clark_west_horizon_and_hac_policy_declared.py`, `test_gv19e3_pit_transform_declared.py`, `test_gv19e3_berkowitz_lag_and_tail_mode_declared.py`, `test_gv19e3_dynamic_quantile_regressor_set_declared.py`

### GV-19F1 — VaR exception coverage, independence, and traffic-light backtesting family
- **Domain:** governance, validation, market-risk control, and owner-visible model-quality diagnostics
- **Purpose:** Preserve one canonical institutional backtesting family so QTT does not stop at CVaR / expected-shortfall estimation, drawdown ratios, or raw realized P&L when a materially used market-risk sleeve still needs explicit coverage, exception-clustering, and traffic-light diagnostics on the declared VaR basis.
- **Families included once here:** `VAR_HIT_SEQUENCE`, `KUPIEC_POF_UNCONDITIONAL_COVERAGE`, `CHRISTOFFERSEN_INDEPENDENCE`, `CHRISTOFFERSEN_CONDITIONAL_COVERAGE`, `BASEL_TRAFFIC_LIGHT_EXCEPTION_ZONE`
- **Formula / operating law:** define the hit indicator on the declared loss basis as `I_t(alpha) = 1` when realized loss exceeds the declared one-day or horizon-matched `VaR_t(alpha)` and `0` otherwise; let `x = Sum_t I_t(alpha)` and `p_hat = x / T`; the Kupiec / proportion-of-failures statistic is `LR_uc = -2 * ln(((1 - alpha)^(T - x) * alpha^x) / ((1 - p_hat)^(T - x) * p_hat^x))`; with first-order transition counts `N00, N01, N10, N11`, define `pi01 = N01 / (N00 + N01)` and `pi11 = N11 / (N10 + N11)` on the declared zero-denominator fallback policy, and define the Christoffersen independence statistic `LR_ind = -2 * ln((((1 - p_hat)^(N00 + N10) * p_hat^(N01 + N11))) / (((1 - pi01)^N00 * pi01^N01 * (1 - pi11)^N10 * pi11^N11)))`; the conditional-coverage statistic is `LR_cc = LR_uc + LR_ind`; when the declared traffic-light benchmark basis is active, use a rolling 250-observation window on the 99% VaR basis with zone map `{GREEN: 0..4 exceptions, YELLOW: 5..9 exceptions, RED: >=10 exceptions}`.
- **Inputs:** declared VaR forecast series, realized P&L or loss series on a matched sign convention, horizon basis, confidence level `alpha`, hit sequence, transition counts, rolling-window length, benchmark traffic-light basis, and strongest simpler realized-loss comparator
- **Outputs / basis:** hit-sequence packet, exception-count receipt, Kupiec `LR_uc` packet, Christoffersen `LR_ind` packet, Christoffersen `LR_cc` packet, exception-clustering alert, traffic-light zone receipt, and comparator delta versus plain realized-loss and CVaR monitor packets
- **Public default:** advisory and shadow / research governance only; no sleeve may auto-promote or auto-demote solely on one VaR exception test without the broader replay / shadow / economic evidence already required elsewhere
- **Seed authority route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed):** one-day 99% VaR hit-sequence basis for institutional-style backtesting, rolling window `T = 250`, traffic-light zone mapping `{GREEN <= 4, YELLOW 5..9, RED >= 10}`, unconditional-coverage plus independence both preserved, and conditional-coverage shown whenever the transition counts are valid; owner-facing daily and quarterly reviews may render the same rolling window on the same declared loss basis
- **Bounded search range:** `alpha ∈ {0.01, 0.025, 0.05}` with `0.01` as the Day-1 institutional-style default; rolling window `{125, 250, 500}` with `250` as Day-1 default; hit basis `{LOSS_EXCEEDS_VAR, NEGATIVE_PNL_BELOW_NEG_VAR}` with one explicit sign convention only; zero-denominator fallback policy `{QUARANTINE_TEST, ADD_EPSILON_WITH_DIAGNOSTIC_RECEIPT}`; transition-memory order fixed to `{FIRST_ORDER_MARKOV_ONLY}` for Day-1
- **Runtime resolution:** batch_evaluation_only for backtest and promotion-sensitive governance; owner-visible rolling diagnostics allowed in live observability, but never as a hidden autonomous authority surface
- **Fallback behavior:** if the VaR sign convention, hit basis, horizon basis, rolling window, or transition-count policy is ambiguous, QTT must quarantine the family as advisory-only and fall back to the strongest approved realized-loss / CVaR / drawdown diagnostics with a `VAR_BACKTEST_FALLBACK_RECEIPT` rather than guessing a backtest basis
- **Validation hooks:** `test_var_hit_sequence_basis_declared.py`, `test_kupiec_pof_formula_basis_declared.py`, `test_christoffersen_transition_count_policy_declared.py`, `test_traffic_light_zone_map_declared.py`, `test_var_backtest_fallback_receipt_required_when_basis_ambiguous.py`

Hard rules:
- no materially used VaR family may publish exception counts without an explicit hit-basis and loss-sign convention;
- unconditional coverage and independence may not be silently conflated; if both are shown, `LR_uc`, `LR_ind`, and `LR_cc` must remain separately reconstructible;
- the traffic-light map is a benchmark-style owner diagnostic, not a standalone live-authority switch;
- if transition counts are too thin or degenerate, QTT may still show unconditional coverage and the traffic-light zone, but it must mark independence / conditional-coverage diagnostics as low-confidence or advisory only rather than guessing stability;
- no sleeve may advertise market-risk control as institution-style complete unless the declared VaR exception family is either explicitly inapplicable or explicitly packetized.

### GV-19F2 — Expected-shortfall backtesting and spectral-tail coverage family
- **Domain:** governance, validation, market-risk control, and owner-visible model-quality diagnostics
- **Purpose:** Preserve one canonical expected-shortfall backtesting family so QTT does not stop at ES / CVaR estimation when a materially used market-risk sleeve still needs explicit tail-model validation on the same declared loss, horizon, and confidence basis.
- **Families included once here:** `EXPECTED_SHORTFALL_BACKTEST_PANEL`, `ACERBI_SZEKELY_ES_BACKTEST`, `SPECTRAL_RISK_MEASURE_COVERAGE_TEST`, `ES_PLUS_VAR_JOINT_DIAGNOSTIC_PANEL`
- **Formula / operating law:** the active family must evaluate ES forecasts on the same declared loss basis, horizon, and confidence level used by the producing risk engine; Day-1 support includes the model-free Acerbi–Székely ES backtest family and a joint ES-plus-VaR diagnostic panel, with QTT preserving the realized tail-loss sample, the ES forecast series, and the matched VaR series on one aligned evaluation window rather than inferring ES adequacy from VaR exceptions alone.
- **Inputs:** declared ES forecast series, matched realized loss series, matched VaR forecast series when joint diagnostics are active, confidence level, rolling evaluation window, tail-loss sign convention, and strongest simpler VaR / realized-loss comparator
- **Outputs / basis:** `ES_BACKTEST_PANEL_PACKET`, `ACERBI_SZEKELY_TEST_RECEIPT`, `ES_PLUS_VAR_JOINT_DIAGNOSTIC_RECEIPT`, `TAIL_MODEL_FAILURE_ALERT`, and comparator delta versus the existing VaR-backtesting family
- **Public default:** advisory and shadow / research governance only; no sleeve may auto-promote or auto-demote solely on one ES backtest without the broader replay / shadow / economic evidence already required elsewhere
- **Seed authority route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed):** one-day or horizon-matched 97.5% ES basis on the declared loss convention for market-risk sleeves that already preserve ES; rolling window `T = 250`; joint display with the existing VaR traffic-light and exception family whenever the same sleeve also preserves a matched VaR forecast basis
- **Bounded search range:** `alpha_es_bt ∈ {0.025,0.01}` with `0.025` as the Day-1 institutional-style default for ES; rolling window `{125,250,500}` with `250` as Day-1 default; ES backtest family `{ACERBI_SZEKELY_MODEL_FREE, STRONGER_DECLARED_PUBLIC_EQUIVALENT}`; joint-panel mode `{ES_ONLY, ES_PLUS_MATCHED_VAR}`
- **Runtime resolution:** batch_evaluation_only for backtest and promotion-sensitive governance; owner-visible rolling diagnostics allowed in live observability, but never as a hidden autonomous authority surface
- **Fallback behavior:** if the ES sign convention, confidence basis, rolling window, or matched realized-loss basis is ambiguous, QTT must quarantine the family as advisory-only and fall back to the strongest approved VaR / realized-loss / CVaR monitor packet with an `ES_BACKTEST_FALLBACK_RECEIPT` rather than guessing a tail-validation basis
- **Validation hooks:** `test_es_backtest_basis_declared.py`, `test_acerbi_szekely_receipt_required.py`, `test_es_plus_var_joint_panel_basis_aligned.py`, `test_es_backtest_fallback_receipt_required_when_basis_ambiguous.py`

Hard rules:
- no materially used ES family may claim institution-style completeness while preserving estimation but omitting tail-model validation;
- ES backtesting may not silently change sign convention, horizon, or confidence level relative to the producing ES engine;
- when the same sleeve preserves both ES and VaR, QTT must be able to render a joint ES-plus-VaR diagnostic panel on the same matched evaluation basis rather than leaving the relationship implicit;
- ES backtesting is owner-visible risk validation, not a standalone live-authority switch.

### GV-19F2B — Joint VaR-plus-ES strictly-consistent comparative-scoring family
- **Domain:** governance, validation, market-risk control, and owner-visible comparative model-quality diagnostics
- **Purpose:** Preserve one canonical family for strictly consistent joint VaR-and-ES comparative scoring so QTT does not stop at separate VaR exception counts, separate ES backtests, or generic proper-scoring surfaces when a materially used tail-risk sleeve needs one declared matched-pair score for model comparison, replay ranking, and triggered live-concurrent shadow-comparison promotion review.
- **Families included once here:** `JOINT_VAR_ES_STRICTLY_CONSISTENT_SCORE_PACKET`, `FZ_PATTON_JOINT_VAR_ES_SCORE`, `JOINT_VAR_ES_DM_COMPARATOR_PACKET`, `JOINT_VAR_ES_SCORE_AGGREGATION_RECEIPT`
- **Formula / operating law:** on the declared matched horizon and matched sign basis, Day-1 support includes the Patton parameterization of the Fissler-Ziegel class for a realized return or P&L observation `y_t`, matched VaR forecast `v_t`, matched ES forecast `e_t`, and tail probability `alpha`, written on the negative-tail convention as `L_t = (1 / (alpha * e_t)) * 1{y_t <= v_t} * (y_t - v_t) + v_t / e_t + log(-e_t) - 1`; when the producing sleeve stores losses as positive-right-tail quantities instead, QTT must apply the declared internal sign-normalization profile before computing the score rather than silently mixing return-space and loss-space conventions.
- **Inputs:** matched VaR forecast series, matched ES forecast series, realized return / P&L or loss series on a declared sign convention, tail probability `alpha`, matched horizon basis, sign-normalization profile, score family, aggregation window, score aggregation basis, strongest simpler comparator, and comparator mode when the score differential is tested formally
- **Outputs / basis:** `JOINT_VAR_ES_SCORE_PACKET`, `JOINT_VAR_ES_MEAN_SCORE_RECEIPT`, `JOINT_VAR_ES_DM_COMPARATOR_PACKET`, `JOINT_VAR_ES_SIGN_NORMALIZATION_RECEIPT`, and comparator delta versus the existing VaR exception and ES backtesting families
- **Public default:** advisory and shadow / research governance only; no sleeve may auto-promote or auto-demote solely on a joint VaR-plus-ES score without the broader replay / shadow / economic evidence already required elsewhere
- **Seed authority route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed):** one-day or horizon-matched `alpha = 0.025` joint VaR-plus-ES basis for materially used market-risk sleeves that already preserve matched VaR and ES forecasts; Patton/FZ Day-1 score form on the declared matched sign basis; rolling evaluation window `T = 250`; mean score aggregation on the declared window; Diebold-Mariano with Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction on the score differential when pairwise comparison between two joint VaR-plus-ES forecast packets is required
- **Bounded search range:** `alpha_var_es_joint ∈ {0.025,0.01}` with `0.025` as the Day-1 institutional-style default; score family `{FZ0_PATTON_PARAMETRIZATION, STRICTLY_CONSISTENT_DECLARED_PUBLIC_EQUIVALENT}`; sign-normalization profile `{RETURN_SPACE_LEFT_TAIL_WITH_VAR_AND_ES_NEGATIVE, LOSS_SPACE_RIGHT_TAIL_WITH_INTERNAL_NEGATIVE_ES_NORMALIZATION}`; rolling window `{125,250,500}` with `250` as Day-1 default; score aggregation basis `{MEAN_SCORE_PER_WINDOW,SUM_SCORE_PER_WINDOW,ROLLING_MEAN_SCORE}`; comparator mode `{AVERAGE_SCORE_ONLY,DM_HLN_ON_SCORE_DIFFERENTIAL,BOTH}` with `DM_HLN_ON_SCORE_DIFFERENTIAL` as Day-1 comparator default when two forecast packets are compared; HAC lag policy `{H_MINUS_1,SQRT_T,DECLARED_EXPLICIT_LAG}`
- **Runtime resolution:** batch_evaluation_only for replay, walk-forward, shadow, and promotion-sensitive governance; owner-visible rolling diagnostics allowed in live observability, but never as a hidden autonomous authority surface
- **Fallback behavior:** if the matched VaR series, matched ES series, sign-normalization profile, tail probability, horizon basis, or comparator mode is ambiguous, QTT must quarantine the family as advisory-only and fall back to the strongest already-declared ES backtesting and VaR backtesting packets with a `JOINT_VAR_ES_SCORE_FALLBACK_RECEIPT` rather than guessing a score basis
- **Validation hooks:** `test_joint_var_es_score_requires_matched_var_and_es.py`, `test_fz_patton_score_formula_basis_declared.py`, `test_joint_var_es_sign_normalization_declared.py`, `test_joint_var_es_dm_comparator_mode_declared.py`, `test_joint_var_es_score_fallback_receipt_required_when_basis_ambiguous.py`

Hard rules:
- no materially used sleeve may claim joint VaR-and-ES comparative superiority unless the VaR forecast series and ES forecast series are matched by horizon, timestamp, and sign convention;
- no score consumer may silently mix return-space negative-tail forecasts with loss-space positive-tail realizations; the sign-normalization profile must remain explicit and reconstructible;
- the joint VaR-plus-ES score is a comparative-scoring and ranking surface, not a replacement for VaR exception coverage, ES backtesting, profitability evidence, or owner-gate law;
- when `DM_HLN_ON_SCORE_DIFFERENTIAL` is active, the same declared HAC lag policy and horizon basis must apply to the score-difference series rather than being inferred package-locally;
- no sleeve may advertise institution-style tail-model comparison as complete if it preserves separate VaR and ES forecast packets but leaves the joint strictly-consistent score implicit.
