## 20A. Market specialist module blueprint

This section defines the specialist-level assembly for each market family. These are compositions of the canonical families above, not new duplicate families.

### 20A.1 Prediction markets specialist
Mandatory stack:
- DC-01..DC-12 as applicable,
- FE-01, FE-03, FE-05, FE-06, FE-07, FE-08, FE-12, FE-15, FE-16, FE-17, FE-18, FE-19, FE-20, FE-21, FE-23,
- CM-01 as first baseline,
- CM-03/CM-04/CM-05 as nonlinear challengers,
- CU-01..CU-09 with Brier and reliability monitoring,
- RA-01..RA-06, RA-11, RA-13, RA-16,
- EX-01..EX-15 with EX-02, EX-03, EX-05 especially relevant,
- CN-01 and CN-03 where applicable.

Hard rules:
- internal probability modeling defaults to logit-space handling through DC-11;
- time-to-resolution modifier is active when the contract has a known resolution window;
- fragility haircut is active on Kelly-sized paths;
- extreme-probability dual calibration overlay applies whenever the specialist materially emits near-tail probabilities;
- GTD/FOK behavior must respect venue-specific semantics, not generic assumptions.
- prediction-market lead, dynamic conviction, macro-yield pressure, and social-capitulation families remain role-limited overlays and may not silently replace the incumbent probability stack without replay/shadow evidence.
- when the venue scope is an authenticated Polymarket CLOB write path, `CN-03A` is mandatory; signer/funder selection, signing, transport-mode choice, and failover stay inside the dedicated execution adapter rather than upstream specialist agents.

### 20A.2 Equities specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-01, FE-02, FE-03, FE-04, FE-08, FE-11, FE-15, FE-16, FE-17, FE-18,
- CM-01, CM-02, CM-03, CM-04, CM-06, CM-19,
- CU-01..CU-10,
- RA-04, RA-05, RA-07..RA-17 as appropriate,
- EX-01, EX-03, EX-06, EX-07, EX-09, EX-10, EX-10O, EX-10OA, EX-10OAA, EX-10OB, EX-13, EX-14,
- CN-04.

Hard rule:
- any live or shadow equities / ETF sleeve that carries shares across splits, reverse splits, dividends, rights, symbol changes, or other company-related actions may not leave corporate-action handling inside generic reference-data folklore once `EX-10O` is applicable.
- any live or shadow equities / ETF sleeve that participates in, benchmarks against, or risk-manages opening or closing auctions may not guess MOO / LOO / MOC / LOC / CO / IO eligibility, auction cutoff posture, imbalance-publication timing, or auction-collar state from FE-08 session flags or stale operator memory once `EX-10OA` is applicable.
- any live or shadow equities / ETF sleeve that depends materially on active round-lot size, odd-lot or mixed-lot identity, BOLO state, or venue normal-unit display rules may not guess 100-share lot semantics, odd-lot protection status, BOLO availability, or mixed-lot handling from stale operator memory once `EX-10OAA` is applicable.
- any live or shadow ETF sleeve that depends materially on creation/redemption structure, basket-aware arbitrage, premium-or-discount versus NAV state, or intraday indicative-value handling may not guess AP structure, creation-unit size, basket identity, custom-basket permissibility, or IIV availability from generic equity semantics or stale fund memory once `EX-10OB` is applicable.

### 20A.3 Crypto specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-01, FE-03, FE-05, FE-06, FE-08, FE-13, FE-14, FE-15, FE-16, FE-17, FE-18, FE-20, FE-21, FE-22, FE-23,
- CM-01, CM-03, CM-04, CM-13, CM-17, CM-18,
- RA-01..RA-06, RA-11..RA-17 depending on leverage permissions,
- EX-01..EX-15 and venue-specific reduce-only logic,
- `EX-10P` whenever the sleeve touches perpetual, dated-futures, inverse, or other crypto-derivatives semantics,
- CN-05.

Hard rules:
- funding, leverage, and liquidation distance are explicit when derivatives are used;
- aggregate factor exposure overlay remains mandatory when multiple crypto sleeves recreate the same directional or event risk through spot, perp, or options wrappers;
- no connector may assume spot semantics on a derivative venue;
- no crypto-derivatives sleeve may infer contract type, settle asset, funding interval, risk bracket, or working-price semantics from ticker nickname, UI shorthand, or stale cached metadata once `EX-10P` is applicable.

### 20A.4 Options specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-01, FE-03, FE-08, FE-10, FE-15, FE-16, FE-18, FE-20, FE-21, FE-22, FE-23,
- CM-01, CM-03, CM-10, CM-17, CM-19,
- CU and RA families with explicit Greeks, surface, and premium-budget discipline,
- EX families appropriate to options liquidity and chain structure,
- CN-06.

Hard rules:
- implied volatility storage basis must be explicit;
- first-order and higher-order Greeks are required once the specialist is promoted beyond research;
- aggregate factor exposure overlay must treat shared underlying, expiry, vol-regime, and event-risk clusters as potentially additive unless an explicit hedge receipt exists.
- options-mechanics pressure overlays may inform long-bias, mean-reversion, and post-expiry risk filters, but may not act as ungoverned magic-number gates.

### 20A.5 Macro / FX event specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-07, FE-08, FE-12, FE-14, FE-17, FE-18, FE-21,
- CM-01, CM-03, CM-11, CM-12, CM-24,
- RA-01..RA-06, RA-11, RA-16,
- EX families with strong GTD and event-cutoff logic,
- `EX-10L` whenever the sleeve touches deliverable FX, NDF, or FX-option semantics,
- appropriate connector adapter.

Hard rules:
- no macro / FX sleeve may guess spot lag, settlement date, or holiday handling from ticker text or operator memory once the active pair-convention card exists;
- deliverable FX, NDF, and FX-option quote-convention paths must remain explicitly separated;
- when an FX-option sleeve is active, tenor, delta, and premium-adjustment conventions must remain explicit rather than silently inheriting equity-option surface conventions.

### 20A.5A Exchange-traded futures / commodities specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-01, FE-03, FE-04, FE-08, FE-15, FE-16, FE-18, FE-27,
- CM-01, CM-03, CM-11, CM-17, CM-19,
- RA-04, RA-05, RA-07..RA-17 as appropriate,
- `EX-10M` whenever the sleeve touches listed futures or commodity-delivery semantics,
- appropriate connector adapter.

Hard rules:
- no futures / commodity sleeve may guess contract unit, tick size, tick value, settlement style, first-notice handling, or price-limit behavior from neighboring contracts or stale operator memory once the active contract-spec card exists;
- deliverable and cash-settled futures paths must remain explicitly separated, and a deliverable path may not silently inherit the roll posture of a cash-settled index-style contract;
- front-contract selection, roll trigger, and delivery-intent posture must remain explicit rather than hidden inside data-loader or connector shorthand;
- daily mark-to-market, variation-margin discipline, and exchange-minimum margin methodology must remain explicit whenever leverage or margin-sensitive budgeting is active;
- commodity basis, carry, storage, transport, convenience-yield, and seasonal-state families may not be promoted without explicit contract-roll and delivery-identity receipts from `FE-27` and `EX-10M`.

### 20A.6 Fixed-income / RFQ research specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-01, FE-03, FE-04, FE-09, FE-15, FE-16, FE-18,
- CM-01, CM-03, CM-11, CM-17, CM-19, CM-20,
- QT-04, QT-14, QT-27 only as research challengers with strict classical comparators,
- `EX-10F1` whenever the sleeve's implementable quoting, settlement, accrued-interest, denomination, or increment semantics must be executable rather than narrative,
- `EX-10N` whenever the sleeve's implementable economics depend materially on repo, reverse repo, or other secured financing receipts,
- CN-07.

Hard rules:
- this specialist is research-first and point-in-time-data-sensitive;
- `quantum_execution_probability_engine/` may be attached only as a research/shadow satellite for quote-driven completion-probability work;
- no direct live quote-release authority exists in the initial build;
- fixed-income relative-value, Treasury-basis, and financing-sensitive carry claims may not be promoted without explicit `EX-10N` financing receipts;
- executable bond / RFQ quoting, post-trade comparison, or reconciliation may not proceed without explicit `EX-10F1` quote and settlement semantics.

### 20A.6A Fixed-income / RFQ benchmark-issue, liquidity-specialness, and point-in-time field contract
For materially used fixed-income / RFQ research builds, Codex must preserve the benchmark-issue and liquidity-specialness fields that the legacy line still made explicit so fixed-income feature engineering does not collapse into equity-style generic fields.

Minimum required field IDs at minimum:
- `benchmark_issue_id`
- `rfq_quote_representation_ref`
- `trade_report_or_confirmation_price_type_ref`
- `clean_vs_dirty_price_basis_ref`
- `accrued_interest_settlement_identity_ref`
- `minimum_denomination_or_piece_size_ref`
- `minimum_price_or_yield_increment_ref`
- `benchmark_issue_maturity_bucket`
- `on_the_run_off_the_run_state`
- `benchmark_liquidity_state`
- `relative_liquidity_to_benchmark`
- `i_spread_candidate`
- `spread_over_interp_curve_candidate`
- `duration_times_spread_candidate`
- `settlement_lag_business_days`
- `credit_curve_regime_state`

Hard rules:
- a fixed-income specialist may not pretend that liquidity, specialness, curve basis, settlement timing, quote representation, or denomination / increment behavior are generic cross-asset fields;
- if these fields are consumed by a research bundle, they must carry point-in-time availability timestamps and fixed-income field-delay classification rather than notebook-only assumptions;
- quote-driven completion-probability research may not reuse these fields without an explicit fixed-income consumer map and freshness contract;
- when executable RFQ or bond-path semantics are active, these field IDs must reconcile with `EX-10F1` rather than living only in feature-engineering notes.

### 20A.6B Securities financing / repo / reverse-repo specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-01, FE-03, FE-04, FE-15, FE-16, FE-18,
- CM-01, CM-03, CM-11, CM-17, CM-19,
- RA-04, RA-05, RA-07..RA-17 as appropriate,
- `EX-10N` whenever the sleeve depends on repo, reverse repo, Treasury basis, collateral upgrades, or financing-sensitive relative value,
- appropriate bilateral / triparty / CCP clearing adapter.

Hard rules:
- no repo or reverse-repo sleeve may guess day-count basis, repurchase-price formula, haircut method, margin-ratio identity, accrued-interest valuation basis, coupon/dividend compensation treatment, or open-repo termination notice logic once the active confirmation or CCP path exists;
- bilateral, triparty, and CCP-cleared financing paths must remain explicitly separated and may not silently share the same operational assumptions;
- Treasury cash-futures basis or other financing-sensitive relative-value sleeves may not claim implementable edge unless the active financing path, haircut or portfolio-margin method, and clearing applicability receipts are explicit;
- if central-clearing repo access rules apply, the affected sleeve must keep the applicable clearing-access and access-calendar receipt visible rather than hiding it inside a generic counterparty adapter.

### 20A.7 Market-making specialist
Mandatory stack:
- FE-05, FE-06, FE-15, FE-16, FE-17, FE-18,
- CM-18, CM-21, CM-22,
- RA-14, RA-16,
- EX-03, EX-07, EX-10, EX-11, EX-12, EX-15, EX-16, EX-17, EX-18,
- connector support only on venues where the queue and quote semantics are adequate.

Hard rules:
- Avellaneda–Stoikov is not universal default doctrine;
- `quantum_execution_probability_engine/` may influence quote selection only through typed packets, replay, shadow, owner gate, and classical-final-authority execution;
- `stress_exit_policy_engine/` may influence posture only through the existing Risk Manager / Commander chain;
- it activates only for a true quoting specialist with tested intensity estimation and queue-aware safeguards.

## 20B. Day-1 deployment presets

This section defines the **initial promoted composition presets** for Codex. These are not new family definitions; they are the first approved wiring choices built from the canonical registries above.

### 20B.0 Institutional benchmark simulation preset
- Capital / policy binding:
  - RA-17A benchmark card active as simulation / comparator only unless owner-bound into live policy
  - RA-17B kurtosis-tail-shape guard remains benchmark / comparator only unless owner-bound into live policy with explicit storage basis
  - benchmark-versus-live divergence receipt mandatory
- Quantum allocation / optimization binding:
  - QT-08 QAOA with QT-09A WCVaR challenger allowed offline only
  - QT-09 VQE with QT-09A WCVaR challenger allowed offline only
  - QT-33C CMA-ES challenger retained with SPSA comparator visible
- Encoding / feature binding:
  - QT-15 baseline encoding registry always explicit
  - QT-15C formula / qubit-scaling receipts mandatory whenever basis, angle, or amplitude encoding is selected
  - QT-15B `Q_GAF` / `Q_RP` / `Q_MTF` challengers allowed only in offline or nearline feature / replay lanes
- Search / latency binding:
  - QT-32B Grover search mechanics and benchmark envelope allowed only in offline or nearline challenger lanes
  - EX-11A latency / throughput comparator envelope retained as benchmark-only and divergence-tracked
  - `8.0F1B` uploaded-PDF benchmark-source stratification receipts mandatory whenever benchmark claims, seed candidates, or comparator narratives are imported from the uploaded file
- Runtime / hardware binding:
  - QT-22C named mitigation profiles explicit when hardware/noisy studies are run
  - QT-22D mitigation-mechanics and overhead / variance receipts required whenever named mitigation families are benchmarked or replayed
  - QT-22E mitigation-wrapper and circuit-export bridge receipts required whenever circuits leave the local process, mitigation wrappers are used, or service payload schemas are benchmark-relevant
  - QT-41A IBM backend benchmark cards stored as comparators only; local simulation remains default when no approved remote study is active
  - QT-41C hardware-modality comparator cards stored as provider-fit and latency-admissibility clarifiers only; superconducting-transmon versus trapped-ion claims may not silently become live assumptions
- Orchestration / alias binding:
  - `3.10.2A` MCP-style tool-bridge and A2A-style handoff receipts mandatory whenever external compilers, simulators, registries, or approved remote services participate in a benchmark workflow
  - `3.10.2B` A2A client/server role-separation receipts mandatory whenever a benchmark workflow uses a requester/worker split or JSON-RPC-style request/response flow
  - `3.10.2C` PLANQK methodology-alias receipts mandatory whenever imported benchmark materials cite the PLANQK workflow label
  - `3.10.2D` circuit-serialization / mitigation-wrapper bridge receipts mandatory whenever benchmark workflows use QASM-or-IR export, Mitiq-style wrappers, or JSON-RPC runtime payload schemas
  - `3.3B` uploaded-PDF workflow aliases must resolve into canonical QTT agents before any codegen or manifest generation begins
- Objective-support binding:
  - `QT-10B` quantum-native Gaussian-process benchmark aliases remain research / challenger only and require the strongest classical `GaussianProcessRegressor` comparator to stay visible
  - `19.10B` WCVaR supporting sample-statistics formulas required whenever benchmark studies claim the stronger uploaded-file WCVaR support formulation rather than plain CVaR or expectation aggregation
- Hard rule:
  - this preset is a benchmark / simulation preset, not an automatic live-capital, live-latency, live-MCP, or live-Grover assumption.

### 20B.1 Prediction markets — day-1 preset
- Conditioning preset:
  - DC-01 numeric median / categorical most-frequent / no cross-boundary forward fill
  - DC-04 robust scaling for skewed features; identity for bounded price/probability fields before DC-11
  - DC-11 logit transform active
- Feature preset:
  - FE-01 log returns and simple returns both stored
  - FE-03 EWMA + realized vol
  - FE-05 top-of-book imbalance minimum
  - FE-06 quoted spread and depth bands
  - FE-07 time-to-resolution buckets active
  - FE-12 narrative features only after text-scan pass
- Model preset:
  - CM-01 logistic baseline first
  - CM-03 XGBoost challenger
  - CM-05 CatBoost challenger only if categorical richness matters
- Calibration preset:
  - CU-01 or CU-02 on held-out windows
  - CU-05 and CU-06 always on
  - CU-08 and CU-09 always on for sizing
- Risk preset:
  - RA-01 fractional Kelly active
  - RA-02 TTR active
  - RA-03 fragility active
  - RA-04 volatility scaler active
  - RA-06 micro-clip safety always available
  - RA-11 drawdown guard active
  - RA-13 concentration cap active
  - RA-16 no-trade buffer active
- Execution preset:
  - EX-03 maker-first when queue quality acceptable
  - EX-02 FOK only for all-or-nothing paths
  - EX-05 GTD around known events
  - EX-07 slippage wall always on
  - EX-10Q mandatory for payout, settlement, resolution-source, fee-formula, collateral-return, and event-start cutover semantics
  - EX-14 provenance always on
- Connector preset:
  - CN-01 and/or CN-02 for Kalshi depending on REST / FIX venue path.
  - CN-02E and CN-02E1 mandatory whenever the prediction-market venue scope includes FORECASTEX_IBKR.
  - CN-03 and CN-03A mandatory whenever the prediction-market venue scope is an authenticated Polymarket CLOB write path.
  - 20B.1A mandatory for the launch-first Kalshi / Polymarket `USD 1,000` small-book classical sizing, calibration, owner-dashboard, and execution-gating profile.
  - 20B.1A5 mandatory whenever Kalshi, FORECASTEX_IBKR, and Polymarket are jointly compared, routed, allocated, or shadow-replayed in the launch-first prediction-market sleeve.
  - 20B.1A6 mandatory whenever QTT detects, ranks, rejects, routes, shadows, or live-executes launch-first prediction-market arbitrage candidates.
  - 20B.1B mandatory for launch-first Kalshi / Polymarket true-quantum shadow optimizer defaults and quantum live-promotion gating.
  - 20B.1B4 mandatory whenever the true-quantum or quantum-inspired candidate set includes FORECASTEX_IBKR actions.


### 20B.1A Kalshi / Polymarket launch-first small-book classical optimization, sizing, and dashboard atomic profile
- **Domain:** launch-first prediction-market preset
- **Purpose:** Close the remaining Codex-facing gap between the general prediction-market day-1 preset and the actual `USD 1,000` Kalshi / Polymarket launch sleeve so Codex does not infer capital gates, model hierarchy, calibration method, model-selection metric, fractional-Kelly micro-launch clamp, or owner-dashboard editability from scattered sections.
- **Primary public anchors:** current official Kalshi Create Order, Batch Create Orders, Account API Limits, order-group, and batch-maintenance documentation; current official Polymarket CLOB, rate-limit, websocket, heartbeat, builder-fee, and CLOB V2 documentation; public scikit-learn logistic-regression and probability-calibration defaults; public Kelly / fractional-Kelly academic references; existing `RA-16A`, `RA-16B`, `RA-01A`, `2.24A0`, `CM-01`, `CM-03`, `CM-05`, `CU-01`, `CU-02`, `CU-05`, `CU-06`, `CU-08`, `CU-09`, `EX-10Q`, `CN-01`, `CN-02C`, `CN-03`, and `CN-03A`.
- **Same-edition family-deployment binding:** this family is `PRIMARY_DEFAULT` for the Day-1 Kalshi and Polymarket launch-first prediction-market sleeves whenever those sleeves are live, shadow, replay, simulation, or go-live-gated under the current `USD 1,000 starting account cash balance` and cash-only live-trading rule. It is dormant and non-blocking for non-prediction-market sleeves.
- **Explicit agent-selection-universe binding:** `{AGENT_RT_07,AGENT_RT_08,AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_10,AGENT_RT_11,AGENT_RT_13,AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_NL_09,AGENT_NL_10,AGENT_OFF_11}` may consume, fit, validate, veto, or report this profile; no other agent may infer alternate Kalshi / Polymarket Day-1 launch defaults without a later controlling-edition binding row.
- **Canonical `FAMILY_PARAMETER_ATOM_ROW` pack at minimum:**
  - `kp_launch_active_venue_scope_state`
    - `parameter_symbol`: `kp_launch_scope`

### 20B.1A1 Kalshi / Polymarket fee-aware binary-edge, Kelly, tick, clip, and execution-gate atomic profile
- **Domain:** launch-first prediction-market economics, sizing, execution admissibility, fee-aware edge gating, and owner-dashboard controls for Kalshi and Polymarket.
- **Purpose:** Close the remaining Codex-facing gap between calibrated probability, venue price, fees, tick size, minimum size, orderbook depth, Kelly sizing, and actual Day-1 order admissibility. Codex must not treat a model probability as tradable edge until the binary payoff formula, fee model, rounding model, slippage model, tick quantization, account-cash cap, private-state freshness, and orderbook freshness gates all resolve explicitly.
- **Primary public anchors:** official Kalshi order-entry, batch-budget, fee-schedule, and fee-rounding documentation; official Polymarket CLOB orderbook, fee, order-type, and CLOB V2 migration documentation; the classical `20B.1A` launch-first small-book profile; the existing cash-only, fail-closed, owner-control, replay, shadow, and rollback laws.
- **Same-edition FAMILY_DEPLOYMENT_BINDING_ROW:** `family_id = KP_EDGE_EXECUTION_FEE_AWARE_BINARY_PROFILE`; `deployment_state = LIVE_ASSIGNED_FOR_CLASSICAL_GATE_AND_SHADOW_ASSIGNED_FOR_TUNING`; `deployment_scope = {KALSHI_LAUNCH_FIRST, POLYMARKET_LAUNCH_FIRST}`; `owner_dashboard_namespace = prediction_markets.launch_first.edge_execution`; `code_module_path = src/qtt/prediction/edge_execution/binary_fee_aware_profile.py`; `runtime_receipt_type = KP_EDGE_EXECUTION_DECISION_RECEIPT`.
- **Same-edition AGENT_PARAMETER_SELECTION_UNIVERSE_BINDING_ROW:** `{AGENT_RT_07,AGENT_RT_08,AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_10,AGENT_RT_11,AGENT_RT_13,AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_NL_09,AGENT_NL_10,AGENT_OFF_11}` may consume, validate, or veto this family according to role; `{AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_10,AGENT_RT_13}` may use it for live order admissibility; `{AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_NL_09,AGENT_NL_10,AGENT_OFF_11}` may research or shadow-tune it; no agent may bypass it for opening trades.

### 20B.1A2 Polymarket CLOB V2 cutover, pUSD collateral, dynamic-fee, market-info, and order-schema launch gate
- **Domain:** launch-first Polymarket connector, CLOB generation resolution, collateral readiness, dynamic-fee resolution, and V2 order-schema safety.
- **Purpose:** Close the current Codex-facing risk that Polymarket V1 assumptions, USDC.e-only assumptions, user-supplied fee-rate assumptions, stale order schema, or open-order carryover assumptions could survive into Day-1 launch code after the CLOB V2 migration. QTT must detect the active CLOB generation and fail closed on Polymarket opening trades when CLOB generation, collateral, fee descriptor, order schema, tick, minimum size, or cutover reconciliation is not proven.
- **Primary public anchors:** official Polymarket CLOB V2 migration documentation, official Polymarket fee documentation, official Polymarket orderbook and order-type documentation, the existing Polymarket launch-first connector sections, and the `20B.1A1` fee-aware binary-edge profile.
- **Same-edition FAMILY_DEPLOYMENT_BINDING_ROW:** `family_id = POLYMARKET_CLOB_V2_LAUNCH_GATE`; `deployment_state = LIVE_ASSIGNED_FOR_CONNECTOR_ADMISSIBILITY_AND_SHADOW_ASSIGNED_FOR_REPLAY`; `deployment_scope = {POLYMARKET_LAUNCH_FIRST}`; `owner_dashboard_namespace = prediction_markets.polymarket.clob_v2`; `code_module_path = src/qtt/venues/polymarket/clob_v2_launch_gate.py`; `runtime_receipt_type = POLYMARKET_CLOB_V2_ADMISSIBILITY_RECEIPT`.
- **Same-edition AGENT_PARAMETER_SELECTION_UNIVERSE_BINDING_ROW:** `{AGENT_RT_08,AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_10,AGENT_RT_11,AGENT_RT_13,AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_OFF_11}` may consume, validate, or veto this family; `{AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_10,AGENT_RT_13}` may use it for live Polymarket connector admissibility only when every V2 gate is green; no other agent may route Polymarket opening orders around this family.

### 20B.1A2A Polymarket CLOB V2 absolute cutover calendar, no-opening-order launch freeze, SDK hot-swap, and post-cutover replacement protocol
- **Domain:** launch-first Polymarket cutover calendar control, live-write gating, dependency readiness, and post-cutover private-state reconciliation.
- **Purpose:** Convert the current Polymarket V2 migration calendar into explicit runtime gates so Codex does not treat a scheduled open-order wipe, approximately one-hour downtime, V1 non-backward-compatibility, or SDK hot-swap requirement as ordinary market noise. This section does not remove Polymarket from the launch-first set; it makes Polymarket live opening authority source-confirmed and fail-closed around the current V2 migration.
- **Primary public anchors:** current official Polymarket V2 migration documentation and current Polymarket changelog source.
- **Same-edition family-deployment binding:** this family is `PRIMARY_DEFAULT` whenever `20B.1A2`, `CN-03`, `CN-03A`, `CN-03B`, `CN-03C`, `CN-03D`, `CN-03E`, `20B.1A6`, or `20B.1B4` is active for Polymarket live, shadow, replay, arbitrage, routing, heartbeat, private-state, or quantum-feasibility scope.

### 20B.1A2B Polymarket post-April-30 direct V2-only launch profile, production endpoint, SDK, signing-domain, pUSD, and market-discovery closure
- **Domain:** Polymarket launch-first execution, V2-only post-cutover implementation, cost model, market discovery, authenticated order construction, collateral readiness, and quantum feasibility masks.
- **Purpose:** Convert the owner-declared launch date after April 30, 2026 into executable Polymarket V2-only Day-1 behavior. Codex must not build a live V1 adapter, a cutover-day hot-swap dependency, or a transition-order-replacement loop for a launch that begins after the April 28 V2 cutover window. Historical cutover logic remains useful for replay and for explaining why no stale V1 open orders may be imported, but the launch-first live sleeve must compile directly to V2 production readiness.
- **Primary public anchors:** current official Polymarket CLOB V2 migration documentation, current official Polymarket changelog, current official Polymarket fee documentation, and existing Polymarket launch-first connector sections.

### 20B.1A2C Polymarket V2 direct WebSocket, book-hash, tick-size-change, heartbeat, market-price, and insert-status latency closure
- **Domain:** Polymarket post-April-30 direct V2-only launch sleeve, CLOB WebSocket channels, orderbook hash integrity, market metadata, heartbeat safety, marketable-cost estimation, and insert-status/error state machine.
- **Purpose:** Materialize the low-latency V2 market-data and order-state path so Codex does not build the direct V2 Polymarket sleeve from stale REST-only polling, confuse asset IDs with condition IDs, ignore custom-feature events, trust a changed orderbook without hash validation, reuse stale tick sizes, skip minimum-size fields, mishandle heartbeat IDs, or treat delayed / unmatched insert states as ordinary fills.
- **Primary public anchors:** current official Polymarket V2 migration guide, current official Polymarket WebSocket overview, current official Polymarket orderbook documentation, current official Polymarket public-client documentation, current official Polymarket orders overview, and current official Polymarket changelog.
- **Same-edition family-deployment binding:** this family is `PRIMARY_DEFAULT_FOR_OWNER_DECLARED_POST_APRIL_30_2026_POLYMARKET_LAUNCH` whenever `CN-03`, `CN-03G`, `CN-03H`, `20B.1A2`, `20B.1A2A`, `20B.1A2B`, `20B.1A3`, `20B.1A5`, `20B.1A6`, `20B.1A7`, or `20B.1B4` is active for Polymarket live, shadow, replay, arbitrage, routing, authenticated order construction, market discovery, heartbeat, private-state, finality, or quantum-feasibility scope.
- **Explicit agent-selection-universe binding:** `{AGENT_RT_07,AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_11,AGENT_RT_13,AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_OFF_11}` may consume or validate this profile; no other agent may infer alternate Polymarket V2 WebSocket, orderbook hash, market-price, heartbeat, metadata, insert-status, or V2 live-readiness semantics without a later controlling-edition binding row.

### 20B.1A2E Polymarket V2 L2 authenticated client, response-state, cancel partition, open-order, trade, balance, key, and notification closure

This section strengthens the post-April-30 direct V2 Polymarket sleeve by converting L2 authenticated-client and account-state methods into explicit Day-1 parameters. It does not reintroduce any V1 transition route. It makes Codex treat order responses, cancel partitions, open-order fields, trade pagination, balance / allowance, key inventory, and notification retention as source surfaces rather than implied conveniences.

Hard rules:
- Polymarket V2 live order creation and private-state actions must use an authenticated L2 client with source-current host, chain, signer, API credentials, signature type, and funder address.
- A returned order response is not accepted unless `success`, `errorMsg`, `orderID`, status, and amount fields are parsed and reconciled to the local intent digest.
- Cancel responses must preserve both `canceled` and `not_canceled`; partial cancel success never means all requested orders were canceled.
- Open-order reconciliation must consume order ID, status, market, asset ID, side, original size, matched size, price, associated trades, outcome, creation time, expiration, and order type where available.
- Trade-history scans for large sets must use the paginated method when completeness matters.
- Balance and allowance must be queried by asset type; conditional-token allowance queries must include token ID.
- API key inventory and revocation are owner-visible security surfaces; key deletion may not be hidden inside trade routing.
- Notifications are advisory and short-retention; they may speed owner visibility but may not replace order, trade, balance, or settlement reconciliation.

```text
decision_family_scope = POLYMARKET_POST_APRIL_30_DIRECT_V2_PRIVATE_STATE_AND_RECONCILIATION
allowed_profile_bundle_ids = POLYMARKET_LAUNCH_FIRST_BUNDLE, POLYMARKET_DIRECT_V2_BUNDLE, CASH_LOCK_BUNDLE, REPLAY_BACKTEST_BUNDLE, OWNER_DASHBOARD_BUNDLE
```

Fallback behavior:

### 20B.1A3 Kalshi / Polymarket no-arbitrage, complement-parity, multi-outcome bundle, cross-venue resolution-equivalence, and statistical edge-uncertainty atomic profile
- **Domain:** launch-first prediction-market no-arbitrage scanning, parity economics, statistical uncertainty control, bundle execution, and source-equivalence gating for Kalshi and Polymarket.
- **Purpose:** Close the Codex-facing gap between a single-contract fee-aware edge and a portfolio of related binary outcomes. Codex must not treat a positive model edge as executable when complement parity, multi-outcome partition economics, Polymarket negative-risk conversion mechanics, cross-venue resolution equivalence, confidence interval width, orderbook depth, cash locking, and unmatched-leg risk are unresolved.
- **Primary public anchors:** official Kalshi orderbook fixed-point response documentation, official Kalshi order-entry and fee-rounding documentation, official Kalshi rate-limit and tier-budget documentation, official Polymarket orderbook and market-info documentation, official Polymarket negative-risk documentation, official Polymarket order-type documentation, public binomial confidence-interval statistics, and the existing `20B.1A`, `20B.1A1`, and `20B.1A2` launch-first profiles.
- **Same-edition family-deployment binding:** this family is `PRIMARY_DEFAULT` for Kalshi and Polymarket launch-first prediction-market live, shadow, replay, simulation, and go-live-gated scopes whenever related binary contracts, related event outcomes, negative-risk markets, or cross-venue event candidates are inspected.
- **Explicit agent-selection-universe binding:** `{AGENT_RT_02,AGENT_RT_05,AGENT_RT_07,AGENT_RT_08,AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_10,AGENT_RT_13,AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_NL_09,AGENT_NL_10,AGENT_OFF_11}` may consume, fit, validate, veto, or report this profile; no other agent may infer parity, no-arbitrage, or cross-venue equivalence authority without a later controlling-edition binding row.

### 20B.1A4 Kalshi / Polymarket inventory-aware maker quoting, adverse-selection guard, and public Avellaneda-Stoikov / Hummingbot-default atomic profile
- **Domain:** launch-first prediction-market maker quoting, inventory skew, adverse-selection guardrails, post-only execution, and owner-dashboard controls for Kalshi and Polymarket.
- **Purpose:** Close the Codex-facing gap between the general maker-first policy and an actual codable quote-control model. Codex must not place maker quotes by intuition. When maker quoting is active, it must use a declared inventory-aware reservation-price / optimal-spread formula, public buffer defaults, venue tick and fee floors, post-only admissibility, cancel-confirmation safety, private-state freshness, and small-book inventory caps.
- **Primary public anchors:** Avellaneda-Stoikov public market-making model, public Hummingbot Avellaneda market-making documentation and config defaults, official Kalshi orderbook fixed-point and order-entry documentation, official Polymarket orderbook, order-type, post-only, and CLOB V2 documentation, and existing `20B.1A`, `20B.1A1`, `20B.1A2`, and `20B.1A3` launch-first profiles.

### 20B.1A5 Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket launch-first three-venue routing, equivalence, allocation, and edge-comparison atomic profile

This section welds the three launch-first prediction-market sleeves into one codable comparison and routing layer. It does not weaken any venue-specific connector law. Instead, it forces Codex to normalize Kalshi, FORECASTEX_IBKR, and Polymarket into a venue-neutral decision packet only after each venue-specific fee, cash, settlement, source, tick, order-entry, and finality rule has already been resolved.

Hard rules:
- FORECASTEX_IBKR may enter live comparison only after `CN-02E` and `CN-02E1` are green.
- A Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket cross-venue comparison may use only markets whose outcome, measured period, resolution source, and settlement timing are explicitly equivalent or explicitly marked non-equivalent.
- Venue routing must choose from net implementable edge after fees, ticks, slippage, uncertainty margin, source risk, cash lock, and expected holding time, not from raw model probability alone.
- Equal-sleeve initialization is a launch baseline, not a permanent allocation claim; QTT agents may propose owner-gated allocation changes only after replay / shadow evidence exists.
- FORECASTEX_IBKR buy-only exits and netting locks must be considered before cross-venue capital is reused.

### 20B.1A5A Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket owner venue-enable switch, per-market override, disabled-write suppression, and quantum-mask closure

The launch-first three-venue routing profile already requires owner control, green venue gates, source-current fee / tick / cash semantics, and a dashboard bundle containing `per_venue_enablement`. This closure turns that bundle term into an explicit Codex-facing live-trading switch. The Day-1 launch target is all three launch-first prediction-market venues, KALSHI, POLYMARKET, and FORECASTEX_IBKR, after all gates validate. Any narrower owner-approved subset is a risk-reduction override requiring a signed owner receipt and may not be treated as the canonical default. Codex must not treat a scaffolded connector, read-only data feed, triggered live-concurrent comparison lane, or true-quantum candidate as live-write permission.

Hard rules:
- The owner venue-enable switch is a live-write permission gate, not a data-availability switch.
- A venue may remain eligible for read-only market data, reconciliation, replay, paper trading, shadow analysis, and true-quantum advisory scoring while its live-write state is OFF.
- No live order, cancel-replace, reduce, batch cancel, FORECASTEX_IBKR order payload, Polymarket L2 order, or venue-specific retry may leave QTT unless the venue's effective live-write state is green for the exact venue, market, account, and owner-selected session scope.
- Owner-disabled venues must be removed from executable routing and fixed to zero in the true-quantum feasibility mask before QUBO construction, Ising conversion, finite-shot sampling, exact comparison, or live order-intent formation.
- Turning a venue OFF must immediately block new live writes, keep private-state reconciliation running, preserve cash / position / order-state truth, and emit a disable receipt; canceling existing resting orders is a separately declared owner action unless an existing kill switch or venue emergency gate already requires cancellation.
- Turning a venue ON requires two-step owner confirmation, green connector / account / cash / source / fee / execution / risk / replay gates, and a typed armability receipt; an enabled venue whose gates are not green remains non-live.
- A daily session override may narrow live trading to an owner-approved risk-reduction subset without rewriting the canonical launch-first sleeve set; the override must be explicit, signed, receipt-bound, and never silent.
- The Polymarket sleeve is part of the Day-1 all-three-platform live trading target after all Polymarket gates, source dependencies, connector semantics, cash readiness, risk caps, kill-switch state, and order-state safety checks are green.

### 20B.1A6 Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket proof-gated arbitrage, fake-arbitrage refusal, and launch-first opportunity taxonomy profile

This section makes QTT explicitly arbitrage-capable while preventing Codex from treating every apparent cross-venue price difference as tradable arbitrage. Prediction-market arbitrage is allowed only when the opportunity survives resolution-equivalence proof, payout normalization, fee / tick / rounding / slippage accounting, uncertainty margin, cash-lock accounting, fill-risk control, unmatched-leg handling, venue finality, FORECASTEX_IBKR buy-only normalization, and the cash-only risk gate.

Hard rules:
- QTT may detect and trade proof-gated prediction-market arbitrage across Kalshi, FORECASTEX_IBKR, and Polymarket when every required gate is green.
- QTT must reject fake arbitrage when apparent edge disappears after costs, uncertainty, source mismatch, settlement timing, fill risk, cash lock, or finality delay.
- Cross-venue mispricing, YES / NO complement gaps, multi-outcome bundle gaps, negative-risk conversion opportunities, and maker / taker execution-edge opportunities are candidate families only; none is automatically live-tradable.
- FORECASTEX_IBKR arbitrage variables must use buy-only and opposing-contract netting semantics, never short or sell semantics.
- Abstention is the correct action when net edge after all required deductions is zero, negative, stale, ambiguous, or unproven.
- Arbitrage receipts must serialize candidate type, venue set, equivalence proof, payout normalization, cost terms, uncertainty terms, cash locks, fill plan, finality state, risk verdict, and owner-dashboard state.

### 20B.1A7 Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket low-latency source-integrity arbiter, final-ack capital reuse, and quantum-off-critical-path execution profile

This section welds the launch-first venue-specific low-latency closures into one codable execution arbiter. It does not weaken the fee-aware, source-aware, cash-aware, uncertainty-aware, or proof-gated routing laws in `20B.1A5` and `20B.1A6`. It prevents Codex from improving apparent speed by skipping source integrity, using stale books, reusing cash before final acknowledgement, or waiting for a true-quantum routine inside the final live order-release path.

Hard rules:
- The final live order-release path consumes a precomputed candidate packet; it must not perform full-catalog strategy search, large model inference, replay simulation, or true-quantum sampling while the order writer is waiting.
- WebSocket or source-stream state is preferred for live book and private-state updates when the venue exposes it; REST is used for snapshots, resync, metadata, preview, or source-specific fallbacks.
- A faster route is not a valid route unless its book, metadata, fee, cash, order-state, and source-finality receipts are current.
- Capital may not be reused after a submit event alone; each venue must reach the declared final acknowledgement or finality state for the capital being released.
- True quantum remains shadow/off-critical-path on Day 1 unless a later owner-gated promotion proves latency noninferiority and preserves the classical fallback path.

- **Same-edition family-deployment binding:** this family is `PRIMARY_DEFAULT` whenever `20B.1A5`, `20B.1A6`, `CN-01E3`, `CN-02E5`, `20B.1A2C`, `CN-01`, `CN-02E`, or `CN-03` is active for launch-first live routing, assisted-live arbitrage, maker quoting, taker routing, replay, owner-dashboard monitoring, or quantum-feasibility scope.
- **Explicit agent-selection-universe binding:** `{AGENT_RT_07,AGENT_RT_08,AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_11,AGENT_RT_13,AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_NL_09,AGENT_NL_10,AGENT_OFF_11}` may consume or validate this profile; no other agent may alter final live order-release latency policy, source-integrity requirements, capital-reuse finality, or quantum critical-path exclusion without a later controlling-edition binding row.

### 20B.1A8 Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket operational-state, capacity, and true-quantum feasibility-mask injection closure
- **Domain:** launch-first cross-venue operational feasibility, capacity gating, QUBO / Ising variable masking, candidate invalidation, and owner-dashboard operational-state controls.
- **Purpose:** Force every classical route candidate and every true-quantum / quantum-inspired candidate to consume the same venue-operational-state and capacity mask before optimization. This prevents Codex from letting a fast model or quantum routine optimize infeasible Kalshi pause states, FORECASTEX_IBKR market-data capacity failures, Polymarket allowance failures, stale lifecycle states, or final-order candidates invalidated by a live gate flip.
- **Primary public anchors:** current official Kalshi exchange-status and market-lifecycle documentation, current official IBKR Web API market-data / Client Portal session documentation, current official Polymarket V2 order-create documentation, and current public IBM / Qiskit primitive and optimizer surfaces already bound in the true-quantum sections.
- **Same-edition family-deployment binding:** this family is `PRIMARY_DEFAULT` whenever `20B.1A5`, `20B.1A6`, `20B.1A7`, `20B.1B`, `20B.1B4`, `CN-01E4`, `CN-02E6`, or `20B.1A2D` is active for launch-first live routing, assisted-live arbitrage, shadow quantum, replay, owner-dashboard monitoring, QUBO construction, Ising translation, exact comparator, finite-shot comparison, or quantum-feasibility scope.
- **Explicit agent-selection-universe binding:** `{AGENT_RT_07,AGENT_RT_08,AGENT_RT_09,AGENT_RT_11,AGENT_RT_13,AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_NL_09,AGENT_NL_10,AGENT_OFF_11}` may consume or validate this profile; no other agent may infer alternate operational-state, capacity, mask-injection, candidate invalidation, or true-quantum feasibility semantics without a later controlling-edition binding row.

### 20B.1A11 Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket normalized order-intent digest, idempotent retry, duplicate-lock, and quantum advisory boundary closure

This section closes a cross-venue duplicate-order risk that remains after source-integrity, post-trade, and contract-identity gates. It makes every launch-first live order attempt pass through a canonical order-intent digest and venue-specific idempotency key before any retry is allowed. It also prevents the quantum optimizer from creating retry authority or duplicate live submits by implication.

Hard rules:
- Every live order attempt must first materialize a normalized order-intent digest covering venue, account or wallet scope, market identity, outcome side, action, price, quantity, time-in-force, post-only or maker/taker mode, reduce-only or decrease semantics, cost cap, source-state digest, risk digest, cash-lock digest, and owner-mode digest.
- A retry must reuse the venue-appropriate idempotency key or order identifier rule for the same intent and must never create a second independent live order unless the prior intent is proven terminal, canceled, rejected, or owner-approved for replacement.
- Kalshi retries use `client_order_id` for deduplication before a venue `order_id` is known and must store the key locally before submission.
- FORECASTEX_IBKR retries use `cOID` uniqueness and serialized acknowledgement rules; a second order may not be submitted while the previous order chain is unresolved.
- Polymarket retries reconcile returned `orderID`, signed-order digest, open-order state, cancel partition, and trade history before replacement.
- Retry backoff is state-machine driven by source receipts and pacing gates; QTT must not use a blind fixed sleep as evidence that a live order is safe to duplicate.
- Quantum artifacts may score candidates or produce advisory route digests, but may not mint idempotency keys, authorize retries, or bypass duplicate locks.

### 20B.1B1 Kalshi / Polymarket quantum QUBO objective, penalty, CVaR, and classical-comparator shadow profile
- **Domain:** launch-first prediction-market quantum / true-quantum optimization objective construction, QUBO penalty binding, sampling interpretation, and classical benchmark comparison.
- **Purpose:** Close the remaining Codex-facing gap between the existing QAOA / SPSA / SLSQP / COBYLA defaults and the actual economic objective that a Kalshi / Polymarket quantum shadow optimizer must encode. A true-quantum shadow run may not optimize an abstract toy problem unless the candidate variables, edge coefficients, cost terms, constraint penalties, normalization policy, sampling aggregation, solution repair, and classical comparator are all explicit.
- **Primary public anchors:** Qiskit Algorithms QAOA, CVaR aggregation, SPSA, SLSQP, and COBYLA documentation; IBM Runtime sampler shot-default documentation; public QUBO / Ising portfolio-optimization mapping literature; the `20B.1A1` fee-aware binary-edge profile and the existing `20B.1B` optimizer profile.

### 20B.1B2 Kalshi / Polymarket true-quantum exact-comparator, QUBO-to-Ising translation, finite-shot confidence, degeneracy, and shadow-promotion atomic profile
- **Domain:** launch-first prediction-market true-quantum QUBO validation, classical comparator enforcement, Ising translation, finite-shot evidence, degeneracy handling, and owner-gated promotion.
- **Purpose:** Close the Codex-facing gap between a declared QUBO objective and a trustworthy quantum result. Codex must not treat a sampled QAOA / SamplingVQE / hardware result as economically valid unless the QUBO-to-Ising translation is deterministic, exact or best-available classical comparator evidence is present, finite-shot uncertainty is reported, degenerate solutions are decoded consistently, infeasible bitstrings are repaired or rejected, and the result remains triggered live-concurrent shadow-comparison-only unless owner promotion gates are explicitly green.
- **Primary public anchors:** Qiskit Optimization `MinimumEigenOptimizer` and `to_ising` documentation, Qiskit CVaR optimization documentation, IBM / Qiskit sampler-shot documentation already referenced by `20B.1B`, public QAOA / SPSA / SLSQP / COBYLA defaults already referenced by `20B.1B`, and existing `20B.1B1` QUBO objective profile.
- **Same-edition family-deployment binding:** this family is `TRIGGERED_LIVE_CONCURRENT_SHADOW_COMPARISON_ASSIGNED` for Kalshi and Polymarket launch-first true-quantum optimizer scopes and `REPLAY_ONLY_ASSIGNED` for offline simulator diagnostics; it is not live-authoritative unless the owner-approved quantum promotion path in sections `2.1A` and `2.1A1` is active for the declared scope.
- **Explicit agent-selection-universe binding:** `{AGENT_NL_02,AGENT_NL_05,AGENT_NL_09,AGENT_NL_10,AGENT_NL_11,AGENT_NL_12,AGENT_OFF_03,AGENT_OFF_04,AGENT_OFF_07,AGENT_OFF_11,AGENT_RT_07,AGENT_RT_13}` may consume, fit, validate, veto, or report this profile; no ordinary live execution agent may use the true-quantum result as direct order-release authority without the declared owner-promotion receipt.
- **Canonical `FAMILY_PARAMETER_ATOM_ROW` pack at minimum:**
  - `kp_quantum_result_authority_state`

    - `parameter_role_description`: live-authority state of any quantum optimizer result in Kalshi / Polymarket launch sleeves
    - `resolution_class`: `STATIC_ENUM_WITH_OWNER_PROMOTION_GATE`

    - `reference_range_or_structural_constraint`: enum subset `{TRIGGERED_LIVE_CONCURRENT_COMPARISON_ONLY_NO_DIRECT_LIVE_ORDER_AUTHORITY,OWNER_APPROVED_HYBRID_ADVISORY,OWNER_FORCED_TRUE_QUANTUM_PRIMARY_WITH_FALLBACK,REPLAY_ONLY}`
    - `bounded_search_space_or_fit_constraint`: profitable shadow result alone is not live authorization; owner promotion or owner force remains required
    - `value_source_class`: `QTT_QUANTUM_LIVE_PROMOTION_LAW`
    - `owner_dashboard_editability_class`: `OWNER_ONLY`
    - `ui_widget_class`: `QUANTUM_RESULT_AUTHORITY_BADGE`

    - `resolution_class`: `STATIC_POLICY_WITH_LIBRARY_SOURCE_POINTER`

    - `reference_range_or_structural_constraint`: variable-to-qubit order must be deterministic and recorded; objective sense, offset, scaling, and penalty signs must be preserved
    - `bounded_search_space_or_fit_constraint`: any mismatch between original QUBO objective and decoded Ising objective blocks promotion and emits translation-failure receipt
    - `value_source_class`: `PUBLIC_QISKIT_OPTIMIZATION_DOCUMENTATION`

### 20B.1B3 Kalshi / Polymarket true-quantum feasibility-mask, pending-state, and venue-capacity comparator profile

This section closes the remaining quantum launch-first integration gap. A true-quantum optimizer is only useful for QTT if its candidate universe matches the venue-reachable action universe. Therefore the quantum candidate generator, QUBO builder, Ising translator, sampler, simulator, and exact classical comparator must receive the same cash, allowance, open-order reservation, heartbeat, pending-state, and finality masks used by the live classical execution router.

Hard rules:
- Quantum candidates must be generated after venue feasibility masks, not before them.
- A QUBO coefficient may encode expected edge only for actions that pass the launch-first venue feasibility mask.
- Infeasible actions must be removed from the candidate variable set or fixed to zero before QUBO / Ising translation.
- Penalty terms must not be used as a substitute for mandatory cash, allowance, heartbeat, and finality masks. If a candidate is not venue-reachable, it must not enter the candidate set.
- The classical exact comparator must use the same feasibility mask, capacity formula, and pending-state lock as the quantum path.
- Pending states that are not terminal must remain locked until their venue-specific terminal proof is observed.
- Quantum output receipts must include the mask digest, variable-set digest, removed-variable list, fixed-zero-variable list, capacity-state digest, finality-state digest, and comparator digest.

### 20B.1B4 Kalshi / FORECASTEX_IBKR / Polymarket true-quantum three-venue feasibility, buy-only netting, and source-finality mask profile

This section extends the launch-first true-quantum feasibility mask from Kalshi / Polymarket to the full launch-first venue set that now includes FORECASTEX_IBKR. The purpose is to prevent QUBO, Ising, QAOA, sampler, simulator, or exact-comparator paths from treating FORECASTEX_IBKR buy-only exits, source-delayed markets, coupon uncertainty, or IBKR netting locks as ordinary unconstrained binary choices.

Hard rules:
- FORECASTEX_IBKR candidate variables must be removed or fixed to zero before QUBO / Ising conversion unless buy-only order entry, opposite-contract conid pairing, source freshness, cash capacity, and netting reconciliation gates are green.
- FORECASTEX_IBKR exit variables must encode buy-opposing-contract behavior, not sell behavior.
- FORECASTEX_IBKR coupon EV may be included in the quantum objective only when the same source-verified coupon policy used by the classical comparator is green.
- The exact classical comparator and the quantum path must use the same three-venue mask digest.
- Quantum outputs remain triggered live-concurrent shadow-comparison-only by default and may not create FORECASTEX_IBKR live orders without owner-governed promotion and classical execution-router approval.

## 20C. Runtime state machine

The runtime state machine ensures that the system transitions predictably instead of improvising under stress.

States:
- `BOOTSTRAP`
- `DATA_WARMING`
- `READY_CLASSICAL_ONLY`
- `READY_CLASSICAL_PLUS_DEEP`
- `READY_CLASSICAL_PLUS_QUANTUM_ARTIFACTS`
- `SHADOW_TESTING`
- `CANARY_ACTIVE`
- `LIVE_ACTIVE`
- `THROTTLED`
- `HALTED`
- `RECOVERING`

Transitions:
1. `BOOTSTRAP -> DATA_WARMING` when connectors and clocks start.
2. `DATA_WARMING -> READY_CLASSICAL_ONLY` only when required feeds, configs, and local risk controls are healthy.
3. `READY_CLASSICAL_ONLY -> READY_CLASSICAL_PLUS_DEEP` only when nearline artifacts are fresh and healthy.
4. `READY_CLASSICAL_PLUS_DEEP -> READY_CLASSICAL_PLUS_QUANTUM_ARTIFACTS` only when quantum artifacts are present, fresh, benchmarked, and marked eligible.
5. Any ready state -> `THROTTLED` on drift, connector degradation, calibration stress, or drawdown severity above soft thresholds.
6. `THROTTLED -> HALTED` on hard risk, provenance failure without durable local buffer, or connector/account integrity failure.
7. `HALTED -> RECOVERING` only through explicit reset flow.
8. `RECOVERING -> READY_*` only after health and consistency checks pass.

Hard rule:
No state transition may silently add quantum influence to live decisions. That requires explicit artifact eligibility and owner approval.

### 20C.1 Change-shadow and incident-repair transition overlay

The runtime state machine must also expose change-test and post-incident resume overlays rather than forcing the operator to infer them from generic states.

Minimum required overlay states at minimum:
- `INCUMBENT_LIVE_CONTINUES_CHANGED_SCOPE_SHADOWING`
- `AFFECTED_SCOPE_PAUSED_PENDING_REPAIR_CLASS`
- `CLASS_A_SOAK_ACTIVE`
- `CLASS_B_FORMAL_SHADOW_ACTIVE`
- `CLASS_C_STAGED_LIMITED_RESUME_ONLY`

Hard rule:
These overlays do not replace the base runtime state machine. They annotate it so Codex cannot confuse ordinary `LIVE_ACTIVE` with changed-scope shadowing or post-incident limited-resume behavior.

### 20C.1A Maintenance-pause safety protocol and post-resume health gate

The runtime state machine must also preserve one explicit maintenance-pause and resume-safety protocol so Codex does not reduce pause/resume handling to a blind toggle. The protocol exists to prevent resuming into a broken, stale, or compromised system state after maintenance, outage, repair, or manual pause.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `PRE_PAUSE_POSITION_SNAPSHOT_CARD`
- `MAINTENANCE_PROTECTIVE_ORDER_POLICY_CARD`
- `POST_RESUME_HEALTH_CHECK_CARD`
- `POST_RESUME_HEALTH_COMPONENT_ROW`
- `SELF_DIAGNOSIS_REPAIR_GUIDE_CARD`
- `MAINTENANCE_RESUME_APPROVAL_RECEIPT`

Minimum required protocol components at minimum:
1. **Pre-pause position snapshot and risk assessment** — capture open positions, pending orders, stop-loss state, unrealized P&L, and the currently active risk/regime context before pause confirms.
2. **Exchange-side protective order policy** — where venue semantics allow it, protective exchange-native stop or exit orders may remain live during pause according to declared policy; the default policy must be explicit rather than implied.
3. **No forced liquidation rule** — maintenance pause may never silently force-close, market-sell, or liquidate positions purely because the system is pausing.
4. **Post-resume health check** — no trading may resume until required resume-health checks are evaluated.
5. **Self-diagnosis and repair guidance** — failing or warning components must produce plain-language diagnosis and suggested remediation steps, but never auto-execute a fix unless a separately approved repair workflow already exists.

Minimum required post-resume health categories at minimum:
- API connectivity
- data-feed freshness
- model artifact integrity
- code / checksum integrity
- expected-versus-actual position reconciliation
- GPU / driver / runtime health
- volatility or risk-model staleness
- risk-manager parameter consistency

Mandatory `resume_component_state` enumeration:
- `PASS`
- `WARNING`
- `FAIL`

Hard rules:
- any `FAIL` in a required resume-health component blocks trading until resolved;
- `WARNING` components may only be bypassed through an explicit owner override receipt;
- the no-forced-liquidation rule is non-configurable;
- the protocol is safety-governance only and may not be bypassed by ordinary strategy bundles, connector convenience flags, or generic resume commands.

### 19.19I Hierarchical capital-allocation reference
For deployable capital `C_dep`, baseline sleeve volatility estimate `σ_i`, capacity haircut `h_cap,i ∈ [0,1]`, crowding haircut `h_crd,i ∈ [0,1]`, correlation-stress haircut `h_corr,i ∈ [0,1]`, and execution-realizability haircut `h_exec,i ∈ [0,1]`:
- baseline inverse-volatility weight: `ẁ_i = (1/σ_i) / Σ_j (1/σ_j)`
- adjusted implementable weight: `w_i = ẁ_i * h_cap,i * h_crd,i * h_corr,i * h_exec,i`
- normalized sleeve weight: `w*_i = w_i / Σ_j w_j` when `Σ_j w_j > 0`, else zero-allocation fallback
- sleeve capital allocation: `C_i = C_dep * w*_i`

Operational rule:
if any haircut drives `w_i` to zero, the sleeve may remain researched or shadowed, but it receives no incremental deployable capital.

Stage-1 owner-visible allocation note:
when `RA-15` is active and pricing / execution support are admissible, `HEDGING_AND_CONVEXITY` may initialize at a 10% deployable-capital seed with an owner-visible 10%..15% reference band and the already-declared hard upper bound; this is a bounded sleeve, not an unconstrained tail bet.


### 19.19I1 Hierarchical capital-allocation atomic parameter pack
- **Purpose:** Materialize the Day-1 parameter rows for `19.19I` so baseline weighting, volatility basis, haircut stack, zero-weight fallback, and bounded hedging/convexity seed policy do not remain only prose-canonical when deployable-capital allocator cards are rendered.
- **Primary public anchors:** public inverse-volatility and risk-budgeting references together with stronger existing QTT capital-allocation and sleeve-bounding laws.
- **Canonical `FAMILY_PARAMETER_ATOM_ROW` pack at minimum:**
  - `capital_allocation_baseline_weight_family`
    - `parameter_symbol`: `cap_base`

### 19.19J Deterministic hedge-failure and neutralization priority reference
For an active exposure `E_t` whose intended hedge has not completed, the neutralization priority is ordered lexicographically rather than opportunistically:
1. same-venue repair if the connector remains healthy and the original hedge instrument remains admissible;
2. cross-venue repair if an approved equivalent venue path exists and the connector matrix still admits it;
3. approved proxy hedge if an approved factor/correlation proxy remains within its admissibility bounds;
4. inventory haircut / size reduction under the active exposure-decay protocol;
5. flatten-to-cash.

Operational rule:
no sleeve may skip directly to a lower-priority repair path while a higher-priority admissible path remains both healthy and faster inside the declared exposure-time budget.

### 19.19K Time-source precedence and timestamp-basis reference
Default timestamp precedence when available:
- NIC hardware timestamp synchronized through PHC/PTP
- kernel timestamp
- userspace monotonic capture timestamp

Operational rule:
replay, shadow, and live comparisons must declare which timestamp basis is authoritative for sequencing, latency measurement, and venue-clock comparison; incompatible bases require an explicit normalization receipt.

## 20D. Dashboard and operator surfaces

Hard rule:
The primary operator dashboard must be readable from the local control surface without requiring open inbound internet exposure. External publication, if ever approved, must be a separately hardened derivative surface rather than the authoritative live dashboard.

The operator dashboard must expose:

### 20D.1 Live strategy panel
- strategy ID,
- current state,
- active family IDs,
- active defaults vs tuned profiles,
- last promotion date,
- last rollback date,
- last health event.

### 20D.2 Parameter panel
- family ID,
- parameter name,
- unit and render format,
- public default,
- seed route (institutional-style only if evidence-backed),
- day-1 start value,
- current validated default,
- current live value,
- current triggered live-concurrent shadow-comparison candidate value when present,
- last-known-good live value,
- reference range,
- bounded search range,
- owner-dashboard editability class,
- widget class,
- shadow-trigger class,
- last tune receipt,
- fallback profile,
- affected modules,
- owner approval record.

### 20D.2A Owner parameter-control and edit workflow panel
The owner dashboard must expose every materially used editable parameter through one consistent control surface so the owner can review, change, and track values without forcing Codex to infer how edits propagate.

Minimum required per-row controls at minimum:
- visible current live value and its source-of-truth class,
- visible day-1 start value,
- visible reference range separate from bounded search range,
- visible editability class and widget class,
- visible shadow-trigger class,
- `Open edit dialog` when the parameter is editable,
- `Create triggered live-concurrent shadow comparison candidate` or equivalent action text when the edit has a live execution surface and a shadow trigger,
- explicit read-only rationale when the row is not owner-editable,
- explicit last-known-good live pointer for rollback review.

Hard rules:
- the dashboard may not present one ambiguous “current value” field where the live value, validated default, and pending triggered live-concurrent shadow-comparison candidate differ;
- any editable row must render its reference range, bounded search range, and unit/scale before the edit is confirmed;
- every committed edit must create a `PARAMETER_EDIT_IMPACT_RECEIPT` and, where required, a `PARAMETER_CHILD_BUNDLE_RECEIPT` before the system may claim the candidate is ready for replay or shadow;
- the owner dashboard may support direct manual edits, but it may not bypass replay / shadow / owner-gate law for materially behavior-changing parameter classes.

Validation hooks:
- `test_parameter_panel_shows_day1_start_current_live_and_lkg.py`
- `test_parameter_panel_shows_reference_range_separate_from_search_range.py`
- `test_parameter_panel_shows_widget_and_editability_class.py`
- `test_parameter_edit_impact_receipt_created_on_commit.py`

### 20D.2B Owner parameter-source provenance and legitimacy panel
The owner dashboard must expose not only the value but also the legitimacy basis for every materially used parameter row so the owner can distinguish a public package default, a public academic seed, an institutional-style public seed, and an internally validated override.

Minimum required per-row provenance fields at minimum:
- visible `value_source_class`
- visible `default_legitimacy_class`
- visible `value_source_anchor_id` or equivalent source badge
- visible `reference_range_source_basis`
- visible `search_range_source_basis`
- explicit blocker badge when the row is `NOT_ELIGIBLE_FOR_DAY1_LIVE`

Hard rules:
- an editable parameter row may not be shown as Day-1-ready unless its legitimacy class and source badge are rendered on the owner surface;
- the dashboard may collapse provenance details behind a disclosure control, but it may not hide that provenance entirely for materially used rows;
- any owner-approved override must update the provenance panel so the distinction between accepted-source-packet start value and internal validated live override remains explicit.

Validation hooks:
- `test_owner_parameter_provenance_panel_required.py`
- `test_day1_ready_rows_show_legitimacy_class.py`
- `test_owner_override_updates_provenance_panel.py`

### 20D.2C Owner atomic-parameter drilldown and export panel
The owner dashboard must expose not only family-level parameter cards but also an atomic drilldown view so materially used family parameters can be inspected, exported, and reviewed without forcing Codex or the owner to infer hidden sub-parameters from prose.

Minimum required panel capabilities at minimum:
- expand a family row into its `FAMILY_PARAMETER_ATOM_ROW` members;
- show `parameter_id`, symbol, live value, day-1 seed rule, reference range or structural constraint, search space, source badge, editability class, and shadow-trigger class;
- render `FIT_TIME_RESOLVED` parameters as live resolved values plus the declared resolution rule rather than as fake static constants;
- permit CSV / YAML export of the atomic parameter rows for the selected family or bundle;
- show explicit read-only rationale for non-editable fitted parameters;
- show last-known-good pointers for any parameter that participates in rollback scope.

Hard rules:
- a family may not be marked owner-review-complete if its owner surface does not permit atomic drilldown when the family is materially used;
- dashboard family summaries may be collapsed by default, but the atomic parameter view must remain available on demand;
- export views must preserve provenance badges and unit / basis declarations so copied parameter sheets do not lose their legitimacy context.

Validation hooks:
- `test_owner_atomic_parameter_drilldown_panel_required.py`
- `test_fit_time_resolved_rows_render_live_value_plus_rule.py`
- `test_family_parameter_export_preserves_source_badges.py`

### 20D.3 Connector panel
- connector health,
- session state,
- rate-limit state,
- last error,
- maintenance window status,
- read-only / write-enabled status.

### 20D.4 Quantum artifact panel
- artifact ID,
- family ID,
- freshness TTL,
- backend/solver identity,
- comparator status,
- eligible/ineligible state,
- current quantum-promotion-fabric stage,
- linked strongest classical comparator,
- fallback bundle,
- last benchmark packet,
- last replay packet,
- last shadow packet,
- live-eligibility packet status.

### 20D.4AA Quantum candidate lifecycle and owner-control panel
The owner and operator surfaces must also preserve one dedicated **Quantum Candidate Lifecycle Panel** so repeated true-quantum research, replay, shadow, cached-live influence approval, rollback, revitalization, and retirement can be executed through one canonical grammar rather than through scattered notes.

Minimum required panel actions at minimum:
- `research`
- `replay`
- `shadow`
- `extend shadow`
- `approve cached-live influence`
- `rollback`
- `revitalization`
- `retire`

Minimum required panel fields at minimum:
- `quantum_candidate_id`
- `current_stage`
- `objective_formula_id`
- `strongest_classical_comparator_id`
- `artifact_ttl_class`
- `freshness_class`
- `fallback_bundle_id`
- `resource_envelope_class`
- `expected_information_gain_band`
- `expected_economic_upside_band`
- `cyber_risk_band`
- `owner_override_state`
- `last_stage_transition_timestamp`

Hard rules:
- the panel is a governance and workflow surface, not an unaudited shortcut around the underlying stage machine;
- no button may render as enabled when the preceding required stage receipts are missing;
- `approve cached-live influence` may render enabled only when replay, shadow, fallback, freshness, and classical-final-authority compatibility receipts remain green;
- the panel must show the exact blocker reason when a requested lifecycle action is unavailable.

### 20D.4A MBO / order-lifecycle observability panel
- venue and dataset identity,
- attribution-confidence state,
- order-reference continuity state,
- child-print concentration bucket,
- queue-persistence bucket,
- iceberg / hidden-liquidity state,
- displayed-vs-executed multiple bucket,
- cancel-to-fill bucket,
- replace-to-fill bucket,
- visual authority legend (`packet-backed`, `packet-assisted`, or `training/screenshot only`),
- and the exact packet IDs feeding the visual surface.

### 20D.4B Quantum intelligence panel
The operator and owner surfaces must also preserve one dedicated **Quantum Intelligence Panel** so quarterly scouting output, stack health, and discovery backlog do not disappear into generic research cards.

Minimum required panel sections at minimum:
- domain breakdown for discoveries screened across the four scouting domains,
- stage breakdown across the five-stage evaluation pipeline,
- benchmark completion summary with PASS / MARGINAL / FAIL counts,
- proposal summary with current owner-decision status,
- implementations-live summary with benchmark-predicted versus actual realized effect so far,
- cumulative quantum-upgrade P&L,
- QTT quantum-stack health,

Required ordering rules at minimum:
