Canonical normalized command-form doctrine at minimum:
- unary queue-view commands use exactly one token: `/packet`, `/decisions`, `/risk`, `/live`, `/research`, `/shadow`, `/refine`, `/backlog`, `/changeq`
- unary card-action commands use exactly two tokens: `/ack CARD_ID`, `/approve_shadow CARD_ID`, `/more_research CARD_ID`, `/reject_archive CARD_ID`, `/backlog_revitalization CARD_ID`, `/approve_live CARD_ID`, `/return_refinement CARD_ID`, `/restrict_live CARD_ID`, `/kill_switch CARD_ID`, `/investigate CARD_ID`, `/reopen_gate1 CARD_ID`, `/keep_parked CARD_ID`, `/updated_research CARD_ID`
- the only three-token owner queue action in this surface is `/extend_shadow CARD_ID EXTEND_SHADOW_BASIS_CLASS`

Hard rules:
- canonical owner-command argument tokens are `CARD_ID`, `EXTEND_SHADOW_BASIS_CLASS`, `AGENT_OR_POD_ID`, `CONVERSATION_ID`, `SCOPE_ID`, `LINKED_CARD_ID`, `AGENT_ID`, `QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`, and `OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT`; they are authoritative command-grammar atoms, not unresolved template tokens;
- executable command examples may not use angle-bracket template token grammar or bracketed optional-argument grammar; optionality must be normalized into separate admissible command forms instead of symbolic shorthand;
- legacy `_OPTIONAL` suffix labels may not remain inside executable or normalized command-form examples once the admissible command forms have been made explicit;
- every accepted or rejected owner command must emit `OWNER_COMMAND_PARSE_RECEIPT`, `OWNER_COMMAND_ARGUMENT_BINDING_RECEIPT`, and either `OWNER_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_RECEIPT` or `OWNER_COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_RECEIPT` before `OWNER_COMMAND_FINALIZATION_RECEIPT` is emitted;
- Telegram commands are shortcuts into the same audited action codes used by the dashboard packet;
- Telegram may not bypass audit logging, required evidence display, owner confirmation class, or the two-gate owner ladder;
- Telegram may summarize for speed, but it may not omit the default safe action or hide a required owner action.
- `command_parser_profile_id` must resolve to one declared parser profile and may not be inferred from transport, client, or notebook context;
- `authoritative_owner_command_parse_instance_id` must be emitted once at parse time and then reused unchanged across `OWNER_COMMAND_PARSE_RECEIPT`, `OWNER_COMMAND_ARGUMENT_BINDING_RECEIPT`, `OWNER_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_CAPTURE_RECEIPT`, `OWNER_COMMAND_REJECT_REASON_RECEIPT`, and `OWNER_COMMAND_FINALIZATION_RECEIPT` for the same command event;
- `owner_command_transport_normalized_text_hash` must bind the transport-normalized command text to the same authoritative parse instance and may not be recomputed into a second authoritative identity later in the receipt chain;
- `owner_command_transport_event_id_when_available` must be preserved exactly when the ingress transport supplies one and may not be discarded before idempotency resolution;
- `owner_command_idempotency_key` must be computed before any downstream action release and must bind the normalized command form, authoritative parse-instance id, and transport-normalized command text under one declared dedup identity;
- `owner_command_delivery_dedup_state` must resolve explicitly before finalization and may not be inferred from action-layer side effects;
- `owner_command_duplicate_delivery_state` must distinguish `{NEW_DELIVERY, DUPLICATE_DELIVERY_SUPPRESSED, DUPLICATE_DELIVERY_REQUIRES_OPERATOR_REVIEW}` rather than collapsing all duplicate situations into one silent retry path;
- `owner_command_execution_claim_state` must resolve explicitly before any downstream action release whenever the command is otherwise admissible for action;
- `owner_command_execution_claim_holder_id_when_applicable` must identify the single authoritative claim holder allowed to emit the downstream action code for that command event;
- `owner_command_execution_claim_receipt_ref_when_applicable` must resolve to the exact claim receipt proving exclusive action authority for the authoritative parse instance;
- `owner_command_claim_expiry_state` must resolve explicitly and may not be inferred from silence, heartbeat absence, or transport timeout folklore alone;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_state` must resolve explicitly whenever a stale or abandoned claim is reclaimed or reviewed;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_mode_class` must resolve explicitly whenever policy compatibility is evaluated and may not be conflated with the runtime progress state of a specific recovery attempt;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_mode_class` is bounded to `{AUTO_RECLAIM_ALLOWED_OR_REVIEW_ESCALATION, REVIEW_ESCALATION_ONLY_NO_AUTO_RECLAIM}` in this surface; undeclared recovery-mode variants are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_state` is the runtime state for the recovery attempt and may not be used as a policy-class substitute;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_state` is bounded to `{NOT_REQUIRED_NOT_STALE, STALE_DETECTED_PENDING_POLICY_EVALUATION, AUTO_RECLAIM_IN_PROGRESS, AUTO_RECLAIM_COMPLETED, REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED, REVIEW_ESCALATION_COMPLETED, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION, FAIL_CLOSED}` in this surface; undeclared recovery-state variants are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_entry_state_admissibility` must resolve explicitly and may not be inferred from implementation convenience;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_entry_state_admissibility` is bounded to `{ENTRY_ALLOWED, ENTRY_FORBIDDEN}` for each declared recovery state;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_terminality_state` must resolve explicitly and may not be inferred from prose markers such as `terminal`;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_receipt_ref_when_applicable` must resolve to the exact typed receipt proving why a stale claim was reclaimed, suppressed, or escalated instead of leaving claim recovery to undocumented worker habit;
- `owner_command_claim_expiry_policy_class` must resolve explicitly before `owner_command_claim_expiry_deadline_ts` is materialized and may not be inferred from undeclared transport, thread, or worker defaults;
- `owner_command_claim_expiry_policy_class` is bounded to `{FIXED_MONOTONIC_TTL, FIXED_UTC_DEADLINE, OWNER_REVIEW_ONLY_NO_AUTO_RECLAIM}` in this surface; undeclared policy variants are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_expiry_policy_class` and `owner_command_claim_clock_basis` must resolve through one exact compatibility matrix: `FIXED_MONOTONIC_TTL -> MONOTONIC_CLOCK_ONLY`, `FIXED_UTC_DEADLINE -> UTC_WALL_CLOCK_ONLY`, `OWNER_REVIEW_ONLY_NO_AUTO_RECLAIM -> NO_AUTO_EXPIRY_TIMER_REQUIRED`; invalid policy / clock combinations are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_expiry_policy_class`, `owner_command_claim_clock_basis`, and `owner_command_claim_expiry_deadline_ts` must also resolve through one exact deadline-shape matrix: `FIXED_MONOTONIC_TTL -> monotonic-deadline timestamp required`, `FIXED_UTC_DEADLINE -> UTC deadline timestamp required`, `OWNER_REVIEW_ONLY_NO_AUTO_RECLAIM -> no auto-expiry deadline timestamp may be materialized`; invalid policy / deadline-shape combinations are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_expiry_policy_class` and `owner_command_claim_recovery_mode_class` must also resolve through one exact recovery-mode matrix: `FIXED_MONOTONIC_TTL -> AUTO_RECLAIM_ALLOWED_OR_REVIEW_ESCALATION`, `FIXED_UTC_DEADLINE -> AUTO_RECLAIM_ALLOWED_OR_REVIEW_ESCALATION`, `OWNER_REVIEW_ONLY_NO_AUTO_RECLAIM -> REVIEW_ESCALATION_ONLY_NO_AUTO_RECLAIM`; invalid policy / recovery-mode combinations are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_mode_class` and `owner_command_claim_recovery_state` must also resolve through one exact mode-to-runtime-state compatibility matrix: `AUTO_RECLAIM_ALLOWED_OR_REVIEW_ESCALATION -> {NOT_REQUIRED_NOT_STALE, STALE_DETECTED_PENDING_POLICY_EVALUATION, AUTO_RECLAIM_IN_PROGRESS, AUTO_RECLAIM_COMPLETED, REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED, REVIEW_ESCALATION_COMPLETED, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION, FAIL_CLOSED}`, `REVIEW_ESCALATION_ONLY_NO_AUTO_RECLAIM -> {NOT_REQUIRED_NOT_STALE, STALE_DETECTED_PENDING_POLICY_EVALUATION, REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED, REVIEW_ESCALATION_COMPLETED, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION, FAIL_CLOSED}`; invalid recovery-mode / runtime-state combinations are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_state` must also resolve through one exact admissible transition graph: `NOT_REQUIRED_NOT_STALE -> {STALE_DETECTED_PENDING_POLICY_EVALUATION, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION}`, `STALE_DETECTED_PENDING_POLICY_EVALUATION -> {AUTO_RECLAIM_IN_PROGRESS, REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION, FAIL_CLOSED}`, `AUTO_RECLAIM_IN_PROGRESS -> {AUTO_RECLAIM_COMPLETED, FAIL_CLOSED}`, `AUTO_RECLAIM_COMPLETED -> {REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION}`, `REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED -> {REVIEW_ESCALATION_COMPLETED, FAIL_CLOSED}`, `REVIEW_ESCALATION_COMPLETED -> {SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION}`, `SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION -> {NO_SUCCESSOR_STATES}`, `FAIL_CLOSED -> {NO_SUCCESSOR_STATES}`; undeclared transitions are forbidden;
- the admissible entry-state set is exactly `{NOT_REQUIRED_NOT_STALE, STALE_DETECTED_PENDING_POLICY_EVALUATION, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION, FAIL_CLOSED}`; direct initialization into `{AUTO_RECLAIM_IN_PROGRESS, AUTO_RECLAIM_COMPLETED, REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED, REVIEW_ESCALATION_COMPLETED}` is forbidden unless reached through the declared transition graph;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_entry_state_admissibility_map` must resolve exactly to `{NOT_REQUIRED_NOT_STALE -> ENTRY_ALLOWED, STALE_DETECTED_PENDING_POLICY_EVALUATION -> ENTRY_ALLOWED, AUTO_RECLAIM_IN_PROGRESS -> ENTRY_FORBIDDEN, AUTO_RECLAIM_COMPLETED -> ENTRY_FORBIDDEN, REVIEW_ESCALATION_REQUIRED -> ENTRY_FORBIDDEN, REVIEW_ESCALATION_COMPLETED -> ENTRY_FORBIDDEN, SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION -> ENTRY_ALLOWED, FAIL_CLOSED -> ENTRY_ALLOWED}`; undeclared entry-admissibility mappings are forbidden;
- `owner_command_claim_recovery_terminality_state` is bounded to `{NON_TERMINAL, TERMINAL_NO_SUCCESSOR_STATES}` and must resolve as `TERMINAL_NO_SUCCESSOR_STATES` exactly for `SUPPRESSED_DUE_TO_PRIOR_FINALIZATION` and `FAIL_CLOSED`; all other recovery states must resolve as `NON_TERMINAL`;
- `owner_command_claim_clock_basis` must resolve explicitly and may not be inferred from unspecified wall-clock assumptions when claim expiry is evaluated;
- `owner_command_claim_expiry_deadline_ts` must be materialized explicitly for each authoritative claim instance before the claim can be evaluated as stale, reclaimed, or still authoritative;
- `receipt_emission_order_state` must resolve exactly to `PARSE_THEN_BIND_THEN_PAYLOAD_OR_REJECT_THEN_FINALIZE` for accepted or rejected owner commands in this surface;
- `command_finalization_state` may not become `FINALIZED_ACCEPTED` until the normalized form, argument binding, payload-capture when applicable, and accepted action-code reference are all green;
- `command_finalization_state` may not become `FINALIZED_REJECTED` until the normalized form, argument binding attempt, and reject-reason receipt are all green;
- `accepted_action_code_ref_when_applicable` must remain empty on rejected commands and must resolve to the exact downstream audited action code on accepted commands;
- `rejected_before_action_code_state` must resolve to `TRUE` for rejected commands and `FALSE` for accepted commands;
- no owner command may emit two contradictory finalization receipts for the same authoritative parse instance;
- no owner command receipt in this surface may refer to a different `authoritative_owner_command_parse_instance_id` once the parse receipt has been emitted;
- no second authoritative parse-instance id may be minted for the same transport-normalized command text after binding, payload capture, rejection, or finalization has begun;
- no downstream action code may execute before `OWNER_COMMAND_FINALIZATION_RECEIPT` is green for the same authoritative parse instance.
- if `owner_command_duplicate_delivery_state = DUPLICATE_DELIVERY_SUPPRESSED`, the command may emit receipts and a final rejected-or-suppressed outcome but may not emit a second downstream action code;
- no mirrored, retried, replayed, or transport-repeated owner command delivery may cause a second live action when the same `owner_command_idempotency_key` has already produced a green finalization receipt;
- if two or more workers see the same admissible owner command before finalization, exactly one may hold `owner_command_execution_claim_state = CLAIM_HELD_FOR_ACTION_RELEASE`; all others must resolve to a non-authoritative wait, suppress, or reject state and may not emit the action code;
- downstream action release requires both a green idempotency decision and a green exclusive execution claim for the same authoritative parse instance;
- execution-claim resolution belongs to the owner-command plane itself and may not be deferred to downstream action handlers or connector-side luck.
- a claim holder that fails, stalls, disconnects, or otherwise abandons the command before finalization may not retain indefinite exclusive authority; stale claims must resolve through the explicit claim-expiry and claim-recovery states;
- reclaiming a stale claim may not emit a second downstream action code if the prior claim already produced a green action release or green finalization for the same authoritative parse instance;
- claim expiry and claim recovery belong to the owner-command plane itself and may not be deferred to operator memory or undocumented service restarts.
- no claim may be marked stale, reclaimed, or still-authoritative without the declared `owner_command_claim_clock_basis` and `owner_command_claim_expiry_deadline_ts`;
- no claim may be marked stale, reclaimed, or still-authoritative without the declared `owner_command_claim_expiry_policy_class`, `owner_command_claim_clock_basis`, and `owner_command_claim_expiry_deadline_ts`;
- claim expiry must evaluate against the declared clock basis rather than against transport latency folklore, notebook-local time, or undeclared service defaults.
- idempotency resolution belongs to the owner-command plane itself and may not be deferred to downstream action handlers as an implicit safety net.

### 20D.8A0 Direct owner-to-agent conversational command extensions

The dashboard packet and Telegram mirror are still not fully Codex-complete if the owner can approve, reject, extend, or kill but cannot directly open a bounded conversation with a named agent, specialist pod, or broadcast scope. QTT must therefore preserve one exact direct-conversation command extension surface that remains under the same audit and action grammar as the rest of the owner command plane.

Minimum required owner-visible conversational commands at minimum:
- `/chat AGENT_OR_POD_ID`
- `/reply CONVERSATION_ID OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT`
- `/broadcast SCOPE_ID OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT`
- `/transcript CONVERSATION_ID`
- `/messages AGENT_OR_POD_ID`
- `/directive AGENT_OR_POD_ID`
- `/directive AGENT_OR_POD_ID LINKED_CARD_ID`
- `/pause_agent AGENT_ID`
- `/resume_agent AGENT_ID`
- `/quantum_research QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`
- `/quantum_replay QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`
- `/quantum_shadow QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`
- `/quantum_extend_shadow QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`
- `/quantum_approve_cached_live QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`
- `/quantum_rollback QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`
- `/quantum_revitalization QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`
- `/quantum_retire QUANTUM_CANDIDATE_ID`

Canonical normalized conversational command forms at minimum:
- the former optional linked-card slot is normalized into two exact admissible forms only: `/directive AGENT_OR_POD_ID` and `/directive AGENT_OR_POD_ID LINKED_CARD_ID`
- reply and broadcast commands require a trailing free-text payload field and therefore normalize exactly to `/reply CONVERSATION_ID OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT` and `/broadcast SCOPE_ID OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT`
- `OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT` begins immediately after the last fixed positional token and consumes the remaining command payload verbatim under the audited owner-command logging surface
- `OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT` must contain at least one non-whitespace codepoint after trimming outer transport whitespace; empty payloads are invalid for `/reply` and `/broadcast`
- command parsing splits only on the fixed positional tokens declared above; quoting, punctuation, packet IDs, or URLs inside `OWNER_MESSAGE_TEXT` do not create additional command arguments and do not change positional parsing

Hard rules:
- `EXTEND_SHADOW_BASIS_CLASS` must resolve through the bounded enum `{DAYS, SAMPLES, REGIMES}` before the command is accepted;
- direct conversation commands enter the same audited owner action surface as dashboard actions and may not create a parallel unaudited chat plane;
- conversational commands may target a single agent, a specialist pod, or a bounded broadcast scope, but may not silently expand to undeclared recipients;
- a direct conversation may request analysis, clarification, explanation, or a bounded operational directive, but any live-affecting state change must still map into the canonical decision/action ladder, risk gates, and owner audit law;
- `/pause_agent` and `/resume_agent` remain governance actions and may not bypass kill-switch, runtime-profile, or risk-manager authority;
- quantum lifecycle commands remain audited owner actions and must resolve through the exact Quantum Promotion Fabric stage machine rather than through a free-form side channel.

### 20D.8A0A Plain-English owner idea intake, one-click submission, and auto-routing law

The direct-conversation command surface is still not fully owner-friendly if the owner must know slash commands, agent IDs, or pod IDs just to feed one new idea into QTT. Codex must therefore preserve one exact plain-English idea-intake surface on the dashboard and Telegram mirror so the owner can submit a new idea in ordinary language while QTT converts it into the same audited intake and routing objects already used elsewhere.

Minimum required owner-facing actions at minimum:
- dashboard button labeled `New Idea`
- Telegram quick action labeled `Send New Idea`
- plain-English free-text submission box on both surfaces
- optional category picker
- optional priority picker
- optional attachment or link picker
- visible `Submit` action

Minimum required plain-English intake form fields at minimum:
- `plain_english_idea_text`
- `idea_type` in `{new_quantum_strategy, new_market_or_platform_idea, risk_or_control_improvement, data_or_source_idea, bug_or_incident_relevance, other}`
- `priority_class` in `{normal, high, urgent}`
- optional `source_url_or_attachment_refs`
- optional `owner_note`
- optional `affected_market_or_venue`

Minimum required post-submit owner feedback at minimum:
- generated `ri_id`
- one-line summary of the interpreted idea
- routed target scope
- routing confidence class
- current safe default action
- next step
- link into the canonical intake card and research-topic timeline

Hard rules:
- the `New Idea` and `Send New Idea` surfaces must create the same underlying `RESEARCH_INTAKE_RECORD_CARD` object used by command-driven or fallback intake paths;
- no ordinary owner workflow may require slash-command memorization when the plain-English intake surface is available;
- QTT must auto-route the idea to the correct scout, specialist pod, or triage queue using the same routing and audit grammar already required by the research-intake law;
- if routing confidence is low, the system must place the intake into an explicit review queue rather than silently guessing a mandate owner or agent target;
- the dashboard and Telegram mirror may optimize the form factor, but they may not invent a second intake object type, a second status ladder, or a second audit trail;
- the plain-English idea surface is an intake surface only and may not directly approve shadow, approve live, or bypass the owner-gate ladder.

Plain-English example doctrine:
- an owner message such as `Look into whether a new true quantum optimizer could improve options-vol surface mispricing` must be admissible without command syntax;
- QTT must translate that sentence into one typed intake record, one routing decision, and one owner acknowledgment summary before any downstream research or proposal generation continues.

### 20D.8A1 Multi-channel owner mirror, degraded-rendering, and fallback-channel law

Telegram remains the primary mirrored command surface by default, but QTT may also preserve optional Discord and Slack mirrors for journaling, secondary review, or team-style notification routing. The authoritative governance language remains the same across all channels.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `CHANNEL_MIRROR_PROFILE_CARD`
- `MIRROR_DELIVERY_RECEIPT`
- `CROSS_CHANNEL_STATE_SYNC_RECEIPT`
- `MIRROR_DEGRADED_RENDERING_NOTICE`

Hard rules:
- the dashboard remains the authoritative color-rich surface; Telegram, Discord, and Slack mirrors may accelerate review, but they may not create a second approval grammar or a second audit trail;
- if a mirror channel cannot faithfully render full colors, embeds, buttons, or layout, the message must degrade into emoji, bounded severity tags, packet IDs, and exact action labels rather than silently losing meaning;
- Telegram remains the default actionable mirror; Discord and Slack are read-only by default unless the owner explicitly binds them to the same audited action codes and confirmation classes;
- positive or negative P&L semantics may never rely on color alone in mirror channels; a text or emoji fallback such as `🟢 PROFIT`, `🔴 LOSS`, `🟠 REVIEW`, or `🛑 CRITICAL` is mandatory;
- mirror delivery failures must emit a `MIRROR_DELIVERY_RECEIPT` or alert rather than silently dropping owner-relevant notifications.

### 20D.8B Packet cadence, unread-state, and owner audit law

Minimum required packet-generation cadence at minimum:
- one scheduled owner packet per declared review cycle,
- event-driven packet generation for any `S3_URGENT` or `S4_CRITICAL` event, Gate 2 completion, live restriction, or owner-requested refresh,
- no-noise suppression so minor telemetry wobble does not create a fresh owner packet unless a decision state or severity changed.

Minimum required card read-state enumeration at minimum:
- `UNREAD`
- `READ`
- `ACTIONED`
- `SUPERSEDED`
- `EXPIRED`

Hard rules:
- every owner action must emit an immutable audit row with `packet_id`, `card_id`, selected action, timestamp, and pre/post state;
- if an owner dismisses a packet without acting, unresolved actionable cards must remain visible in the next packet until resolved, superseded, or explicitly expired;
- dashboard UI and Telegram rendering layers may change spacing, iconography, or scan aids, but not the canonical audit state, action semantics, or safe-default meaning.

### 20D.8C Exact visual review-speed rendering law

The owner packet and Telegram mirror are not fully Codex-complete if action labels, safe-default emphasis, scan badges, and review colors remain informal. Codex must therefore preserve one exact rendering contract so dashboard and Telegram accelerate review without inventing a second governance language.

Hard rule:
The underlying action code remains authoritative. Emoji, icons, and colors are scan aids only. UI polish may change spacing or icon order, but it may not invent new actions, rename underlying action semantics, or change safe-default meaning.

Canonical emoji-enhanced button labels at minimum:

Gate 1 — Research Proposal Card
- `🧪 Approve for Shadow`
- `🔍 Request More Research`
- `🗃️ Reject-Archive`
- `📦 Return to Backlog-Revitalization`

Gate 2 — Shadow Results Card
- `✅ Approve Live`
- `⏳ Extend Shadow`
- `❌ Reject`
- `🛠️ Return for Refinement`
- `📦 Return to Backlog-Revitalization`

Live Alert Card
- `👁️ Acknowledge`
- `🟠 Restrict Live`
- `🛑 Kill Switch`
- `🧭 Request Investigation`

Backlog Reopen Card
- `🔄 Reopen to Gate 1`
- `💤 Keep Parked`
- `🔎 Request Updated Research`

Change Queue Review Card
- `📋 View Change Packet`
- `🧪 View Shadow Evidence`
- `⏸ Keep Disabled`
- `🚀 Approve Rollout` only when a separate Gate 2 live approval already exists

Default-safe-action highlighting law:
- if Gate 1 evidence is incomplete, visually emphasize `🔍 Request More Research`;
- if Gate 2 sample count, regime coverage, or shadow evidence is incomplete, visually emphasize `⏳ Extend Shadow`;
- if live safety is uncertain, visually emphasize `🟠 Restrict Live` over `🛑 Kill Switch` unless a true hard-stop condition exists.

Exact base color palette at minimum:

| UI state | Hex | Intended use | Emoji fallback |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Profit / healthy / approved | `#16A34A` | positive P&L, healthy live state, approve-live outcome | 🟢 / ✅ |
| Review / info blue | `#2563EB` | Gate 1 cards, informational research items, non-risk review states | 🔵 / 📘 |
| Shadow / diagnostic purple | `#7C3AED` | Gate 2 cards, shadow packets, challenger diagnostics | 🟣 / 🧪 |
| Priority amber | `#F59E0B` | sample deficiency, extend-shadow default, caution review | 🟡 / ⏳ |
| Urgent orange | `#F97316` | restrict-live state, urgent owner review | 🟠 / ⚠️ |
| Critical red | `#DC2626` | kill-switch, hard stop, reject on safety grounds | 🔴 / 🚨 / 🛑 |
| Backlog / parked slate | `#64748B` | backlog, revitalization, archived-neutral states | ⚪ / 📦 / 💤 |
| Gold highlight | `#D97706` | priority research, owner-highlighted card, scorecard emphasis | ⭐ |
| Neutral border / text | `#CBD5E1` | secondary borders, non-action metadata | ⚪ |

Minimum required quick-scan badge slots at minimum:
- severity badge,
- mode badge,
- safe-default badge,
- time badge.

Minimum required canonical badge values at minimum:
- severity badge in `{S0_INFO, S1_REVIEW, S2_PRIORITY, S3_URGENT, S4_CRITICAL}`
- mode badge in `{LIVE, RESEARCH, SHADOW, REFINE, BACKLOG, CHANGE}`
- safe-default badge = `SAFE DEFAULT`
- time badge in `{NOW, TODAY, THIS_WEEK}` or explicit date.

Profit Impact Scorecard color discipline:
- expected profit impact = green only if positive and benchmarked, amber if estimated but unbenchmarked, red if negative or degraded,
- confidence level = green for strong, amber for moderate, red for weak,
- time to implementation = blue for design-only, amber for code plus triggered-live-concurrent-shadow-comparison when required, slate for backlog,
- risk level = green for low, amber for medium, red for high.

Hard rule:
No scorecard cell may be rendered green unless the underlying metric is supported by benchmark, replay, or shadow evidence.

### 20D.8D Owner progress-strip, owner-progress-field, and linked-card law

The Owner Dashboard Packet and Telegram mirror are not fully Codex-complete if the owner can see a card but still cannot tell who currently owns the work, who is blocking forward progress, what the next step is, or where the item sits on the research-to-live timeline. Codex must therefore preserve one canonical progress-strip and owner-progress-field contract for every material research, change, shadow, incident, or rollout item.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `OWNER_PROGRESS_TIMELINE_PACKET`
- `OWNER_CARD_CUSTODY_PACKET`
- `OWNER_LINKED_ARTIFACT_INDEX_PACKET`

Minimum required owner-progress fields at minimum:
- `current_holder`
- `pending_with`
- `next_owner`
- `current_stage`
- `completed_timestamp`
- `last_update_timestamp`
- `sla_or_review_window`
- `blocking_issues`
- `linked_cards`
- `canonical_safe_default_action`

Minimum required stage strip order at minimum:
1. intake
2. triage
3. research_analysis
4. architecture_review
5. gate1
6. build_replay
7. shadow
8. gate2
9. limited_live
10. terminal state in `{full_live, backlog, reject, refinement}`

Hard rules:
- every material card in the owner packet must show its current stage on the canonical strip;
- `current_holder` means the agent or owner with custody right now;
- `pending_with` means the actor blocking forward progress;
- `next_owner` means who must act after the current step completes;
- clicking `linked_cards` must open the underlying proposal, shadow, incident, change, memo, or benchmark artifact directly;
- dashboard or Telegram presentation may compress layout, but may not omit owner-progress fields for materially actionable items.

### 20D.8E Agent reaction / response tracking law

The owner should be able to inspect not only final status but also how each agent reacted to the task while it moved through intake, research, replay, shadow, repair, and promotion. Codex must therefore preserve one canonical reaction-audit contract so refusals, vetoes, stalls, and partial completions do not disappear into prose or chat history.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `AGENT_REACTION_AUDIT_ROW`
- `AGENT_REACTION_SUMMARY_PACKET`

Minimum required reaction-state enumeration at minimum:
- `accepted`
- `refused_out_of_scope`
- `requested_more_data`
- `escalated`
- `completed_partial_work`
- `detected_risk`
- `vetoed`
- `timed_out_or_missed_sla`
- `superseded`

Minimum required audit fields at minimum:
- `task_or_card_id`
- `agent_id`
- `reaction_state`
- `timestamp`
- `reason_or_note`
- `resulting_handoff_target`

Hard rules:
- reaction tracking is an audit surface, not a second approval ladder;
- vetoes by Risk Manager or owner-gated surfaces must remain visible in the same audit chain as ordinary accept/complete reactions;
- a material stall, timeout, refusal, or veto may not disappear merely because a later agent completed the task.

### 20D.8E1 Owner-direct conversation, agent-message ledger, and transcript-visibility law

The owner should not be forced to route ordinary runtime directions through ChatGPT or Codex once QTT is built. QTT must therefore preserve one canonical conversation ledger so the owner can speak directly to a named agent, specialist pod, or bounded broadcast scope through the dashboard or Telegram mirror, while still seeing the resulting inter-agent conversation history, directives, handoffs, and audit outcomes.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `OWNER_AGENT_CONVERSATION_LEDGER_ROW`
- `AGENT_MESSAGE_LEDGER_ROW`
- `CONVERSATION_DIRECTIVE_ENVELOPE`
- `CONVERSATION_DELIVERY_RECEIPT`
- `OWNER_VISIBLE_TRANSCRIPT_PACKET`

Minimum required machine-readable fields at minimum:
- `conversation_id`
- `message_id`
- `sender_actor_id`
- `recipient_scope`
- `linked_agent_ids`
- `linked_card_ids`
- `linked_artifact_ids`
- `message_class` in `{STRUCTURED_COMMAND, FREEFORM_DIRECTIVE, QUESTION, STATUS_UPDATE, HANDOFF_NOTE, SYSTEM_NOTICE}`
- `delivery_state`
- `runtime_effect_scope`
- `resulting_action_code_if_any`
- `visible_to_owner_flag`
- `created_timestamp`

Hard rules:
- the owner may send structured commands and free-form directions directly to a named agent, specialist pod, or bounded broadcast scope through the dashboard or Telegram mirror;
- free-form owner text that can affect runtime behavior must be canonicalized into a `CONVERSATION_DIRECTIVE_ENVELOPE` before any agent may act on it;
- ChatGPT and Codex remain design-time authoring and build tools; they may help create or revise QTT, but they are not mandatory runtime relays for ordinary owner-to-agent direction;
- agents may coordinate automatically through typed handoff envelopes and message-ledger rows; the owner may inspect the resulting transcript/history from the dashboard without relying on raw backend logs;
- no agent may delete, rewrite, or silently hide a material handoff, veto, refusal, owner directive, or delivery failure from the owner-visible transcript packet;
- read-only owner visibility is mandatory for inter-agent message history affecting research, replay, shadow, live restriction, promotion, rollback, or incident response;
- if a chat channel is unavailable, the canonical conversation ledger remains authoritative and the system must surface the last synced transcript state and delivery-failure receipt rather than silently dropping the conversation.

Validation hooks:
- `test_owner_agent_conversation_ledger_required.py`
- `test_freeform_owner_text_requires_directive_envelope_before_runtime_effect.py`
- `test_owner_visible_transcript_packet_required_for_material_cross_agent_flows.py`
- `test_runtime_directions_do_not_require_chatgpt_or_codex_relay.py`

QTT must therefore preserve one exact dashboard-native transcript workspace that is functionally Slack-like in channel and thread ergonomics while remaining governed by the canonical append-only message ledger rather than by mutable UI state.

- `forensic_export_class = READ_ONLY_JSONL_PLUS_HTML`
- `owner_participation_mode = READ_WRITE_DIRECT_PARTICIPANT`

Bounded search range at minimum:
- `thread_render_mode` in `{INLINE_PLUS_EXPANDABLE_THREAD_DRAWER, SPLIT_THREAD_PANE}`
- `transcript_refresh_mode` in `{PUSH_STREAM_WHEN_AVAILABLE_ELSE_POLL_FIVE_SECONDS, POLL_TWO_SECONDS, POLL_FIVE_SECONDS}`

- `owner_participation_mode` in `{READ_ONLY_OBSERVER, READ_WRITE_DIRECT_PARTICIPANT}`

Hard rules:
- the authoritative dashboard must render one polished always-on transcript workspace that is functionally Slack-like in channel list, timeline, thread, unread badge, search, and pin ergonomics for all owner-visible QTT conversations;
- the dashboard workspace is authoritative for transcript inspection and detailed conversation review; Telegram and any optional Discord or Slack mirrors may deep-link into the same `conversation_id`, `channel_scope_id`, or `thread_id_when_applicable`, but they may not replace the authoritative dashboard transcript workspace;
- every delivered owner-visible message row must render sender identity, recipient scope, timestamp, delivery state, materiality badge, runtime-effect badge when applicable, and linked card or artifact references without requiring the owner to inspect raw backend logs;
- material delivered messages are append-only and immutable; corrections, clarifications, or superseding context must appear as new rows linked to the prior `message_id` rather than by destructive rewrite or silent deletion;
- optional summaries, clustering, or AI-generated digests are admissible only as overlays; they may not replace, hide, reorder, or collapse away the underlying raw transcript rows for material messages;
- every delivered owner-visible cross-agent message affecting research, replay, shadow, live restriction, promotion, rollback, incident response, runtime directives, or delivery failure must have one raw render row in the transcript workspace and one exportable ledger row; only unsent drafts and purely local view-state artifacts may remain outside the canonical transcript;
- the workspace must support channel-level and cross-channel search, filtering by agent, pod, severity, card, artifact, stage, and time range, plus pinned-context strips for the governing card, bundle, or incident packet so the owner can reconstruct why the conversation happened;
- if live sync degrades, the workspace must surface a `SYNC_GAP_BANNER_RECEIPT`, the last synced timestamp, and the affected channel or thread scope rather than silently presenting stale conversation state as current;
- forensic export is read-only and owner-visible; exports may assist audit, replay, or incident review, but they may not become a second writable chat plane;
- mirror channels may preserve familiar team-chat ergonomics, but the canonical transcript identity remains the append-only QTT ledger and dashboard workspace, not a third-party channel history whose retention or edit semantics QTT does not control.

- `test_forensic_transcript_export_read_only.py`

### 20D.8C1 Autonomous implementation queue, one-click merge/deploy, and no-manual-coding law

The decision queue and change queue are still not fully owner-friendly if a bounded change still expects the owner to open a shell, edit files, or debug test failures personally. Codex must therefore preserve one exact **Autonomous Implementation Queue** so owner-visible change packets can be admitted, auto-coded, auto-debugged, reviewed, and merged or deployed through ordinary dashboard/Telegram actions rather than through manual coding labor.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `AUTONOMOUS_IMPLEMENTATION_QUEUE_CARD`
- `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS_TIMELINE_CARD`
- `IMPLEMENTATION_DIFF_SUMMARY_CARD`
- `IMPLEMENTATION_TEST_REPORT_CARD`
- `IMPLEMENTATION_BLOCKER_SUMMARY_CARD`
- `IMPLEMENTATION_FALLBACK_OPTIONS_CARD`

Minimum required owner-visible actions at minimum:
- `🛠️ Auto-Implement`
- `🧾 Review Diff`
- `🧪 Review Test Report`
- `✅ Approve Merge`
- `🚀 Approve Research Deploy`
- `🌒 Approve Shadow Deploy`
- `⛔ Keep Disabled`
- `🔁 Retry Auto-Debug`
- `↘️ Approve Narrower Scope`
- `🧷 Approve Disabled Behind Flag`
- `👁️ Approve Read-Only Variant`
- `🌒 Keep Shadow-Only`
- `🧩 Approve Partial UI Variant`
- `🌿 Continue Research Branch`
- `↩️ Roll Back To Last Known Good`

Hard rules:
- the autonomous implementation queue must remain part of the existing `CHANGE_QUEUE_AND_DEPLOYMENT_STATE` layer rather than becoming a second unaudited engineering workflow;
- once `🛠️ Auto-Implement` or the equivalent dashboard/Telegram action is approved for an admitted change, QTT must perform patch generation, test execution, and auto-debug iteration automatically inside the bounded implementation lane;
- the owner may inspect diffs and reports at any time, but the ordinary workflow may not assume manual code editing, manual command-line operation, or manual debugging by the owner;
- `✅ Approve Merge`, `🚀 Approve Research Deploy`, and `🌒 Approve Shadow Deploy` remain governance actions only; they may not bypass the stronger existing triggered-shadow-comparison and live owner gates or the stronger existing deployment restrictions;
- if the autonomous implementation queue reaches a blocked state, the owner-visible blocker summary must present a plain-English reason, the smallest next action, and the selected safe fallback-path class; raw engineering chores may not be rendered as the default owner burden;
- the owner surface must render `IMPLEMENTATION_FALLBACK_OPTIONS_CARD` whenever the lane is blocked, and that card must expose one or more approved actions consistent with the selected fallback-path class, including rollback when rollback is the selected minimum safe path;
- `↘️ Approve Narrower Scope`, `🧷 Approve Disabled Behind Flag`, `👁️ Approve Read-Only Variant`, `🌒 Keep Shadow-Only`, `🧩 Approve Partial UI Variant`, `🌿 Continue Research Branch`, and `↩️ Roll Back To Last Known Good` are bounded governance actions only; they may not bypass stronger existing owner gates, deployment restrictions, or non-delegable authorities.

Minimum required rendering-mode rules at minimum:
- **Owner mode** = bold, simple, color-coded, decision-ready;
- **Engineer mode** = full drilldown, filters, event markers, provenance links, audit references, and raw-trade links where authorized;
- preferred implementation split may use Dash/Plotly for owner interaction, Apache ECharts for dense attribution charts, and Grafana for telemetry/ops monitoring, but these are rendering choices only and may not redefine the canonical fields;
- purpose-driven color semantics on the authoritative dashboard surface must at minimum preserve `green = net-positive gains or positive uplift`, `red = realized loss, negative uplift, or negative drag`, `blue = classical baseline or neutral incumbent comparator`, `purple = quantum-applied series or quantum-specific uplift family`, `orange = degradation watch / warning state`, `yellow = caution, partial support, or insufficient sample size`, and `gray = unattributed, inactive, unavailable, or partial-receipt state`;
- color may accelerate review speed, but every materially used color encoding must also have text labels, legends, tooltips, or pattern differentiation so meaning never depends on color alone.

Hard rules:
- this layer is observability and capital-routing intelligence only, not a direct live-authority surface;
- owner mode and engineer mode must remain numerically identical for the same time window and filter state;
- no panel may render a sleeve green merely because gross P&L is positive if net P&L, drawdown, or friction state makes the sleeve economically weak;
- the Quantum Edge Comparator, degradation alarm, and capital-routing recommendation surfaces must use net-of-friction results after fees, slippage, borrow, and declared execution-cost drag rather than raw paper alpha or gross-only series;
- no quantum uplift percentage may render as decision-grade unless the strongest declared classical comparator, support count, support-time-span, confidence tier, and receipt-status tier are simultaneously available;
- the `What Is Hurting Me Most?` and `What Is Paying Me Best?` panels may summarize, but may not omit the worst/best supporting field set when materially nonzero;
- quantum-attributed contribution may not render as a winning sleeve unless the linked `QCAR_REPORT` or equivalent comparator-backed attribution receipt exists;
- specialist flow and Sankey-style rendering may summarize contribution paths, but may not fabricate certainty when the route or attribution chain is partial;
- capital-routing recommendations remain advisory and owner-gated unless a stricter existing law separately authorizes a bounded automated routing adjustment under replay, shadow, and rollback law.

Hard rules:
- this panel is diagnostic and governance-only; it may not directly mutate live policy;
- a module may not be rendered as clearly profitable if the realized gains are dominated by unchanged decisions while the changed-decision subset is weak or unattributed;
- counterfactual opportunity loss may not render as decision-grade if the strongest classical comparator, match quality tier, and support-count gate are missing;
- capital-routing recommendations may summarize decision evidence, but they remain advisory and may not silently reallocate live capital without the stronger existing replay, shadow, owner-gate, and rollback laws;
- when matched counterfactual evidence is unavailable, the panel must render uncertainty explicitly rather than silently collapsing to bundle-level profit.
- decision-level rendering may not suppress half-life decay, no-trade value, toxicity, or shadow-twin deltas when those fields exist for the rendered decision;
- quantum agreement and Bayesian truth-maintenance fields remain diagnostic and governance-grade, but when they are available they must be rendered on the same decision basis as the changed decision rather than at only bundle level.

### 20D.8H Slippage-intelligence and execution-cost-forensics law

The broader Performance Intelligence layer already preserves fee/slippage drag and specialist attribution, but the late legacy line also carried a stricter **bidirectional Slippage Intelligence System**. Codex must therefore preserve one explicit slippage-intelligence and execution-cost-forensics contract instead of leaving negative slippage, positive slippage, attribution, and tolerance-learning implied inside generic execution-quality receipts.

- market family
- platform / venue
- timestamp

- order-book depth snapshot basis or explicit unavailability reason

Minimum required dashboard fields at minimum:
- cumulative positive slippage captured for lifetime and trailing 30/90/365 day windows

Hard rules:
- positive and negative slippage must use the same typed schema so execution quality is measured symmetrically rather than only as a cost;
- negative slippage may never remain blended invisibly into generic loss forensics when an expected-versus-actual execution comparison is available;
- if economic repricing is enabled, the dashboard and typed store must preserve amend-path cost visibility rather than show only raw price-improvement capture;
- slippage-tolerance learning may generate research-tagged proposals only and may never auto-apply to live envelopes without replay, shadow, owner-gate, and rollback support;
- the slippage-intelligence database or equivalent typed store is observability and research infrastructure only, not live trading authority;
- if the expected fill-price basis is unavailable or unreliable, the row must declare the basis failure explicitly rather than fabricate an attribution number.

The stronger canonical body already preserves `20D.8H` slippage-intelligence and execution-cost-forensics law, `GV-10C` elite-strategy monitoring and retirement governance, and the broader performance-intelligence/dashboard spine. But legacy v8.9.66 still carried two exact high-salience owner-facing panel names that may still appear in deferred ledgers, dashboard requests, and older Codex tasks: the **Cumulative Slippage Dashboard** and the **Elite Strategy Panel**. Codex must therefore preserve those exact surfaces explicitly so older references resolve deterministically without inventing parallel dashboards or silently renaming away a requested panel.

- `NET_SLIPPAGE_PNL_TREND_CARD`

- linked `SLIPPAGE_PATTERN_ALERT` and `SLIPPAGE_TOLERANCE_RESEARCH_PROPOSAL` state when applicable

Hard rules:
- the exact names `Cumulative Slippage Dashboard` and `Elite Strategy Panel` may remain first-class or exact-alias-backed, but they may not silently disappear if older owner workflows or Codex tasks still reference them directly;
- the cumulative slippage dashboard may summarize execution-cost trends, but it may not suppress cumulative negative slippage cost, cumulative positive slippage capture, or net slippage P&L when materially nonzero;

## 20E. Migration rule for future edits

Any future revision to this master plan must:
1. edit the canonical slot where the family already lives,
2. regenerate the full master plan as a coherent whole,

4. never reintroduce duplicate family definitions,
5. preserve stronger live-safety, point-in-time, provenance, and fallback doctrine unless the owner explicitly approves a replacement.

### 19.19G Nelson-Siegel / Svensson curve reference
- **Formula / basis:** Nelson-Siegel spot curve `z(m) = β0 + β1 * ((1 - exp(-m/τ1)) / (m/τ1)) + β2 * (((1 - exp(-m/τ1)) / (m/τ1)) - exp(-m/τ1))`; Svensson extends with `+ β3 * (((1 - exp(-m/τ2)) / (m/τ2)) - exp(-m/τ2))`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** annualized decimal-yield basis for `β0..β3`, positive maturity-scale parameters `τ1, τ2`, fit objective family, bond-filtering / off-the-run policy, and maturity unit basis.
- **Hard rule:** Nelson-Siegel and Svensson fits are empirical curve-parameterization families and may not be overclaimed as arbitrage-free short-rate models without an explicit separate model-family receipt.

### 19.19H Differential Sharpe reference
- **Formula / basis:** maintain exponential moment estimates on the declared return basis, `A_t = A_(t-1) + eta * (R_t - A_(t-1))` and `B_t = B_(t-1) + eta * (R_t^2 - B_(t-1))`, then compute the first-order differential-Sharpe increment as `D_t = (B_(t-1) * Delta A_t - 0.5 * A_(t-1) * Delta B_t) / (B_(t-1) - A_(t-1)^2)^(3/2)` with `Delta A_t = R_t - A_(t-1)` and `Delta B_t = R_t^2 - B_(t-1)`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** declared return basis, EMA decay `eta`, warm-start policy, denominator-guard policy, and side-by-side comparator metrics `{windowed_sharpe,pnl_after_cost}`.
- **Hard rule:** differential Sharpe is an adaptive-training or diagnostics metric, not a basis-free replacement for ordinary performance review. It may not be shown or optimized unless the return basis, decay rule, and denominator guard are explicit.

### 19.19L Implementable alpha, monetizability, and realization-ratio reference
- **Formula / basis:** declared predicted net edge on the approved objective basis `alpha_hat_net = alpha_hat_gross - c_fees_hat - c_spread_hat - c_slippage_hat - c_impact_hat - c_latency_hat - c_borrow_hat - c_other_hat`; monetizability ratio `M = alpha_hat_net / max(|alpha_hat_gross|, eps_monetize)`; realized-edge closure ratio `R = pnl_realized_net / max(|pnl_predicted_net|, eps_realize)`.
- **Canonical storage basis:** declared gross-edge basis, full cost-bucket decomposition, net-edge basis, epsilon-floor basis, sign convention, and predicted-versus-realized comparison basis.
- **Hard rule:** no edge may be labeled economically strong unless its monetizability and realization ratios are computed on the same net-of-friction basis used by the strongest declared comparator.

### 19.19M True-quantum profitability-verification and quantum-applicability reference
- **Formula / basis:** true-quantum profitability delta `Delta_Q = Pi_hat_net_quantum - Pi_hat_net_classical`; percentage uplift `U_Q = Delta_Q / max(|Pi_hat_net_classical|, eps_pct_quantum)`; quantum applicability resolves through the declared band lattice over combinatorial structure, nonconvexity, sampling burden, state-compression potential, portfolio-coupling strength, and latency tolerance, not through hidden weight vectors.
- **Canonical storage basis:** strongest classical comparator identity, admitted true-quantum verifier family set, predicted net objective basis, denominator-floor basis for percentage uplift, and cached-live-influence eligibility state.
- **Hard rule:** a sleeve may not claim quantum-enabled live eligibility unless `Delta_Q` and `U_Q` are computed on the declared net implementable objective basis and the underlying verifier family is one of the already admitted true-quantum canonical families.

### 19.19M2 Alpha/edge operating spine family `AE-01`
- **Domain:** alpha / edge discovery, profitability-evidence verification, no-trade recognition, direct-live exception review, and deterioration-aware demotion control
- **Purpose:** Materialize one first-class alpha / edge operating spine so QTT does not reduce profit capture to one hidden model score, one hidden quantum comparator, or one hidden owner-dashboard table.
- **Families included once here:** `EDGE_DISCOVERY_MESH`, `PROFITABILITY_EVIDENCE_MESH`, `EDGE_CANDIDATE_RECORD`, `ALPHA_PROMOTION_SCORECARD`, `PRETRADE_PROFITABILITY_EVIDENCE_PERCENT`, `DIRECT_LIVE_ON_APPROVAL_GATE`, `NO_TRADE_ALPHA_BOARD`, `ONLINE_EDGE_SOURCE_BUDGET_ALLOCATOR`, `ALPHA_DEATH_DETECTION`, and `QUANTUM_DISAGREEMENT_MINING`.
- **Inputs:** daily opportunity census state, edge registry state, strongest classical comparator outputs, admitted true-quantum verifier outputs, all-in cost intelligence, latency telemetry, edge half-life forecasts, crowding diagnostics, live-versus-shadow divergence packets, and owner-governance state.
- **Outputs:** edge candidate records, profitability-evidence percentages, alpha-promotion grades, no-trade board entries, direct-live-on-approval exception packets, source-budget packets, disagreement-mining packets, and alpha-death-detection receipts.
- **Primary public / institutional anchors:** stronger existing expected-information-gain scheduling law; stronger existing implementable-frontier law; stronger existing opportunity-census and edge-registry machinery; official Qiskit Algorithms amplitude-estimation references; official Qiskit Finance portfolio-optimization, option-pricing, fixed-income, credit-risk, and stock-time-series / data-provider references; official Qiskit Optimization QAOA / SamplingVQE / CVaR references; official CUDA-Q hybrid quantum-classical platform references; official PennyLane `lightning.gpu` references; official D-Wave hybrid-solver references; and the current public IBM / HSBC bond-trading reference.
- **Canonical formula / basis set at minimum:**
  - required gate vector `G_edge = {g_net,g_conf,g_impl,g_regime,g_quantum}` with `g_net = GREEN only when expected net edge is positive on the declared net-of-friction basis`, `g_conf = GREEN only when support, confidence, and stability are sufficient under stronger existing replay / shadow law`, `g_impl = GREEN only when execution-realizability is green on the active connector and latency path`, `g_regime = GREEN only when the candidate is admissible in the active regime under the stronger existing regime law`, and `g_quantum = GREEN only when the selected quantum challenger is non-inferior or superior to the strongest declared classical comparator on the same implementable basis`;
  - gate-value map `v(GREEN)=1.0`, `v(AMBER)=0.5`, `v(RED)=0.0`;
  - hard-veto flag `H_edge = 1` whenever any stronger existing hard veto applies, including at minimum negative expected net edge, leakage failure, implementation incompatibility, cash-only violation, unresolved live-versus-shadow divergence, or unarmed live-mode dependence;
  - pretrade profitability-evidence percentage `PEP_edge = 100 * (1 - H_edge) * mean({v(g_net),v(g_conf),v(g_impl),v(g_regime),v(g_quantum)})`;
  - alpha-promotion grade rule `GRADE_edge = A` when all five gates are green and no hard veto is active, `B` when exactly four gates are green with no hard veto, `C` when exactly three gates are green with no hard veto, `D` when exactly two gates are green with no hard veto, and `REJECT` otherwise;
  - default ranking ladder `RANK_edge = LEXICOGRAPHIC(expected_net_edge_basis, probability_of_profit, implementability_state, regime_fit_state, selected_quantum_challenger_result_state, promotion_state, inverse(crowding_risk_class))` with the stronger existing no-trade comparator preserved as a first-class competing action;
  - owner-directed weighted composite formula remains admissible only as `TRIGGERED_LIVE_CONCURRENT_COMPARISON_ONLY_OPTIONAL` and resolves to the explicitly pasted formula `0.30*ExpectedNetEdge + 0.15*ProbabilityOfProfit + 0.10*ConfidenceStability + 0.10*RegimeFit + 0.10*FillRealizability + 0.10*EdgeHalfLife + 0.10*RobustnessAcrossSplits + 0.05*CapacityScore + 0.05*QuantumUpliftScore - LatencyPenalty - CrowdingPenalty - LeakagePenalty - ComplexityPenalty`, with hidden weight changes forbidden;
  - source-budget priority rule `S_budget = LEXICOGRAPHIC(expected_information_gain_per_cost, recent_monetizability_state, novelty_state)` rather than equal-budget polling;
  - alpha-death trigger bundle is the declared conjunction or sequence family over `half_life_shrink`, `crowding_rise`, `slippage_rise`, `quantum_classical_disagreement_widening`, and `live_concurrent_shadow_comparison_divergence_widening`, with the stronger existing owner-gate and rollback laws remaining authoritative for final demotion.
- **Hard rules:**
  - QTT may compute stronger profitability evidence before execution, but it may not claim certainty of future profitability;
  - no trade order may be released because a model says `buy`; a trade order may be released only when the candidate record is green under the declared gates or the stronger existing owner-approved exception path is green;
  - `NO_TRADE` must remain a first-class ranked candidate whenever the no-trade comparator dominates the enter-trade path on the declared net basis;
  - direct-live exception review is owner-only, rare by design, and may not bypass rollback, capital-feasibility, latency-budget, or evidence-packet requirements;
  - the live lane in the default production mode may consume cached profitability-evidence artifacts, but may not wait for new remote quantum runtime or new deep discovery output before taking a safe local action.

## 20. Canonical strategy catalog

This strategy catalog names the strategies the system is structurally prepared to support. The detailed parameter families already live in the family cards above; this section defines how they combine operationally.

### 20.1 Strategy tiers

#### Tier 1 — day-1 production-safe baseline strategies
- calibrated probability forecasting with classical baselines,
- fractional Kelly with confidence, fragility, and volatility modifiers,
- micro-clip sizing,
- maker-first / post-only where economics justify,
- FOK for all-or-nothing urgent entries where venue semantics support it,
- slippage wall and capacity gate,
- core-satellite slower allocation sleeves,
- risk parity / constrained mean-variance slower sleeves,
- realized-vol and EWMA volatility controls,
- basic event-time and time-to-resolution overlays,
- provenance and kill-switch discipline.

#### Tier 2 — production-eligible after replay and triggered live-concurrent shadow-comparison proof
- order-flow imbalance strategies,
- Avellaneda–Stoikov quoting overlays,
- time-to-fill hazard models,
- markout-driven routing,
- regime-aware scaling,
- Black-Litterman slower allocation overlays,
- hierarchical risk parity,
- Treasury cash-versus-futures basis and repo-financing-aware relative-value sleeves,
- heavier gradient-boosted or neural tabular challengers,
- quantum feature bridge artifacts that clearly beat classical comparators.

#### Tier 3 — research-heavy or specialist strategies
- QAOA or annealing-based combinatorial trade or portfolio selection,
- amplitude-estimation pricing or expectation research,
- qGAN or quantum generative scenario engines,
- quantum autoencoder compression,
- latent-regime and state-space specialist families,
- unified conditional stable-GARCH cross-asset heavy-tail allocators,
- barbell / antifragile convex sleeves,
- causal uplift / off-policy quote experimentation,
- differential-Sharpe-trained adaptive controllers.

### 20.2 Strategy assembly rules
A live strategy is not a single model. It is a governed composition:
1. data and contract validity,
2. conditioning family,
3. feature family,
4. base model family,
5. calibrator,
6. uncertainty overlay,
7. sizing and risk overlay,
8. execution policy,
9. provenance packet,
10. rollback pointer.

No strategy may bypass this composition stack.

### 20.2A Live candidate search and policy-cell routing flow
The canonical live candidate-search path must remain hierarchical rather than brute-force:
1. global scout layer updates the candidate-edge mesh from declared online and internal sources,
2. regime and hazard layer builds the current market-state fingerprint,
3. policy-cell router converts the fingerprint into one admissible cell or bounded shortlist,
4. candidate generator produces only the bounded neighborhood allowed by the active budget profile,
5. strongest classical baseline packet opens first,
6. matched quantum sleeve may re-estimate only when the declared problem shape fits,
7. trade-versus-no-trade comparator packet opens on the same net-of-friction basis,
8. friction-realizability layer rejects candidates that fail slippage, fill, latency-decay, queue, crowding, venue, or cash-only tests,
9. survivor-ranking layer orders the remaining candidates by the declared metric profile,
10. execution arbiter applies hard veto, capital / risk, venue-admissibility, staleness, no-trade, micro-size, and execution-style checks in the declared order,
11. post-trade realized writeback updates the same authoritative edge row before promotion rescoring.

Hard rules:
- the live loop may evaluate multiple combinations, but only inside the declared budget classes and neighborhood rules;
- the live loop may not brute-force the full cross-product of all declared parameter / strategy / algorithm combinations;
- the live loop may consume cached or nearline-prepared evidence, but it may not block on new deep research inference or remote true-quantum runtime inside the per-order release path.

### 20.2B Black-swan policy-compression rule
Under black-swan or event-shock conditions QTT must simplify faster rather than optimize harder.

Minimum required black-swan compression actions at minimum:
- shrink the admissible strategy universe,
- tighten active parameter ranges and search neighborhoods,
- raise the no-trade threshold,
- increase friction penalties,
- demote higher-variance challengers,
- reduce live size,
- shorten admissible holding horizons,
- prefer robustness over theoretical edge,
- route marginal candidates to `NO_TRADE`.

Hard rule:
Black-swan mode may compress and harden the policy surface, but it may not silently widen search budgets, widen the strategy universe, or bypass the stronger existing classical-primary release and no-trade laws.

### 20.2C Policy-cell library and selector discipline
The Day-1 policy-cell library is the canonical mechanism that prevents arbitrary agent improvisation when current conditions shift.

Minimum required Day-1 cells at minimum:
- prediction-market event-driven,
- inventory-aware quoting,
- liquidity-dislocation relative-value,
- slow relative-value allocation,
- no-trade preservation.

Each policy cell must declare at minimum:
- allowed strategy families,
- allowed parameter families,
- default seed profile,
- bounded search-neighborhood rule,
- latency budget,
- kill criteria,
- black-swan restriction mode.

### 20D.8O Exact owner-target workflow title-case and OTTI panel continuity law

The owner dashboard and decision surface are not fully continuity-safe if older owner notes or runbooks can still refer to `Owner Trade Target Intake (OTTI)`, `Trade Proposal Card`, `Watch Monitor Card`, `Trade Management Plan`, `Exit Decision Card`, or `Owner Progress Board` but the canonical file answers only with machine-readable IDs.

Required owner-facing continuity at minimum:
- the dashboard must be able to render the owner-target pipeline using either the machine-readable card names or the exact legacy title-case labels without ambiguity;
- `Owner Progress Board` must resolve to the same canonical board and timeline surfaces that already render `OWNER_PROGRESS_BOARD_CARD`;
- `Trade Management Plan` and `Exit Decision Card` must render as owner-facing labels for the existing canonical cards, not as separate implementation families;
- `OTTI` must be searchable, filterable, and traceable to `OWNER_TRADE_TARGET_INTAKE_CARD` in the owner-facing control surface and audit receipts.

### 20D.8P Research/proposal archive, read-later queue, and lifecycle-status panel law

The dashboard must expose one organized archive view for reports, formal proposals, experimental trials, and live-monitoring reviews so the owner may review them asynchronously without losing status, evidence, or next-action context.

Minimum required panel capabilities at minimum:
- filter by market, platform, strategy family, status, severity, and date range;
- separate tabs for `{REPORTS, FORMAL_PROPOSALS, EXPERIMENTAL, LIVE_MONITORING_REVIEWS}`;
- one read-later queue and one unresolved-action queue;
- linked evidence, linked shadow cards, linked implementation packets, and linked rollout / rollback receipts;
- visible criteria-strength badges and profit-priority overlays on every archived item.

Hard rules:
- status icons and archive states must update automatically when a proposal moves from research to triggered live-concurrent shadow comparison, from limited-live canary to owner-approved full/scaled live, back to refinement, or into retirement;
- archive organization may improve readability, but it may not fork the canonical status values already declared in Section `8.11`;
- asynchronous review is allowed, but unresolved owner actions must remain visible until resolved, superseded, or explicitly expired.

### 20D.8Q Cumulative earnings/loss rollup, market-platform attribution, and interactive graph law

QTT must expose scalable interactive graphs for cumulative earnings and losses across markets, platforms, and strategy families so the owner can see where net profit is actually being created or destroyed.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `PNL_TIMESERIES_ROW`
- `MARKET_PLATFORM_ROLLUP_CARD`
- `CUMULATIVE_EARNINGS_GRAPH_SPEC`
- `FEE_AND_SLIPPAGE_WATERFALL_CARD`
- `EXPERIMENTAL_VS_LIVE_COMPARATOR_CARD`
- `QUANTUM_CLASSICAL_COMPARATOR_TIMESERIES_ROW`
- `QUANTUM_UPLIFT_PERCENTAGE_CURVE_SPEC`
- `QUANTUM_REGIME_BUCKET_HEATMAP_CARD`
- `QUANTUM_DEGRADATION_TREND_GRAPH_SPEC`
- `QUANTUM_VALUE_DECOMPOSITION_GRAPH_SPEC`
- `QUANTUM_COMPLEXITY_ROI_GRAPH_SPEC`
- `COUNTERFACTUAL_OPPORTUNITY_LOSS_GRAPH_SPEC`
- `CAPITAL_ROUTING_RECOMMENDATION_OVERLAY_CARD`
- `GRAPH_COLOR_SEMANTICS_LEGEND_CARD`

Minimum required graph families at minimum:
- cumulative realized P&L over time;
- cumulative realized-plus-unrealized P&L over time where applicable;
- market-by-market and platform-by-platform rollups;
- strategy-family contribution and drag decomposition;
- fee, spread, and slippage drag waterfalls;
- drawdown, recovery, and equity-curve overlays;
- EXPERIMENTAL versus approved-live performance comparisons;
- quantum-applied cumulative net P&L versus strongest classical-comparator cumulative net P&L as dual first-class curves;
- absolute quantum uplift versus strongest classical comparator as its own curve rather than implied subtraction;
- percentage quantum uplift versus strongest classical comparator as its own curve with explicit denominator basis;
- regime-conditioned quantum uplift heatmaps and bucketed uplift tables for at minimum `{market, platform, strategy_family, regime, holding_time_bucket, liquidity_bucket_or_explicit_unavailability_reason}`;
- confidence, support-count, and receipt-status overlays for every materially rendered quantum uplift graph;
- quantum degradation trend and alarm overlays showing uplift rollover or worsening relative to the strongest classical comparator;
- quantum value-source decomposition graphs for `{selection, timing, sizing, routing_or_execution}`;
- quantum ROI versus complexity graphs showing uplift dollars, uplift percent, complexity score delta, and uplift per complexity unit;
- counterfactual opportunity-loss graphs showing recovered profit, missed profit, and avoidable loss deltas versus the strongest classical comparator;
- and capital-routing recommendation overlays that summarize `{INCREASE, HOLD, DECREASE, QUARANTINE}` recommendations without directly mutating live capital;
- daily opportunity census heatmaps showing active coverage and white-space gaps by `{market, platform, horizon, regime}`;
- daily alpha-board readiness distributions by monetizability, deployment-readiness, and true-quantum-verification state;
- realized-edge closure ratio curves and execution-loss decomposition waterfalls;
- and alpha-basket concentration, cross-edge-correlation, and failure-mode-diversity overlays.

Hard rules:
- dashboard color semantics must follow the declared review-speed palette, with green for positive gains and red for losses on the authoritative dashboard surface, and the upgraded purpose-driven graph palette must additionally preserve blue for classical-baseline series, purple for quantum-applied series, orange for degradation-watch states, yellow for caution or insufficient-support states, and gray for partial, inactive, or unattributed states;
- interactive graphs must support filtering by market, platform, venue, strategy family, regime, date range, approval class, support tier, confidence tier, and receipt-status tier;
- performance visuals may not hide fees, slippage, borrow, or other cost drag behind gross-only charts;
- quantum-versus-classical comparison graphs must default to net-of-friction basis and must surface the basis explicitly in legends and tooltips;
- percentage uplift graphs must declare the exact denominator basis and floor rule explicitly so percentage differences do not explode on tiny classical baselines;
- no degradation alarm, uplift chart, opportunity-loss chart, or capital-routing overlay may render as decision-grade without support count, support-time-span, and receipt-status context;
- graphs may be colorful for review speed, but colors must remain meaningful, stable, legend-backed, and never purely decorative;
- mirror channels may summarize graph conclusions, but the authoritative interactive graph remains the dashboard surface.

The stronger performance-intelligence layer is still not fully Codex-complete if the owner can see alpha rows but cannot deterministically sort, filter, escalate, or quarantine them. QTT must therefore preserve one explicit alpha/edge review companion artifact for sortable candidate ranking, direct-live exception queueing, source-budget visibility, and alpha-death monitoring.

- the alpha-death monitor may recommend quarantine, demotion, triggered live-concurrent shadow-comparison-only restriction, or rollback review, but it may not silently retire a live family without the stronger owner-gate and rollback laws;
- no dashboard row may hide that the strongest current action is `NO_TRADE` when the no-trade comparator dominates the enter-trade path on the declared net basis.

The alpha/edge review layer is still too easy for Codex to fragment if exact owner-requested artifact IDs survive only as implicit semantics. QTT must therefore preserve one explicit artifact-ID continuity law for quantum-uplift comparison, edge-half-life urgency, and public institution-style weighted-composite benchmarking.

### 20D.8G2B Edge-taxonomy, reaction-order, alternative-data, branded-alias, sort-preset, and Day-1-feasibility dashboard law

The alpha/edge review layer is still incomplete if the owner can see profitability evidence but cannot see **what type of edge it is, whether it is first-order or second-order, which proxy families support it, whether branded pasted-text names are only aliases rather than dependencies, how the board is being sorted, and whether it is actually Day-1 feasible under the active small-book cash-only launch posture**.

Minimum required typed artifacts at minimum:
- `EDGE_TAXONOMY_FILTER_PANEL_CARD`
- `REACTION_ORDER_PANEL_CARD`
- `ALTERNATIVE_DATA_PROXY_PANEL_CARD`
- `BRANDED_ALIAS_RESOLUTION_PANEL_CARD`
- `ALPHA_BOARD_SORT_PRESET_PANEL_CARD`
- `DAY1_FEASIBILITY_BADGE_PANEL_CARD`

Minimum required filter and sort families at minimum:
- edge family
- edge order
- alternative-data family
- branded alias dependency state
- participant-positioning state
- priced-in state
- crowding exhaustion state
- supply-chain propagation state
- forced-flow cluster state
- day1 small-book admissibility state
- sort preset in `{HIGHEST_EXPECTED_NET_EDGE, HIGHEST_QUANTUM_UPLIFT, SHORTEST_HALF_LIFE_HIGHEST_URGENCY, BEST_TRIGGERED_LIVE_CONCURRENT_SHADOW_COMPARISON_CANDIDATES, BEST_DIRECT_LIVE_ON_APPROVAL_CANDIDATES, BEST_NO_TRADE_CANDIDATES, BEST_CROSS_MARKET_TRANSFER_CANDIDATES, HIGHEST_DAY1_FEASIBLE_EDGE}`

Hard rules:
- no owner-facing alpha board may hide whether a candidate is `FIRST_ORDER`, `SECOND_ORDER`, or `THIRD_ORDER_RESEARCH_ONLY`;
- no owner-facing alpha board may hide whether a candidate depends on alternative-data proxies, supply-chain propagation, forced-flow clustering, infrastructure-bottleneck logic, or branded pasted-text aliases that are only research cues;
- any branded name rendered on the owner surface must resolve to one canonical proxy family or platform-analog state rather than appearing as an undeclared hard dependency;
- any candidate rendered as economically attractive but `TRIGGERED_LIVE_CONCURRENT_COMPARISON_ONLY_CAPITAL_OR_PRODUCT_INSUFFICIENT`, `RESEARCH_ONLY_CAPITAL_OR_SCOPE_INSUFFICIENT`, or `BENCHMARK_ONLY_OR_DORMANT` must carry that badge on the same row or linked drawer rather than only in a downstream packet;
- the owner dashboard may permit filter and sort control over these new families and sort presets, but it may not silently upgrade a non-Day-1-feasible edge into live feasibility or a branded alias into a mandatory runtime dependency.

Validation hooks:
- `test_edge_taxonomy_filter_panel_required.py`
- `test_reaction_order_panel_required.py`

### 20D.8R Criteria-strength badges, profit-priority overlays, and proposal-ranking panel law

The owner asked to see everything while still prioritizing what most strongly fits the profit goal. The dashboard must therefore preserve a separate **priority overlay** rather than an invisible filter.

Minimum required panel capabilities at minimum:
- show the strongest criteria on each report or proposal;
- show which criteria are weak, uncertain, or unsupported;
- rank by profit-priority without hiding lower-ranked items;
- allow explicit sorting by `{profit_priority, evidence_strength, market_fit, implementation_cost, latency_fit, security_impact}`.

Hard rules:
- no proposal may disappear from the owner-facing archive solely because one or more criteria are weak;
- profit-priority overlays may change sort order and review urgency, but they may not replace the underlying full proposal;
- criteria badges must be explanatory, not decorative, and must remain traceable to the underlying scored fields.
